The station (ASBTP) at 11,555 feet reported a peak wind gust of 72 MPH at 420 AM.  Wind gust of 58 MPH and higher were reported between 930 PM and 630 AM.
The Humbug Creek station (QHBA3) measured a peak wind gust of 79 MPH at 648 AM. Wind gust over 58 MPH were reported between 948 PM and 1048 AM.

A newspaper reported that large ponderosa pine trees were uprooted and snapped off and damaged RVs and the Lodge 5 miles east of Kohls Ranch at 1100 PM.  A utility company reported that power poles were down about 4 miles north-northwest of Kohls Ranch around 1151 PM. Power outages were reported in the communities of Woods Canyon Lake, Young, Christopher Creek, and Forest Lakes. A driver on Highway 260 between Payson and Forest Lakes reported strong winds blowing debris onto roadway. They had to slow down to maintain control. Wind gusts estimated at 55 MPH.

The weather station at 11,555 feet on Agassiz Peak (ASBTP) reported a peak wind gust of 69 MPH at 1100 PM with frequent winds gust of 58 MPH or higher between 600 PM and 130 AM.  The station at 10767 feet (WX7FGZ-6) had peak wind gusts of 64 MPH between 700 and 715 PM with frequent wind gust of 58 MPH or higher between 445 PM and 1145 PM.  The weather station at 9379 feet (ASBLS-Little Spruce) had a peak wind gust of 64  MPH at midnight.  Wind gust over 58 MPH were observed between 715 PM and 1230 AM. Power outages were reported in parts of Flagstaff to Munds Park.

The Crooks Fire started in the mountains about 11 miles south of Prescott on April 18th. The fire grew to around 9,400 acres and burned well into June. The fire was reached 96% containment by May 25th and access restrictions for the area were lifted. The fire was 100% contained by June 27.

The Tunnel Fire started on April 17 about 14 miles northeast of Flagstaff within the 2010 Schultz Fire scar.  The fire eventually jumped Highway 89 and through Sunset Crater National Monument. The fire also burned at least 30 homes. In all,  the Tunnel Fire burned through 19,088 acres. The Tunnel Fire was marked fully contained Wednesday, June 1.

The Haywire Fire started near Haywire Crater the day after the Pipeline Fire exploded. It burned through pine (ponderosa and pinyon), juniper, grass, and brush. Another fire (Double Fire) started near the Double Crater (two vents) a few days later and merged with the Haywire Fire. The Double Fire was either a spot from the other two fires or lightning caused. Once the two fires merged, 5,575 acres burned. Several years of persistent drought has much of northern Arizona in severe or extreme drought. The drought combined with the time of year, has both the live and dead fuels at critically dry levels. Strong winds also pushed the fire northeastward. The fire continued to burn through July with little additional spread.  The topography and soils (cinders) of the Haywire Fire did not substantially increase the treat of post fire flash flooding.

The Pipeline Fire was reported on June 12, 2022 approximately 6 miles north of Flagstaff on the southwest flanks of Fremont Peak.  Strong southwest winds pushed this fire up and over Fremont Peak, Doyle Peak, eastern portions of Locket Meadow, Sugarloaf Peak, O'Leary Peak, parts of Sunset Crater National Monument,  across Forest Service Roads 420, 556, 418, and across Highway 89. Most of the 26,532 acres burned in June before higher humidity and rain arrived. The burned area lead to many flash flood events once rain started to fall during the yearly summer thunderstorm season (North American Monsoon).   The fire suppression costs were at least 11 million dollars. Damage to the forest and watershed was much more than that.
A land spout was reported near Interstate 40 east of Winona near The Twin Arrows Trading Post.  It persisted for 10-15 minutes. Pictures were posted on social media.

Heavy rain fell over the Pipeline Fire scar (June 2022) and caused flooding on Highway 89 southbound near road NF-9122H. Flooding also was seen in the Wupatki Trails neighborhood on Camio de los Vientos. Homes and roads were impacted by the flood waters.
Heavy rain flooded the Milton/Route 66 under the railroad overpass in downtown Flagstaff. Cars were caught in the flood water.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Prescott (Twitter).
A trained spotter measured a peak wind gust of 60 MPH near Kirkland.

Two inches of rain (radar estimate) from a thunderstorm caused flash flooding in Clarkdale. Water flowed over sections of Wildhorse Lane and Old Jerome Highway. Police reported mud and rocks on the roadways with both streets barricaded.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused major flash flooding of roads and homes in Spring Valley on Hackberry Creek. Flash flooding in Mayer caused threatened the town water supply infrastructure.
Flash flooding was reported in X Canyon, Antelope Canyon, and Lower Antelope Canyon (all the same drainage). Standing water remained in Lower Antelope Canyon on July 6.

Heavy rain over the Pipeline Fire scar (June 2022) caused flash flooding in Government Wash with 8 inches of water, mud, and debris flowing over Highway 89 once the culvert was overwhelmed.  Four garages on Heritage Drive and Pioneer Valley Road were flooded.
A public report of significant ponding of water and water over roads and curbs.
The first wash on Old Highway 279/Camino Real flooded in Cottonwood.

Flooding was reported along North Copeland Lane and nearby homes. Large rocks and debris covered the road and residential yards. Flash flooding was also reported in the Wupatki Trails neighborhood. The flooding was at least 100 feet wide with 2-3 foot debris in the flow.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding and road closures in Verde Lakes.
A trained spotter reported 2.20 inches of rain south-southeast of Camp Verde.
Strong winds from thunderstorms broke tree limbs.
Christopher Creek Rose at least a foot. Local roads were flooded and closed.

A flash flood wave on Ellison Creek near the cascades was 2 feet deep and 10-15 feet wider than normal flow was reported at 730 PM. The flood wave (2-3 feet deep) reached the confluence with the East Verde River by 740 PM.

Prescott Valley Police reported hazardous flooding at the intersection of East Lakeshore Drive and East Towago Drive and the intersection of Navajo Drive and Florentine Road.       Rain Gauges in the area recorded  from 1.50 and 1.86 inches of rain.
A wind gust of 58 MPH was reported in Spring Valley at 415 PM. There was damage to a shed roof and lawn structure as well as a tree was blown down.

Heavy rain fell over the western part of the Pipeline Fire scar (June 2022). This caused Schultz Creek (Dry Lakes gauge) to jump 2.84 feet. This flowed over Mt Elden Road, overwhelmed the drainage system along Highway 180, and flooded apartments and homes along Stevanna Way.

Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire scar (2010), Tunnel Fire scar (April 2022), and Pipeline Fire scar (June 2022) caused flooding in the area below. The water transported mud, ash, and debris across roads and filled ditches.
Heavy rain caused Oak Creek to rise 1.5 feet at the gauge in Sedona (OAKA3).
Heavy rain caused flooding over State Route 77 and Feedmill Road.
The Little Colorado River rose over 8 feet from 300 to 500 PM MST (Woodruff guage WDRA3).
Heavy rain fill a wash with water four feet deep in Cameron.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Antelope Canyon which closed the popular slot canyon for at least a day.
Heavy rain caused water to flow bank to bank, two feet deep, moving very quickly.
Trained spotters reported heavy rain in the Prescott area (1 to 2.5 inches).
Flooding was reported in Alberson Wash/Rose Creek, Lynx Creek, and Agua Fria River all the way to Skull Valley.
A storm chaser posted a video of flash flooding in the Cameron area on Twitter.
A stream gauge reported a 1.6 foot rise on Moenkopi Wash.
Street flooding on South Milton was reported (videos) on social media.
Reports of flooding on the Hopi Nation included First Mesa, Highway 264, Polacca Wash, and other locations.
Heavy rain over the Government Tank drainage and Pipeline/Tunnel fire scars caused flooding along the side of Highway 89 with only  one lane open.
The stream gauge on Cibcue (CBQ) Creek near the confluence with the  Salt River showed a 3.5 foot rise to 2,500 cubic feet per second.
Flash flooding was reported over Highway 98 five miles east of K'ai'bii'to.  Some roads washed out in the area.

Heavy rain over the Pipeline Fire scar (2022) resulted in 1-2 feet of water flowing in Schultz Creek, over Mount Elden Road, and overwhelming the culvert at Highway 180, and flowing onto the bike path next to Highway 180.  The water flowing over the highway caused a temporary closure.
Heavy rain fell just east of Snowflake with 1.22 inches reported.
Flash flooding was reported on the north side of Tuba City washed away dirt roads and people had to be rescued from the water.
A wash in the Sedona area was flowing 8 to 10 inches deep.
Tees Toh Wash was flowing about 2 feet deep about one mile west of Seba Delki.
Flash flooding unearthed two main water pipelines (8 and 10 inch) which had to be shut down. This left around 75 people with out flowing water in Indian Wells, Dilkon, and Seba areas.
A swift water rescue took place along Indian Route 4 by Burnt Corn Wash (about 5 miles east of Pi��on) where an elderly gentleman in his car was rescued.
A stream gauge showed a 7 foot rise on Beaver Creek in less than 15 minutes.
A few people were evacuated from a home that flooded in eastern Chinle near Canyon de Chelly. The time was estimated from radar.
Flooding was reported in rural Steamboat Canyon. Water washed out a residential road.
White Valley Road (N8031) was completely washed out.
Six feet of water was flowing through Burnt Corn Wash.

Heavy rain over the Pipeline/Tunnel (2022) and Schultz Fire (2010) scars caused extensive flash flooding northwest through northeast of Flagstaff. Highway 89 northeast of Flagstaff was closed in both directions around mile post 425 around 442 PM MST. The following roads in far northeast Flagstaff were flooded: Copeland Lane, Gunman Road, Vista de Oro, Pioneer Valley Road, and Neptune Drive. Highway 180 northwest of Flagstaff was closed in both directions around MP 218 at 419 PM. The Stevanna Way and Coconino Estates neighborhoods on the northwest side of Flagstaff flooded with apartments, homes, and streets impacted.
The river gauge on Granite Creek showed a rise of 2.55 feet in 90 minutes (at 1130 AM).  Flooding was reported on Highway 69 near milepost 295.
Heavy rain over the Pipeline, Tunnel, and Schultz Fire scars caused flash flooding that closed Highway 89 in both directions from mile marker 426 to 434.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Antelope Canyon.  The popular tourist slot canyon was closed for at least a day so that the water could be removed and sand could be replaced.

Heavy rain in Utah caused a flash flood in the Paria River that drains into Arizona and the Colorado River near Lees Ferry. The river gauge near on the Paria River near the Colorado River peaked at 6.8 feet at 600 AM.
A video of flash flooding three miles north of Fort Defiance was posted on social media.
Tonto Natural Bridge State Park posted pictures of Pine Creek rising 4 feet between 5:47 PM and 5:52 PM.
The Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City flooded area farm lands. Homes in the area were threatened.
A mix of dime to quarter sized hail was reported northwest of Pinetop-Lakeside.

The Hot Na Na Wash in Marble Canyon (16.5 miles down the Colorado River from Less Ferry) experienced a major flash flood. A rafting party arrived at camp around 600 PM. The wash began to flow around 615 PM and ran well past midnight. The wash was raging at around 700 PM. The waterfall from the flood hit the rock layer below and splashed back up in the air more than 30 feet. Several bodies of farm large animals were in the flood.|Radar precipitation images indicated that heavier rain also fell in the Tanner Wash drainage to the east through south of Hot Na Na Wash.  However, no reports from this area were received.
The river gauge in Granite Creek at Prescott measured a rise from 7.08 feet to 9.51 feet in about 30 minutes.
Heavy rain caused several inches of water to flow across the road at Cosnino Road and Wapiti Trail. Dime sized hail was also reported during the heavy rain.

The Schultz Creek gauge showed a 5 foot rise in about 30 minutes. The upstream rain gauge measured 0.71 inches in 30 minutes. The Flagstaff Emergency Manager reported 1.5-2 feet of water from Schultz Creek flowing over Mt Elden Road. This flow over toped portions of Highway 180 closing both lanes.||This event was larger than the previous flood event in this area. Several dozen homes were directly impacted by the flood waters and several streets are impassable due to mud and flood waters. Highway 180 (primary access to Flagstaff from the northwest was close form around 1230 PM through at least 300 PM MST.||Flooding had severe impacts for the ongoing construction projects, public infrastructure and private property in the area. Multiple streets in Coconino Estates were inundated with 6-12��� of water including Meade, Anderson, and Navajo. Stevanna Way was also inundated with over 2��� of water in places. Water overtopped Frances Short Pond.  Minor flooding occurred along the Rio de Flag between Dale and Cherry, but overall |floodwaters stayed within the channel downstream of Frances Short Pond. Impacts were also felt upstream of Mt. Elden Lookout Road where portions of the road and existing COF water infrastructure were damaged. Creighton Estates saw minor overtopping around 2-3��� deep.
Heavy rain in Winslow caused some street flooding.  Water covered the intersection of North Pope Ave and East Maple Street.
Water, sand, gravel, and rocks covered Navajo Route 60 in several locations near Castle Butte.
The river gauge on the Verde River near Perkinsville measured 12.16 feet. Base flow is about 2 feet.
The Aqua Fria-Mayer river gauge measured a two foot rise.
Big Bug Creek in Spring Valley rose 1-2 feet.

Heavy rain over the Pipeline Fire scar caused flash flooding in Government Wash. The water flowed east of Highway 89 and over topped Vista Del Oro and Heritage Drive, generally less than one foot deep and otherwise stayed within the ditches.
A thunderstorm wind gust of 76 MPH was reported just northeast of Peeples Valley.

The river gauge at Granite Creek showed nearly a 4 foot rise in one hour. It rose from 7.19 feet at 230 PM to 10.96 feet at 320 PM. Ten feet is considered moderate flood stage and 11 feet major flood stage.  The gauge dropped below major flood stage at 445 PM and below flood stage at 545 PM.
Heavy rain over the northern portion of the Pipeline fire cause flash flooding over Highway 89. Both directions were closed due to the flooding between milepost 428 and 430.
A video of a flood in Big Bug Creek was posted on social media. The creek is normally dry.
Two feet of water was flowing in Yaber Wash. The water was 40 to 50 feet wide with low water crossings flooded.
Flash flooding over Highway 160 was reported (Social Media and Law Enforcement) between on Highway 160 between Tonalea, Shonto, and Tsegi. Highway 98 was flooded near Shanto Wash.
The Dilkon Chapter House received multiple reports of Tribal members calling for help because of washed out dirt roads.  Indian routes 6 and 7 were flooded between Indian Wells and White Cone.

The Cornfields Chapter House reported that water was overtopping Navajo Route 15 with Law Enforcement diverting traffic. Greaswood Springs Road to Klagetoh was flooded.  State Route 264 was flooded near County Road 317.

The Havasu Creek Gauge at Supai Village showed water rising 4 feet in 30 minutes from 430 PM to 500 PM. The stream crested around 530 PM (1970 CFS) at 5 feet above normal levels .  The flow remained elevated through 700 PM.
Heavy rain over the Pipeline, Tunnel, and Schultz fire scars caused flash flooding in the area that closed Highway 89 in both directions.
A thunderstorm produced one inch diameter hail, heavy rain, and gusty winds (around 28 MPH).
The river gauge on Agua Fria measured a 5 foot rise in 15 minutes (starting at 1215 PM MST).
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Rock Canyon Creek where the water rose 3.5 feet.

A video on social media showed flooding outside of a hose near Hotevilla. Another video showed water up to the road on Route 2 just south of Kykotsmovi Village. Hopi Police reported that water covered Highway 264 for a distance of 100 yards near mile marker 369 at 725 PM MST.  Arizona Department of Transportation had to send crews out to removed mud from the flood.
Flooding was reported on Sate Route 98 near K'ai'bii'to.

A flash flood was reported on Highway 89 about 8 miles northeast of Doney Park (mile post 430...north of Wupatki Trails and south of the Sunset Crater turnoff).  The highway was closed in both directions.  Flooding also overtopped the highway at Brandis Way.
The stream gauge on Tonto Creek above Gun Creek showed almost a one foot rise in 30 minutes.
The Antelope Creek river gauge at Wickenburg Ranch started rising at 430 PM (around 349 CFS) and peaked at 1359 CFS at 455 PM MST.
A spotter reported major flooding around Kirkland due to very heavy rain.  That wash flows south then west toward Bagdad.
Several videos of major flooding north of Chinle were posted on social media.
The stream gauge on Havasu Creek near the Colorado River showed a 5 foot rise (to 1500 CFS) in less than 15 minutes.  This flooding was downstream from The Supai Village.

Heavy rain across the Rafael Fire (June 2021) caused a flash flood that entered the Verde River. The river gauge showed a 2.5 foot (600 CFS) increase in flow. The Verde River is a main stem river so flooding was not an issue once the flow reached that river.
Pictures on Social Media showed that the road from Polacca to Low Mountain was washed out and impassable. The wash likely flooded to Tolani Lake.
Heavy rain (2.40 inches in a short time) caused flooding in Model Creek and water was flowing over the Peeples Valley Road near the Model Creek School.
Flooding was reported on Highway 191 near Wide Ruin.
Flooding was reported in farmland and along roads near the Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City. This wash flows west then south to the Little Colorado River.

Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire scar (2010) and Tunnel/Pipeline fire scar (2022) caused flash flooding.  North Copeland Lane was overtopped with muddy water and debris 8 inches deep and 10 to 15 feet wide. There was also minor flooding of Henry Drive near Campbell Avenue.
Indian Route 15 from Burnside to Greasewood flooded in areas and there were puddles on the road. This is a paved road.
Major flooding was reported north of Many Farms Lake.

The river gauge on the Little Colorado River near Cameron showed a 3 foot rise between 715 PM and 1115 PM.  The majority of this flow was likely from the Moenkopi Wash that had a flash flood the day before.
Lower Antelope Canyon was close due to flash flooding. Water remained in the popular tourist attraction (sandstone slot canyon) through much of August 16 due to residual flood waters (large puddles).
Flash flooding was reported in the Tse Bonito Wash and across State Route 264 in Window Rock.
Heavy rain fell over the Pipeline Fire scar (June 2022) and caused flooding in Wupatki Trails and into Cinder Lakes and closed Highway 89 about a mile north of the neighborhood.

Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire scar (2010) and the Tunnel/Pipeline Fire scar (2022) caused flooding over a driveway near Glodia Drive and Copland Lane.  A large debris flow was also seen at the intersection of Campbell Avenue and Henry Drive.
The steam gauge on Agua Fria River near Cordes Junction showed a 3.47 foot rise.
A stream gauge on the Wet Beaver Creek measured a 2.15 foot rise.
A stream gauge on Dry Beaver Creek showed a 1.55 foot rise.
Heavy rain caused a 2.2 foot rise in Newman Canyon which flows into Upper Lake Mary.
The stream gauge on Wet Beaver Creek showed a 4.5 foot rise in 60 minutes (6 ENE of Lake Montezuma).  A gauge down steam (2 SW McGuireville) showed a 6.5 foot rise in less than an hour.
Interstate 40 was closed for a time on the eastern side of Joseph City.
Tonto Creek showed a 2.4 foot rise between 515 PM and 645 PM near Jakes Corner before the creek entered Roosevelt Lake.
Granite Creek rose 4.5 feet at the USGS gauge in Prescott.
The Navajo Times reported a major flash flood in lower K'ai'bii'to Creek. Water flooded a portion of State Route 98. Heavy equipment was used to remove water, debris, mud, and rock from the road.
Rincon Road at Hassayampa River (normally dry) was close due to flooding.  The stream gauge on Martinez Wash at Whickenburg showed a 2 foot rise to 700 CFS rise on this normally dry wash.
Heavy rain in Utah caused a two foot rise on the Paria River just before it joined the Colorado River at Lees Ferry.
Tonto Rreek rose 2.25 feet between 730 AM and 800 AM about 10 miles south of Gisela.
Heavy rain with yard flooding was reported near Dewey-Humboldt. Pea sized hail was also reported.
The Humbug Creek RAWS reported sustained winds of 36 MPH with gusts to 71 MPH.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding on Big Bug Creek.  The water rose to the level of the bridge in Spring Valley.  The water almost overtopped South Spring Lane at 635 PM. Photos on social media showed flooding in other areas of the community.
Cataract Creek/Havasu Creek rose 18 inches at the Supai Gauge.
Agua Fria River rose 8 feet near Humboldt at 515 PM and then rose 4 feet near Cordes Junction rose 4 feet at 815 PM.
Hail up to one inch in diameter fell in Cottonwood.
A trained spotter reported a brief funnel cloud.
A train spotter reported at 61 MPH wind gust (Davis Weather Station), pea sized hail, and torrential rainfall.
Golf ball sized hail (1 3/4 inch diameter) fell near Bagdad.
Torrential rain caused flash flooding of the pit mine near Bagdad. Some of the pit walls failed and collapsed. Workers were evacuated from the mine.
The river gauge on Granite Creek in Prescott measured about a 3 foot rise in about 90 minutes (from 7.40 at 300 PM to 10.35 feet at 430 PM).
Heavy rain caused flooding at Fir Street and Monte Tesoro Drive.  The water covered the road one to two feet deep.
A flash flood was reported on Big Chino Wash by Yavapai Country Flood Control District. A river gauge on the wash showed a 4.64 foot rise.

Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire scar (2010) and the Pipeline/Tunnel (2022) Fire scar caused flash flooding over Alice Drive.  The water, mud, and many basketball sized rocks made Alice Drive impassable.
Water flooded roads 5 miles east of K'ai'bii'to.

Heavy rain over the Pipeline Fire scar (June 2021) caused flash flooding in Schultz Creek. The creek rose 4.84 feet at Highway 180. The water flooded apartments, homes, and streets on the west side of Highway 180.
Granite Creek in Prescott rose about three feet.
Flooding was reported about two miles west of Jeddito at the intersection of State Route 264 and BIA-9101.
A funnel cloud was observed along Interstate 40 between mile markers 220 and 240.
The Little Colorado River had a 3 foot rise above Lyman Lake.

The stream gauge on the Big Bug Creek in Mayer showed a rise from 1.9 to 4.9 feet in about 40 minutes starting at noon.  The flood water over topped the Spring Lane bridge over Big Bug Creek in Spring Valley at 130 PM. A video on social media showed water flowing over a low water crossing on Thunderbird Trail in Cordes Junction at 155 PM.  A river gauge on the Agua Fria River just downstream from the confluence with the Big Bug Creek showed a rise from 3.7 feet to 7.9 feet between 200 PM to 300 PM.

A river gauge on Black Canyon Creek showed a rise from 1.8 feet to 3.4 feet between 205 PM and 321 PM. A video on social media at 342 PM showed water rapidly flowing over Maren Avenue at a low water crossing on Black Canyon Creek.
A video of flash flooding in Antelope Canyon was posted on social media.
A weather spotter reported 55 MPH sustained winds with gust to at least 62 MPH on her weather station.  The winds caused damage to a small billboard sign and smaller trees.

The Sunset Point RAWS recorded a peak wind gust of 72 miles per hour at 553 PM MST. There was a tractor trailer crash (due to winds) about 40 minutes before that. Radar and the crash suggest that the strongest winds may have been around 511 PM.
A trained spotter south-southeast of Congress reported hail up to 1 and 1/8 inch.
A trained spotter posted pictures of several miles of downed power poles starting about 3.5 miles northwest of Wickenburg.
The Stanton RAWS measured a peak wind gust of 68 MPH.  The time of the gust was estimated using radar.
One inch diameter hail fell in Skull Valley.  Time was estimated using radar.

The river gauge at the Village of Supai showed a 1.83 foot rise at 1045 AM. The stream gauge at the confluence with the Colorado River (about 10 miles down stream from the Village of Supai) had a 5.5 foot rise in about 45 minutes at 1145 AM. The crest was at 12.57 feet with a flow of 1735 CFS. Base flow is at about 7 feet with a flow of 70 CFS.
A river gauge on the Paria River near the Colorado River showed a 1.83 foot rise at 545 PM MST.
Heavy rain over the Tunnel and Pipeline fire scar caused flash flooding across Highway 89. The highway closed in both directions at mile marker 430 from 108 PM until 440 PM.
Flash flooding was reported about 10 miles north of Joseph City at the intersection of Blairs Spring Wash and North Porter Road. The dirt road was washed out by the flooding and a vehicle got stuck.
The Agua Fria River rose 4 feet near Cordes Junction. This is normally dry.
Flooding was reported along Highway 96 near Bagdad.
The Seligman Fire Department reported 4 to 6 inches of water flowing over the streets in the center of town.
Quarter to golf ball sized hail (one inch to 1 3/4 inch diameter) was reported just north of Holbrook.
Pictures of a funnel cloud near Joseph City and Jack Rabbit were posted on social media.
A land-spout tornado was on the ground briefly south of the Little Colorado River. Dust from the ground was lofted into the air.
A tornado formed and traveled along the leading edge of a thunderstorm outflow boundary.
Havasu Creek rose two feet in 15 minuets just above the Village of Supai.
Heavy rain over far south-central Utah and far north-central Arizona resulted in a flash flood through Paria Canyon. The river gauge near the Colorado River showed almost a 4 foot rise.
Pictures of a funnel cloud near Window Rock were posted on social media.
Yarber Wash flooded Horsebreaker Road and other low water crossing about 5 miles east of  Dewey-Humboldt. A nearby rain gauge measured 3.50 inches of rain.

The river gauge on Havasu creek near the Colorado River rose 6.7 feet in 15 minutes between 1130 and 1145 PM MST. The river gauge is below/downstream from the Village of Supai. The flood damaged all six bridges in and around Supai Village, some of which were a total loss. The main foot and mule trail to the village was damaged and in need of repair. This 8 mile trail is the only way to the village from a road other than by helicopter.

A tornado touched down about 8 miles west-northwest of Williams in the Junipine Estates neighborhood. Ten 10 structures were damaged and or destroyed (homes and outbuildings). One power poll was blown down and the power was out in the entire community. Camping trailers/mobile homes were turn over. Some rooves were blown off houses.
The peak wind gust from a thunderstorm at Prescott Love Field was 60 MPH.
Weather spotters reported wind gusts estimated to be between 50 and 60 MPH with several two inch diameter tree branches knocked down.
Four feet of water was flowing over Back O' Beyond Road in Sedona near Cathedral Rock.
Two Arizona Cypress trees blew over from wind with a thunderstorm. The storm also produce d 1.33 inches of rain.
Wind gust of over 50 MPH was breaking branches in Prescott.
Half dollar sized hail (1 1/4 inch diameter) hail was reported about 7 miles north of Williams just after a tornado swept through.
The Clarkdale Police Department reported that the Old Jerome Highway/89A was closed due to flooding and debris.  Reta Street was also closed due to the flooding.
A funnel cloud was seen over Black Mesa from both Cow Springs and Tonalea.

The Little Colorado River began to rise in Holbrook (LHB) around 300 PM on October 3. This flow started at around 4.9 feet (34 CFS) increased, and peaked around 13.5 feet (3,700 CFS) at 900 AM on October 4. The river gauge near Winslow (LCW) started increasing at 800 AM October 3 (11.75 feet (53 CFS) and rose to 13.4 feet (700 CFS) by 900 AM. The wave from Holbrook arrived around 400 PM and rose to 17 feet/4,700 CFS by 200 AM on October 4. The river reached flood stage (19 feet/ 8,500 feet) by 100 PM. The river at Winslow crested at 19.7 feet/9,000 CFS by 700 PM. The flow crested at the confluence with the Colorado River (LCM) at 700 PM October 9 (4,400 CFS).

The Mogollon Airpark reported a peak wind gust of 60 MPH at 955 PM MST. A Mesonet station at the intersection of Highways 277 and 377 reported a peak wind gust of 65 MPH at 1013 PM. The Limestone Canyon RAWS (QLCA3) had a peak wind gust of 68 MPY at 124 AM. Wind gust of 58 MPH and higher were measured from 1124 PM to 324 AM on October 23.

A weather station in Greer reported a peak wind gust of 64 MPH at 213 AM.
The Window Rock Airport reported wind gusts over 58 MPH at 150 and 153 PM.

The wind sensor at Limestone Canyon measured wind gust over 58 MPH at 924 and 1024 AM. The wind sensor at the junction of Highways 277 and 377 measured wind gust of 58 MPH or higher between 933 AM and 133 PM.  The peak wind gust was 62 MPH at 1223 PM. The Mogollon Airpark reported wind gusts of 58 MPH or higher between 955 AM and 115 PM. The peak wind gust was 63 MPH at 1215 PM.
The Four Springs RAWS reported a 63 MPH wind gust at 319 AM and a wind gust of 62 MPH at 419 AM 6560 feet elevation.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The Taylor Airport measured wind gust of 58 MPH or higher from 1210 to 320 PM. The peak gust was 63 MPH at 155 PM.
A winds sensor at Snowbowl (9969 feet elevation) measured wind gust of 58 MPH or higher between 600 AM and 835 AM. The peak wind gust of 64 MPH was measured at 710 AM.

The winds sensor on Greens Peak (at 10118 feet) had peak wind gusts of 58 MPH or higher from 855 AM to 355 PM. The peak wind gust of 65 MPH was measured from 221 to 227 PM. The highway wind sensor on Highway 260 at mile post 378 measured a peak wind gust of 67 MPH at 1013 AM. The gusts were 58 MPH or higher from 723 AM to 305 PM. The Show Low Airport reported high winds from 915 AM to 320 PM. The peak wind gust of 68 MPH was at 155 PM.  Broken tree branches (one inch diameter) and shingle damage was reported in Show Low at 1143 AM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN COCONINO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: A wind sensor at Two Guns reported wind gusts of 58 MPH or higher from 820 AM to 1155 AM. The peak wind gust of 68 MPH was at 1033 AM.

High winds (58 MPH and stronger) hit the upper reaches of Agassiz Peak (11,555 feet) from 520 AM to 1235 PM. The strongest wind gust was 69 MPH at 920 AM.  A weather station at Lowell Observatory measured a peak wind gust of 63 MPH at 1005 AM.  There was a power outage at 951 AM in the Baderville area due to falling tree branches because of the winds. The power was out for at least 4 hours.  High winds damaged the roof at St Francis of Asis School at 1130 AM.  High winds snapped a tree near Thorpe Park at around 1115 AM.  High winds knocked a tree across powerlines and cause a power outage at around 1019 AM near Linda Vista and Adrianne (north Flagstaff).

The Arizona Department of Transportation reported a number of vehicles that were stuck, slid off the road, or crashed on I-17 on the uphill portion leaving the Verde Valley near Stoneman Lake Road.  One of the vehicles was a fire truck.

Heavy snow fell across portions of Yavapai County causing traffic issues on I-17 north of Camp Verde.  A trained spotter at around 4,800 feet reported 9.5 inches of new snow by 630 AM on December 13. This is a significant amount for that elevation. Heavy Snow criteria for that elevation is only 4 inches.
Eight inches of snow fell 6 miles west-southwest of Greer.
Heavy snow fell across the Western Mogollon Rim. Some totals (in inches) include:  Mormon Lake 10.0, Parks 9.0, east Flagstaff 8.0,  Munds Park 8.0, and Parks 8.0.
Nine inches of snow fell just east of Forest Lakes.
Cold temperatures were felt across The Western Mogollon Rim including: Mormon Lake                  -14 F, Happy Jack -9 F, 2.5 N Doney Park -6 F,  Baderville -4 F, and Williams -2 F.
The Grand Canyon Airport had a morning low of -8 F and Tusayan had a low of -2 F.
Nutrioso had a low of -3 F and Greer had a low of -1 F.

Heavy snow fell across The Western Mogollon Rim.  Snow totals include (in inches): Arizona Snowbowl (10,800 feet) 16.0,  Kachina Village 12.5, Bellemont (NWS Flagstaff) 12.5, Munds Park 15, 3 NE Parks 12.0,  Flagstaff Airport 11.4, Kachina Village 11.3,             |1 ENE Mountainaire 11.0, Fort Valley 11.0, and Flagstaff  9 to 11.
A video on social media showed flash flooding on Wet Beaver Creek between Rim Rock and Lake Montezuma.

Oak Creek began to rise at the river gauge in Sedona 1100 AM on January 1 (550 CFS), crested at over 4,500 CFC at around 500 PM (a 4 foot rise), and then returned to near normal by 1100 AM on January 2.  The Oak Creek gauge near Cornville began to rise at 400 PM on January 1 (440 CFS), crested at over 4,000 CFC in the action stage at around 900 PM (a 4.9 foot rise), and then returned to near normal after 500 PM on January 2. A video on social media showed flooding of low water crossings on Oak Creek near Rainbow Mobile Home Park and The Rainbow Trout Farm.
Ten inches of snow fell near McNary by 800 PM. Eight inches of snow fell in Show Low by 800 on January 2. Pinetop-Lakeside received 16 inches of snow.

Eight inches of snow fell in Kachina Village between 300 PM and 1000 PM.  Other snow totals across the Western Mogollon Rim include (in inches): Kachina Village 12.5, Flagstaff Airport 12.1,  Munds Park 12.0, Williams 11.0, Bellemont (NWS Flagstaff) |10.8,  5 WSW Parks 9.5, and 5 E Mountainaire 9.0.
Just over 4 inches (4.3) of snow fell near the Payson Airport at an elevation of 5,100 feet. A spotter 4 miles southeast of Washington Park reported 8 inches of snow by 730 AM on January 2.
Twenty inches of new snow fell in Forest Lakes.
Ten inches of new snow fell at the South Rim of The Grand Canyon.
Snowfall reports across Yavapai county include (in inches): Walker 8.5, 1 ESE Prescott Courthouse 6.0, and 3 S Prescott Valley 4.0.

Heavy snow fell across the Mogollon Rim.  Some of the snowfall totals include (in inches): Bellemont (NWS Flagstaff) 23.5, Kachina Village 20.0, Parks 19.5, Williams 6E                  19.0, Flagstaff Airport 17.7, Mountainaire 17.0, 7 N Williams  14.0, 10 N Parks                   14.0, and Winona 8.0.

The Grand Canyon National Park reported 10.6 inches of snow at the Desert Watch Tower view point and 8.8 at the Grand Canyon Village. Fifteen inches of new snow fell in 24 hours at the North Rim campground with 50 inches of snow on the ground.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN COCONINO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Wupatki National Monument reported 14 inches of snow.
Ten inches of snow fell three miles west of Walker.
Nine inches of snow fell one mile east of Forest Lakes.

The ADOT weather station at mile marker 378 (8 miles 8 WNW of Greer) measured a peak wind gust of 58 MPH at 1103 PM on January 14. The weather station on Greens Peak had a peak wind gust of 63 MPH at 1230 AM on January 15. The wind gusted to at least 58 MPH between 1215 AM and 145 AM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The Springerville Airport reported sustained winds of 40 MPH and/or gusts over 58 MPH between 150 AM and 740 AM.  The peak wind gust was 75 MPH at 455 AM and the maximum sustain wind was 56 MPH at the same time.
The Limestone Canyon RAWS reported a peak wind gust of 61 MPH at 224 AM.

A foot of new snow fell on the North Rim of The Grand Canyon in 24 hours with 59 inches of snow on the ground at 5 PM on 16 January.  Another 11 inches of snow fell in the 24 hours ending at 5 PM on 17 January with 69 inches of snow on the ground.

Kachina Village reported 9.5 inches of new snow. Flagstaff, Williams, and Munds Park received around 6 inches each by 5 PM on 16 January. Kachina Village reported another 10.5 inches by 5 PM 17 January with 40 inches since 14 January at 5 PM.  Flagstaff Airport had another 9.4 inches of snow in the 24 hours ending at 5 PM 17 January with 27 inches of snow on the ground.
Forest Lakes received 17 to 20 inches from the second storm from the evening of January 15 to January 17 mid-morning.

Snow fall amounts around Flagstaff ranged from around 6 inches in the morning to 9.4 inches at the airport by 500 PM (27 inches on the ground). Kachina Village received a foot (40 inches since 5 PM on Jan 14th) and Bellemont (NWS Flagstaff) 8.8 inches. Snowbowl received 9 inches at 10,800 feet (another foot the next 24 hours for a 4 day total of 61 inches).
The North Rim of The Grand Canyon received another 11 inches of snow in 24 hours.
Another 17 inches of snow fell in Forest Lakes in 24 hours.

events.cz_name: NORTHEAST PLATEAUS AND MESAS FROM HIGHWAY 264 NORTH
events.event_narrative: The Pi��on Chapter House reported 40 inches of snow from January 15 to January 17. Whippoorwill received 15 to 17 inches of new snow.

Heavy snow fell across parts of the Western Mogollon Rim.  The heaviest snow fell along Interstate 40 and west of Flagstaff.  A spotter 5 miles WSW of Parks reported |9.3 inches of snow and another spotter 7 miles north of Williams reported 9.0 inches. The area around and south of Flagstaff received between 6 and 7.3 inches of new snow.
Heavy snow (for the elevation) fell across Yavapai Country below 5000 feet. Some totals include (in inches): Rimrock/Lake Montezuma 7.0, Camp Verde 5.8, Cottonwood 4.0, and Cornville 3.8.
Heavy snow fell across the Eastern Mogollon Rim including Linden with 8.0 inches and Forest Lakes with 7 inches.

Heavy snow fell on the northeast side of Flagstaff where upslope winds enhanced the snowfall.  Reports include: Timberline 11.0 inches, Doney Park 8.5 inches, and Mormon Lake 7.0 inches. Snowbowl received 17.1 inches of snow at 10,800 feet elevation.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Eight and a half inches of new snow was reported 6 miles WNW of Vernon and 7.5 inches of new snow was reported in Vernon.
Eleven to fourteen inches of snow fell in Young. Payson received 4.5 inches close to 5000 feet in elevation.
Show Low received 10 inches of snow and Pinetop-Lakeside  received 12.0 inches of new snow.
Nine inches of snow fell about 6 miles north of Ash Fork.
Three storms hit northern Arizona impacting the Navajo Nation over 4 days. At the end, Black Mesa had 20 to 30 inches of new snow. Jeddito received 16 to 18 inches of snow.

Three storms hit northern Arizona impacting the Navajo Nation over 4 days. At the end, Sawmill 18 to 24 inches of new snow, Pine Springs 16 to 18 inches, and Tsaile 14 to 15 inches of new snow. Navajo Route 13- Buffalo Pass was closed to the public. Some Chapter houses declared and emergency due to the storm. An emergency operations center was activated. Many roads needed the snow cleared...lower elevation roads were soggy/muddy. Food, water, and propane bottles were delivered to Chapter Houses and to residences across The Navajo Nation through the end of January as this and other storms impacted travel across the area.

The sustained wind was above 40 MPH between 650 AM and 730 PM.  The wind sensor at 10,767 feet on Agassiz Peak had wind gusts above 58 MPH from 410 AM to 121 PM. The peak wind gust was 70 MPH at 750 AM. The sustained wind was above 40 MPH between 600 AM and 1130 PM.  The wind sensor at 9,379 feet on Agassiz Peak had a peak wind gust of 62 MPH at 1000 AM.
The Humbug Creek RAWS measured a peak wind gust of 61 MPH at 950 AM.
The Humbug Creek RAWS measured a peak wind gust of 63 MPH at 748 PM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The Winslow Airport reported sustained winds of 40 MPH or higher from 100 PM to around 330 PM, wind gusts of 58 MPH or higher from around 115 PM until around 300 PM, and a peak wind gust of 63 MPH at 219 PM. Blowing dust reduced the visibility at times to less than 3 miles between 100 PM and 230 PM. The ADOT sensors on I-40 at the Little Colorado River had a peak wind gust of 62 MPH at 213 PM and the one on I-40 at Jack Rabbit had a peak wind gust of 62 MPH at 323 PM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Blowing dust reduced the visibility to 3 miles or less between 100 PM and 230 PM.  The lowest visibility on the ASOS sensor was one mile between 100 PM and about 140 PM with wind gusts to around 60 MPH.

Snowfall reports from around the Western Mogollon Rim include (in inches): Doney Park 15.8, Kachina Village 14.8, Flagstaff 12.2, Bellemont (NWS Flagstaff) 11.6,  Munds Park 11.0, 3 SW Williams 10, and Parks 8.8.  Seventeen inches of snow fell at 10,800 feet about 10 miles NNW of Flagstaff.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Vernon received 13 inches of new snow. St Johns received around 8 inches of new snow. Eighteen inches of snow fell about 8 miles north of Vernon.
The Heber-Overgaard area received 8.7 inches of new snow. Linden received 9-11 inches of new snow. Forest Lakes received 18 inches of snow.
McNary received 9.5 inches of new snow, Show Low 11.5 inches, and Greer 10-14 inches.
Six to eight inches of new snow fell in Washington Park.
Forest Lakes Chapter House reported 8 inches of new snow.  Shonto Chapter House reported 7 inches of new snow.

The Tsailie/Wheatfields Chapter House reported 14 inches of new snow.

events.event_narrative: Four and a half inches of snow fell 5 miles west of Joseph City just below 5000 feet elevation.
Six inches of snow fell in Fredonia at an elevation of 4,800 feet MSL.

The Prescott Love Field ASOS reported wind gusts of 58 MPH and higher between 326 and 600 AM. The highest wind gust was 64 MPH at 456 AM. The Humbug Creek RAWS reported wind gust of 58 MPH or higher from 445 AM to around 800 AM. The peak wind gust was 72 MPH at 548 AM and 648 AM. A weather station (FW7304) 5 miles west of the Prescott airport had a peak wind gust of 67 MPH at 509 AM. A power pole was blown down in the Prescott area around 500 AM. A pine tree was blown over and fell on a house on Pine Street in Prescott around 500 PM. ||The Prescott High School athletic field scoreboard was bent in half by the strong winds at around 430 AM.
The peak wind gust at the Sunset Point RAWS was 88 MPH at 653 AM. Wind damage in the Chino Valley included a shed blown over, shingles missing/minor roof damage, and trees blown down.

The peak wind gust at the Limestone Canyon RAWS was 70 MPH at 724 AM. Winds gusted  to 58 MPH or higher from 320 AM to 1000 AM.  The peak wind gust at the ADOT sensor at the intersection of Highways 277 and 377 Intersection was 58 MPH at 303 AM. The Peak wind gust at Happy Jack was 70 MPH at 505 AM. A wind sensor at the Lowell Discovery Telescope had wind gust of 58 MPH or higher between 950 PM and 640 AM. The peak wind gust of 74 MPH was at 642 AM.

The peak wind gust at the Show Low Airport was 59 MPH at 315 AM. The ADOT sensor on Highway 260 at mile post 378 had a peak wind gust of 76 MPH 803 AM.  Wind gust were 58 MPH or higher from around 1150 PM (2/21) to around 515 PM. (There were several hours of missing data during the afternoon).

The Williams Airport observed wind gusts of 58 MPH or higher between midnight and 400 AM. The peak wind gust was 61 MPH at 135 AM. The peak wind gust at Pine Springs and I-40 (MM 159) was 78 MPH at 703 AM. The Flagstaff Airport had a peak wind gust of 74 MPH at 514 AM. Doney Park reported an estimated peak wind gust of 75 MPH at 700 AM. The trees destroyed a chicken coop.  The trees were about 65 feet tall and 22 inches DBH. Tree branches were blown down just west of downtown Flagstaff. ||Power outages were reported in Flagstaff, Doney Park, Bellemont, Mountainaire, and Munds Park.

The Window Rock Airport had a peak wind gust of 61.0 MPH at 853 AM. The wind gusted to 58 MPH or higher from around 850 to 930 AM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The Springerville Airport had a peak wind gust of 58 MPH at 415 and another peak gust of 66 MPH at 915 AM.
The peak wind gust at the Four Springs RAWS was 69 MPH at 1219 AM.

Eight inches of snow was reported near Pinetop-Lakeside by 200 PM. Ten to twelve inches of snow was reported 2 miles north of McNary by 300 PM with drifts 2 to 2.5 feet deep. The Show Low area received around 9 inches of new snow.
A trained spotter reported 9.1 inches if snow by 330 PM in southwest Flagstaff.
A trained spotter one mile east of Forest Lakes reported 13 inches of snow at 5 PM on 22 February, 19 inches at 12 AM on 23 February, and 24 inches by 730 AM on 23 February.

Nine to ten inches of new snow fell in the Williams area. A report from COCORAHS had 13.5 inches of snow 5 miles south-southwest of Parks. Nine inches of snow fell one mile west-southwest of the Flagstaff Mall. Reports from Kachina Village were that 8.5 to 11 inches of new snow fell there.
Nine inches of new snow fell in the Show Low area.
Eleven inches of snow fell near Desert View in the eastern part of The Grand Canyon National Park South Rim. Grand Canyon Village reported 8.5 inches of new snow.
An estimated 8 inches of snow fell in Ash Fork.

events.cz_name: NORTHEAST PLATEAUS AND MESAS FROM HIGHWAY 264 NORTH
events.event_narrative: Ten inches of snow fell at Red Lake.
Heavy snow fell across the Mogollon Rim. Some snowfall totals include (in inches): Kachina Village 13, Flagstaff 7-15, Bellemont 11, and the Williams area 8 to 11.
A trained spotter in Forest Lakes reported 10 inches of snow between 100 AM and 315 PM.
A person reported 5 inches of snow in Paulden at 4, 400 feet elevation. 4.5 inches of snow was reported 7 miles west of Chino Valley.
Five inches of snow was reported in Sedona at an elevation of 4,400 feet. Six inches of snow was reported at The Village of Oak Creek at 4,200 feet elevation.

Heavy snow started to fall around the Flagstaff area around midnight on March 1. The snow fell for over 30 hours. The most snow was 33 inches 3 miles N-NE of Parks. Other reports include (in inches):  Downtown Flagstaff 31, Kachina Village 30.0, Mountainaire 26, Flagstaff Airport  24.5,  Munds Park  23.8, Williams 23.0, Bellemont (NWS Flagstaff) 22.0, and 18 inches of snow fell in Timberline.

The mountains of Yavapai County (above 5,000 feet) received heavy snow. The Prescott area reported 8 to 15 inches of snow. The Iron Springs area received 11 inches of snow. Eight inches of snow fell 7 miles W-SW of Chino Valley at 5,100 feet. Nine inches of snow fell 10 miles west of Ash Fork. Ten inches of snow fell in Seligman.  Just over 11 inches (11.4 inches) was reported W-SW of Cherry at 5,200 feet. Ponderosa Park (3 miles east) reported 13 inches of new snow. Mingus West received 8 inches of snow. A foot of new snow fell 10 miles south of Ash Fort at an elevation of 5,280 feet.

The lower elevations of Yavapai County (less than 5,000 feet) generally received four to six inches of snow. A spotter near Cornville at an elevation of less than 3,400 feet reported 16 inches of new snow. The Paulden area received 4.7 inches of snow at 4,400 feet elevation. Five inches of snow fell at 4,300 feet 4 miles S-SW of Cottonwood. Just over 4 inches (4.3) fell in the Dewey-Humboldt area and in Chino Valley. Clarkdale received 4 inches of snow at 3,400 feet elevation. Four and a half inches of snow fell in Cordes Junction at around 3,700 feet. A foot of snow fell in Yarnell  at 4,800 feet. Eight and a half inches of snow fell 5 miles N-NW of Paulden at 4,750 feet. Five inches of snow and ice (4/1) was reported in Peeples Valley.

Washington Park at 6,000 feet northeast of Payson received 19 inches of snow.  Pine received 9 inches of snow. Five inches of snow fell in Payson right at the 5,000 foot level. Thirteen inches of snow fell 4 miles NW of Tonto Village at 5,800 feet.
Kayenta received 12 inches of snow.
Black Mesa Chapter House received 12 inches of snow.  Inscription Chapter House received 10 inches of new snow.

events.cz_name: NORTHEAST PLATEAUS AND MESAS FROM HIGHWAY 264 NORTH
events.event_narrative: The Pinon area received 6 to 12 inches of snow. Eight inches of new snow fell in Hardrock.
Sedona received 9 to 11 inches of snow at elevations below 5000 feet (Heavy snow criteria is only 4 inches at that elevation).
Fredonia received five inches of snow at around 4,700 feet elevation by 800 AM.
Nine inches of snow was reported at the Desert View Watchtower by 900 AM on March first. Sixteen inches of snow fell at The Grand Canyon South Rim.

A foot of new snow was reported 4 miles southeast of Valle and 4 miles north of Seligman. Ten inches of snow fell in Seligman. Nine inches of new snow was reported 5 miles N-NW of Ash Fork. Sixteen inches of new snow fell 10 miles E-NE of Seligman.
A foot of snow fell in Pinetop-Lakeside area.
Sixteen inches of new snow was reported in Forest Lakes.
Snowfall amounts across the Western Mogollon Rim include (in inches): Flagstaff Airport            10.9, Bellemont (NWS Flagstaff) 9.7, and Kachina Village 9.5.
Ten inches of snow fell in Forest Lakes.

Oak Creek began flooding in Oak Creek Canyon around 700 AM on March 15.  The road was closed near Orchard Canyon Lodge and Banjo Bill Campground. There was 3 feet of water above the road at a stage of 5.22 feet at the Sedona gauge. Cooper Cliffs Road was closed by 1100 AM MST due to the flooding. Doodlebug and New Castle Lane were close at around 200 AM on March 16. The creek remained above this level for just over 3 days. The peak flow as about 10.5 feet at 800 AM MST on March 16.||The Oak Creek gauge near Cornville (OACA3) showed more than a 7.5-foot rise from             5.2 feet at 1PM March 15 to a crest of 12.76 feet at 115 AM on March 16. The gauge dropped back to around 5.2 feet by 1000 AM March 17. ||The Sedona Police Department reported that evacuations were made along Oak Creek from the evening of March 15 through the morning of March 16.  The locations that were evacuated include Rancho Sedona RV Park,  Trails End Road, Trails End Lane, Blackhawk Lane, Newcastle Lane, Oak Creek Mobilelodge,  Sycamore Road, The Center of the New Age, and the Villas at Poco Diablo Resort. ||A rock slide closed Highway 89 through the upper part of Oak Creek Canyon (switchbacks) about 3 miles north of Slide Rock State Park around 323 PM on March 16.

Extensive flooding was reported along Dry Beaver Creek across Kimberlys Way (150 feet wide). The river gauge upstream reported a 4 foot rise. The creek crested around midnight on March 16 at about 4.5 feet above the creek bed.
The Granite Creek Gauge showed water rising from 6.00 feet around 400 AM MST March 15 to a crest of 8.00 feet at midnight on March 16.

The Wet Beaver Creek gauge near Rimrock rose from 5.5 feet at 1000 AM MST on March 15 to 9.4 feet at 400 PM. The creek dropped back to 5.5 feet by noon on March 17. A local newspaper reported that areas along Wet Beaver Creek were evacuated.  This included Rimrock near Lake Montezuma and people along Beaver Vista Drive and Rimrock Drive.  An overnight shelter was set up at Camp Verde Middle School.

The Verde River Gauge near Clarkdale started raising rapidly around 1000 AM March 15 from around 8.00 feet to a crest of around 15.8 feet by 1100 PM MST on March 15. The Verde River dropped back to around 8.0 feet by 900 AM on March 18.  The Verde River in Camp Verde started to rise rapidly around 500 PM on March 15 from 11.8 feet. The crest was at 20.8 feet at 300 March 16 and the river returned to 11.8 feet by 900 PM on March 19.  The Verde River below Tangle Creek began to rise rapidly around 500 PM from 12.0 feet.  The crest was around 700 PM at 20.3 feet and slowly fell back to 12.0 feet by 400 PM by 400 PM March 19.||Homes were flooded along Bates Drive in Cottonwood.
The West Clear Creek gauge near Camp Verde showed a 5-foot rise from 2.8 feet at noon on March 15 to a crest of 8.1 feet by 100 AM March 16. The water level returned to 2.8 feet by 9 AM on March 17.

Snow started to fall in the Flagstaff area around 800 PM on March 20. Eight inches accumulated by 11 AM on March 21. Light snow continued through the day on March 22. By the afternoon of March 22, 10.9 inches of snow fell at the Flagstaff Airport and 9.7 inches at the NWS office in Bellemont. A spotter in Kachina Village reported a total of 9.5 inches of snow.
Ten inches of snow fell in Forest Lakes between the evening of March 20 and the afternoon of March 21 when the snow changed to rain.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The winds at the Springerville Airport had winds gusts of 58 MPH or higher between 1100 AM and 530 PM. The peak wind gust was 73 MPH at 315 PM.  The sustained wind was above 40 MPH for about the same period of time.
The ADOT wind sensor at Lupton and Interstate 40 reported a peak wind gust of 67 MPH at 1133 AM MST.
The Humbug Creek RAWS reported a peak wind gust of 65 MPH at 348 AM. The wind gusts were estimated to be 58 MPH or higher between 308 and 408 AM MST.
The peak wind gust at the Limestone RAWS was 62 MPH at 1024 AM.  The wind gust were estimated to be at or above 58 MPH from around 530 AM to 1030 AM.
The peak wind gust at the Flagstaff Airport of 59 MPH was reported at 1259 AM MST.

The USGS stream gage at Wet Beaver Creek two crests. The first one was from 1000 AM to 400 PM on March 21 and the second one was from 700 AM to 1200 PM on March 22.  Clogging of the gauge affected the actual flows.  Media showed pictures and videos of property and homes flooded in Rimrock along East Beaver Vista and East Sycamore Lanes (both on 3/21 and 3/22).

The stream gauge on Oak Creek in Sedona rose above action stage at  (7 feet) at 900 AM on March 21.  It reached a peak of 16.35 feet at 600 AM on March 22 and then dropped below 7 feet around 1100 PM March 22.  Flood stage is at 14.0 feet.

The Verde River rose above flood state at Clarkdale around 11 PM on March 21 due to rain and melting snow. The flood waters continued downstream into Horseshoe Lake. The water dropped below action stage around noon on March 24. ||The stream gauge on the Verde River near Paulden reported a peak stage of 13.2 feet with a flow of 16,000 CFS at 400 PM on March 22. This is the second highest peak for this gauge. ||Properties between the Verde River and Bates road in Cottonwood south of State Route 89A were reported to have inundated by at least a foot of water by 930 AM on March 22.

Highway 377 between Heber and Holbrook was closed due to flooding at mile post 13 around 900 AM on March 22. Seymour's Crossing was flooded the night of March 22. A vehicle was swept downstream for about an hour. The occupants were able to reach the bank but, were separated. The woman's body was found the next day.

A stream gauge on the Agua Fria River near Black Canyon City reported a rise of over 15.5 feet. The river started to rise at around 800 AM on March 21. The river reached the flood stage around 400 AM March 22 and remained above flood stage until around 500 PM. The Rivers Edge RV Park was evacuated due to flooding.

Rain and rain on snow caused the The Little Colorado River in Navajo County to reach flood stage in the evening of March 22. The river gauge at Holbrook showed a sharp rise around 800 PM. The river dropped back down at that location around 800 PM on March 24.  The river gauge at Winslow showed a sharp rise around 1000 PM on March 23 and dropped back down around 1100 AM on March 24. The Bird Springs Chapter House (downstream of Winslow) poste a video that showed flooding over Navajo Route 71 (impassable) at 1000 AM on March 24.
The Little Colorado River in Apache County began to flood early March 22. The river remained high until mid-day March 24.

The river gauge on the Little Colorado River near Cameron showed a spike starting around 1100 AM on March 21.  The river dropped back down and then showed a steady increase again around noon on March 23 corresponding to flows arriving from the Winslow area. The river at Cameron dropped back down again by the evening of March 25.  The hydrograph on the LCR at the Colorado River showed the same trace 6 hours later...dropping down around noon on March 26.
The Four Springs RAWS had a peak wind gust of 63 MPH at 119 PM.
The peak wind gust at the Grand Canyon Airport was 59 MPH at 354 PM MST.
The peak wind gust at Cherry RAWS was 60 MPH at 311 PM.  The peak wind gust at Humbug Creek RAWS was 58 MPH at 348 PM.
The wind sensor along Interstate 40 at Lupton measured a peak wind gust of 66 MPH at 614 PM MST.  Wind gusts of 58 MPH or higher were measured from 230 to 620 PM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN COCONINO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Wind gusts of 58 MPH or higher were recorded at the Two Guns ADOT wind sensor along Interstate 40 between 1110 AM and around 500 PM MST. The peak wind gust was  67 MPH at 113 PM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Strong winds (58 MPH or higher) blew across the Little Colorado River Valley in Navajo County from late morning through late afternoon. Here are some peak wind gusts recorded in the area (in MPH): Winslow Airport 68 at 232 PM,  Jack Rabbit 64 at 423 PM,                  and Taylor Airport 62 at 355 PM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Strong winds moved across the Little Colorado River Valley in Apache County from around 400 PM to around 600 PM.  The highest wind gust observed were 62 MPH at both Petrified Forest National Park (423 PM) and Springerville Airport (515 PM).

High wind was observed across the Western Mogollon Rim during the afternoon.  Some of the peak wind gusts observed were (in MPH): Williams Airport 62 at 315 PM, Flagstaff Airport 59 at 412 PM,  Arizona Snowbowl Pumphouse 58 250 PM (9,969 feet elevation).
Peak wind gusts across the Eastern Mogollon Rim include (in MPH): Happy Jack                   65 at 419 PM, Limestone Canyon 63 at 524 PM,  and the Highway 277 - 377 Intersection 58 at 543 PM.

The highest wind gust across the White Mountains as 67 MPH on State Route 260 near mile marker 378 (just over 9,000 feet elevation). Greens Peak (over 10,00 feet) had a peak wind gust of 64 MPH at 156 PM.  Greer had a peak wind gust of 61 MPH at 435 PM.

The highest wind gust across the White Mountains as 67 MPH on State Route 260 near mile marker 378 (just over 9,000 feet elevation). Greens Peak (over 10,00 feet) had a peak wind gust of 64 MPH at 156 PM.  Greer had a peak wind gust of 61 MPH at 435 PM.
The Rio de Flag overflowed along Dupont Avenue, Ellery Avenue, and Riles Street due to melting snow.

Warm temperatures, melting snow, and snow blocking drainages caused flooding along Kramer Street and Fremont Boulevard. This happened two days in a row. Enough snow had melted by the third day to prevent flooding of the roads.
Schultz Creek overflowed and impacted homes and apartments along Stevanna Way in the Coconino Estates area.

The Navajo Nation Emergency Manager reported flooding in Chinle on the Chinle Creek early on April 23. The flood warning was downgraded to an advisory on April 30. The emergency operations center was staffed until May 9th.

events.cz_name: NORTHEAST PLATEAUS AND MESAS SOUTH OF HIGHWAY 264
events.event_narrative: The wind sensor on Interstate 40 at the Painted Desert intersection (MP 312) reported a peak wind gust of 59 MPH (sustain at 42 MPH) at 1253 PM MST.
A report from Facebook showed that 1 1/2 inch hail fell two miles east-northeast of Fort Valley.
A report of 1 1/2 inch diameter hail from 5 miles north of Walker was received.
Heavy rain caused flooding along Highway 69 in Prescott Valley. Rose Creek flooded Hornet Drive.

A Yavapai County Alert gauge on Black Canyon Creek showed about a two foot rise at 1040 PM.  A downstream gauge (Auga Fria--AFRA3) showed a rise at 200 AM on April 20. The river remained elevated through the evening of May 23.

A thunderstorm produced 0.87 of an inch of rain about a mile south of downtown Prescott. This storm moved northeast and dropped just over an inch of rain (1.04) four miles north of Prescott Valley. The Prescott Airport received 1.48 inches of rain between 300 PM and 500 PM.
Almost an inch and a quarter (1.24) of rain fell in the Paulden area.
An inch of rain fell in the Cottonwood area.
New record lows were set for Bellemont (23 broke the pervious low of 30 in 2019) and Flagstaff (29  broke the pervious low of 32 set in 1975).
The Grand Canyon Airport set a new record low of 28.  This broke the pervious low of 30 last set in 1998.
The Window Rock Airport set a new record of 31. The pervious record low of 32 was last set in 2019.
The stream gauge on White River (WHTA3) near Ft Apache showed a 400 CFS spike.

Lightning from a Monsoon thunderstorm destroyed a house in Baderville, north of Flagstaff Monday. Summit Fire and Medical crews arrived at the home just after 12:30 p.m. on a report of the roof of the home on fire. As crews got closer to the scene, firefighters could see smoke from Highway 180 and the fire was moved to a first alarm. Initial crews arrived to find heavy smoke coming from the attic of the home. More crews arrived to work the fire, including two water tenders. In all a total of 11 units and two battalion chiefs responded to the fire. There were no injuries to civilians or fire personnel and the home is a total loss (KAFF Country News).
Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire (2010) scar and the Pipeline/Tunnel Fire (2022) caused the Upper Campbell drainage to flood.

A USGS stream gage on the Little Colorado River at Woodruff showed a rise of 6.9 feet starting at 120 PM on August 9. The flow returned to a normal level around 1000 PM on August 10. The flood started at Hoolbrook at 600 PM August and rose around 4.5 feet by 200 AM on August 10. This flood reached the Colorado River at 500 PM on August 10 and the river level rose 1.7 feet.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Antelope Canyon. It was closed for a day to remove the flood debris.
Strong thunderstorm wind gusts observed in Face Canyon (Lake Powell) with considerable blowing sand.
Jacob Lake received more than 12 inches of snow and the North Rim received 15 inches of snow.
As much as 8 inches of snow was reported at Strawberry.
As much as 12 inches of snow fell at the South Rim of the Grand Canyon.
More than 5 inches of snow fell near Seligman.
As much as 13 inches of snow fell near Navajo National Monument.

Snow and strong winds created traffic problems and road closures across the Western Mogollon Rim. Wind gusts to 37 MPH blew the 3 to 6 inches of fresh snow into drifts. Law Enforcement agencies in the area reported 33 traffic accidents and 50 slide-offs/motorist assists. Several area roads were closed due to blowing and drifting snow.
As much as 12 inches of snow fell near Fort Valley.
The North Rim of the Grand Canyon received 12 inches of new snow.
Eight inches of new snow fell at the South Rim of the Grand Canyon.
As much as 6 inches of snow fell in Prescott.
St Michaels received as much as 10 inches of snow.
Nine inches of new snow fell in Greer.

A quick moving winter storm dropped just over seven (7.2) inches in the Flagstaff area Wednesday afternoon into early Thursday morning.  Arizona DPS responded to 11 minor traffic accidents and 42 vehicle slid-offs. The City of Flagstaff Police Department responded to 19 non-injury accidents.

Tonto Creek near Roosevelt started to rise from a level of 3.7 feet (630 CFS) at around 1100 AM on March 21.  The flooding started earlier upstream. The first peak flow of 12.2 feet (23,300 CFS) was at 800 PM on March 21. A second peak of 12.5 feet (25,500 CFS) was observed at 800 AM on March 22. The gauge dropped back down to action level at (4.35 feet) on March 25 at 800 AM. An elderly couple and their dog were killed in the Bear Flat area when they cross the flooded Tonto Creek in their truck.
Landspout tornado was  spotted 10 miles north of Cameron, Arizona at 1:50 MDT. Only visible lofted debris was dust. Dissipated within 10 minutes after sighting. Video on Twitter.
Widespread standing water was seen next to State Route 77. The highway was not flooded.
Indian Route 15 was closed due to flooding at mile post 95 between Cornfields and Greasewood. Report was from Navajo Nation Road Conditions Facebook page.

Fossil Creek Road (Forest Road 708) closed for several days due to damage from heavy             rain and flooding that occurred on August 16th and 17th. Closure began morning of             August 18th and remain closed for several week or more.

Between 1 to 2.5 inches of rain fell in around two hours just east and northeast of the town of Tusayan and the South Entrance to The Grand Canyon National Park. This caused significant flooding of homes homes, buildings, and cars. Highway 64 into the GCNP was closed, shelter in place orders were put into place, and children were stuck in their school             because they could not safely get home.
Heavy rain over the Schultz (2010) and Pipeline (2022) fire scars brought debris flowing over Copland Lane. A road grader was needed to clear the road.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms moving south over the Paria River basin (including in Utah) caused flash flooding. The river gauge on the Paria River near the Colorado River (Lees Ferry) measured a rise in water the level 4.8 feet at 8:15 PM MST to 6.6 feet at 11:00 PM.
One to 1.5 inch diameter hail was reported in the Payson area between 330 and 345 PM MST.
Strong winds broke large tree limbs, uprooted trees, blew shingles off structures, and caused power outages for much of the city of Page.
A short lived-landspout tornado video was relayed to the NWS.
A weather station two miles north of the Prescott Courthouse reported a peak wind gust of 64 MPH.
The Sedona Airport recorded a 60 MPH peak wind gust from a thunderstorm outflow at 315 PM MST.
The Agua Fria River near Cordes Junction rose 2.2 feet between 1100 PM on July 22 and midnight on July 23. The water remained elevated for about 12 hours.
Black Canyon Creek near Cleator rose to 2.92 feet (1026 CFS).
The Verde River near Clarkdale rose from 1.59 feet to 3.84 feet between 900 PM and 1000 PM. The river remained elevated until the next afternoon.
Quarter sized hail was reported in the Yavapai Hills area. One inch diameter hail was reported near Costco about 30 minutes later.
A video on social media showed a flash flood in Big Bug Creek in Mayer.
Heavy rain over the Schultz (2010) and Pipeline (2022) fire scars lead to flooding on the west end of Copeland Lane.

Heavy rain over the northern portion of the Schultz (2010) and Pipeline/Tunnel (2022) fires caused flash flooding in the Wupatki Trails neighborhood. This flooding stayed within the newly constructed channels and into the Cinder Lakes area as designed.

An automated stream gauge on Cataract Creek (9 miles SSE of the Village of Supai) measured a 6 foot rise at 315 PM. A gauge near the confluence with the Colorado River showed a 1.6 foot rise starting at around 400 AM MST on July 31.
A thunderstorm produced high winds (estimated at 60 MPH) with frequent lightning and heavy rainfall.
A thunderstorm produced heavy rain causing street flooding rendering the roads impassable.
A spotter relayed a picture that showed a mixture of dime, nickel, and quarter sized hail.
The stream gauge on Havasu Creek near the Colorado River measured a 1.5 foot rise.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms over southern Utah and far northern Arizona caused flash flooding in the Paria River. The river gauge on the Paria at Lees Ferry (Colorado River) showed a two foot rise between 415 PM and 645 PM.
A landspout was reported near Chino Valley and was on the ground for one to two            minutes.
Quarter sized hail (one inch in diameter), very heavy rain, and local flooding was reported in the Cottonwood area.
Law Enforcement reported that the Big Chino Wash flooded Big Springs Ranch Road.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm caused flooding with debris flows over Highway 89 near mile marker 483. The highway was closed in both directions for about 30 minutes.
The grave gauge on the Verde River at Clarksdale showed a rapid 3 foot rise.

Heavy rain fell across Coconino County. Some of the 24 hour rainfall amounts include (in inches): Arizona Snowbowl: 2.92, Bright Angel Point North Rim: 1.14, Four Springs RAWS: 1.13, Mable Canyon: 0.74, Tusayan: 0.73, and Jacob Lake 0.71.

Heavy rain fell across Yavapai County between September 2 and 3. Here are some 24 hour amounts (in inches) ending at noon on September 3: 11 miles SW of Prescott 1.28, 3 miles northwest of Camp Verde 1.25, 2 miles southwest of McGuireville 1.25,  and 2 miles southwest of Cottonwood 0.93.

Heavy rain over Agassiz Peak and the area between Agassiz Peak and Fremont Peak caused a flash flood on the southern side of Agassiz Peak. The Kachina Trail had two deep channels cut through it about 400 yards apart. Those channels were 10 to 12 feet deep and extended above and below the trail. Some of the rocks in the flow were 3 to 5 feet in diameter. The two channels joined and the debris, water, and mud flowed southwestward. Most of the debris formed an alluvial fan just uphill from Freidlein Prairie Road. Water and mud did flow across that road.
The peak wind gust at Limestone Canyon RAWS was 61 MPH at 124 PM. The wind gusted above 58 MPH from around 1110 AM to 145 PM.
The peak wind gust of 61 MPH was measured at 1103 AM at mile marker 378 on SR 260 near Greer. Gust of 58 MPH ere reported between 940 and 1110 AM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The Springerville Airport reported a peak wind gust of 63 MPH at 1035 AM. Winds peaked above 58 MPH between 1025 and 1120 AM.
A sensor on Greens Peak reported a peak wind gust of 59 MPH at 353 AM (10,100 feet MSL).
The ADOT wind sensor along Interstate-40 at Lupton measured a peak wind gust of 60 MPH at 1053 AM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN COCONINO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The ADOT wind sensor along Interstate 40 at Two Guns reported a peak wind gust of 74 MPH at 1003 AM. Wind gusts above 58 MPH were observed between 930 AM and 1150 AM.
The weather station in Page reported a peak wind gust of 60 MPH.
Limestone Canyon reported a peak wind gust of 66 MPH at 1024 AM. The ADOT wind sensor at the Intersection of Highways 277 and 377 reported a peak wind gust of 58 MPH at 1133 AM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The Taylor Airport measured a peak wind gust of 59 MPH at 1035 AM.

Survey Summary: Showers developed across the central Mogollon Rim and|moved eastward this morning. Radar indicated that one particular cell|located west-southwest of Star Valley moved quickly to the east-|southeast just after 09:35 AM. NWS Flagstaff, in partnership with the|Hellsgate Fire Department, noted the first sign of damage associated|with the tornado just south of Arizona Route 260, roughly one mile|southwest of Star Valley.||This, in conjunction with radar imagery, provides strong evidence|that the tornado initially developed around 09:39 AM MST. The survey|revealed that the tornado tracked rapidly eastward, consistent with|radar imagery. There was noteworthy damage to a home, an outbuilding,|and additional damage to softwood and hardwood trees during the first|one-fourth to one-third mile portion of the damage path.||The tornado continued for a mile and churned eastward toward|Houston Creek where the damage to residential structures, largely|manufactured homes, was most concentrated. At least 20 structures were|impacted, with damage confined to windows and roofs. Some roofs were|partially removed. The concentration of damage diminished just under|one-half mile east of Houston Creek, suggesting that the tornado|dissipated. This is corroborated with radar imagery, and the estimated time|of dissipation is set at 09:49 AM MST. Based on damage indicators, the|tornado estimated peak wind speed was placed at 105 mph (EF1).

Heavy rain over Agassiz Peak caused a flash flood on the northeastern side of the peak Peak into Locket Meadow. The water catchment in Snowslide Canyon was plugged with debris and damaged. One of the pump houses in the Inner Basin was damaged. The waterline that provides up to 30 percent of the water in Flagstaff during the summer was exposed and damaged in several locations. The access road around the water houses on Waterline Road was washed out.

Eight inches of snow fell at North Rim Entrance Station of the Grand Canyon National Park at 8,800 feet elevation. Four inches of snow fell at the Bright Angel Ranger Station on the North Rim (edge) of the Grand Canyon at just over 8,200 feet elevation.

Six to eight inches of snow fell around Del Muerto (8 miles E-NE of Chinle) at 6,400 feet.  Six inches of snow fell in Chinle at 5,500 feet. Six inches of snow also fell in Many Farms at 5,300 feet elevation.
Six to eight inches of snow fell around Del Muerto (8 miles E-NE of Chinle) at 6,400 feet.

Thirteen inches of new snow fell over higher elevations (9,400 feet) of the White mountains over a 50 hour period. Seven inches fell by 800 AM on December 23 (24 hour total). Alpine (8,000 feet) received 7 inches of snow from December 22 to 23.
Eight inches of new snow fell in the community of Wheatfields. Seventeen inches of new snow fell 12 NNW Sawmill and 10 inches fell in Sawmill.
Sunrise Park Ski Resort measured 10.0 inches of snow in 24 hours at an elevation of 10,000 feet. Eight inches of snow fell 5 miles east of Pinetop-Lakeside (at about 7,200 feet elevation).

The Flagstaff airport received 8 inches of snow by noon on January 7.  The total for the day was 10.8 inches. Other snow amounts (in inches): Parks 11.7,  Kachina Village 9.5 to 12.8, Munds Park 10.5, Williams 9.0, NWS Bellemont office 8.8.

Five inches of snow fell in Payson below 5,000 feet elevation. Tonto Village received 7 inches of new snow at 5,800 feet elevation. Washington Park received 9 inches of new snow at around 5,300 feet elevation. Five inches of snow fell in Young at 5,200 feet MSL.
Fourteen inches of snow fell Forest Lakes. Eight inches of new snow fell in Heber-Overgaard. Nine inches of new snow fell 13 miles east-northeast of Clints Well in the Blue Ridge area.
Nine inches of snow fell 4 miles northwest of McNary. Pinetop received 7 inches of new snow.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Nine inches of new snow fell in Concho at around 6,000 feet elevation.
The Tolikan Chapter House reported 8 to 14 inches of new snow their area from Sunday to             Monday depending on location and elevation.
Five inches of snow was reported 8 miles west of Chino Valley at an elevation of 4,800 feet.
Storm total snow was 8 inches at Sawmill Chapter house.

Snow started falling across the Western Mogollon Rim around 630 AM on February 6.  By 730 PM, Parks had received 8.5 inches of snow. The snow continued to fall into the evening of February 9th. Here are some of the three day snowfall totals in inches: Parks 36.0, Flagstaff 32 to 36.1, Williams 30.0,  areas surrounding Flagstaff 11.6 to 28.9,  and Munds Park 28.6.  A location 3 miles south of Mormon Lake received 14 inches of snow by 900 AM on February 7.  Schools were closed in the area.  Many tree branches and trees fell in the Flagstaff under the weight of the snow. There were spotty power outages as well.

Snow started falling over the Grand Canyon Country during the morning of February 6. By 0800 on the 7th, eight inches had fallen at the North Rim. Over 21 inches (21.5) of new snow fell at the North Rim by 1100 AM on the 9th. The South Rim had 10.7 by the time the snow stopped.
Three feet of new snow fell in Forest Lakes in less than three days. Eleven inches of snow fell in Heber.  Just over nine inches (9.2) fell 4 miles south-southwest of Shumway by 400 PM on February 7.

Snow started falling in Washington Park (5,400 feet) at 1100 PM on February 6. Twenty-nine inches fell by the time the snow stopped late morning on February 9th. Strawberry received 24 inches and Pine received 14 inches of snow over 3 days. A location 4 miles south of Washington Park received 15.5 inches of snow in 2 days (by the afternoon of the 8th).

Snow started to fall around 800 AM on February 6 across the White Mountains. McNary picked up 8 inches of snow by 800 AM on the 7th and 14 inches by 800 PM.  The Pinetop-Lakeside area received 10 to 15 inches of new snow by 800 PM on the 7th. Sunrise Ski Park received 29 inches of new snow over 3 days. Nutrioso had a three day total of 7.3 inches.

Heavy snow fell across the greater Prescott area over a three day period. Snow started falling during the evening of February 6.  By 300 AM, some locations above 5000 feet received 8 inches of snow. Snow totals for the three day event ranged from 5 inches north of (lower than Prescott) to over 20 inches northwest of (higher than) Prescott. Groom Creek received 10.3 inches of new snow by 900 AM on the 7th. Crown King received 9 inches by 8 PM on the 7th.

Very strong winds blew out numerous windows and caused extensive damage to Cliffdwellers Lodge near Vermillion Cliffs during the late afternoon on June 4th. The winds, possibly enhanced by the nearby cliffs, blew out windows in 5 parked cars and several of the motel rooms in the Lodge. The housing units also had broken windows, some damaged awnings, and and damaged trailer skirtings. Both the Lee's Ferry and Marble Canyon Lodges reported high winds but, no damage. Blowing dust made it difficult to even see across Highway 89A.

The water flow started to increase (from 4.98 feet) around 100 PM MST on August 13.  There were three crests in the flow: 6.24 feet at 500 PM, 704 feet at 800 PM MST on August 13, and 7.66 feet at 300 AM MST on August 14. Flash flooding occurred which resulted in many people being evacuated from the campgrounds on the creek, with helicopter evacuations for people stranded at the remote village of Supai.  At least 6 homes had flood damage in the Village of Supai. Over 100 campers were stranded in the campground. One person was washed away near the confluence with the Colorado River. Her body was recovered over 18 miles down the Colorado River three days later.
