Tribal officials from the Havasupai Reservation reported that trails were flooded and impassable along Havasu Creek causing hikers to be stranded.  All hikers were later accounted for, no injuries or fatalities.  Some structures in the village of Supai were also impacted.

Public reported via social media a video of a landspout tornado out in a rural field about 5 miles NNE of Springerville.  No damage was reported.  Tornado was rated EFU, but could be an EF0.  No damage survey was done.  Path is approximated.
A thunderstorm produced nickle sized hail that accumulated on the ground.
Wind gusts from a thunderstorm blew down 4 to 6 trees on a golf course.
The Yavapai County Sheriff's Office reported nickle sized hail in and around Mayer.
Strong thunderstorm winds knocked down power lines in Mayer.
A thunderstorm produced heavy rain and hail in Parks.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm flooded portions of Page Springs Road near Page Springs.  The highway department had to remove the rocks that were covering the road as a result of the flooding.

Heavy rain from a thunderstorm caused Houston Creek to overflow in Star Valley east of Payson.  Water crossed two roads three feet deep in places. The roads were closed for about two and a half hours.
A trained spotter sent video and photos of Yuma Wash flooding over N. Reed Road between W Road 4.5 N and W Road 5 N.
A county official reported a 5 foot rise in 45 minutes at the Rio de Flag Coconino County ALERT gauge located near the Flagstaff Mall.
A USGS stream gauge on the Little Colorado River near Woodruff reported a 6.3 foot rise  in one hour from near nearby thunderstorms  producing heavy rainfall.
A USGS river gauge on the Agua Fria River at Cordes Lakes reported at 5.9 foot rise in 45  minutes from thunderstorms upstream along Big Bug Creek.
A Yavapai County river gauge on the Agua Fria River at Kelton Ranch reported a 6.3 foot  rise in 15 minutes. Peak flow was 9,515 cubic feet per second.
Yavapai County Sheriff's Office reported a bridge in Spring Valley was impassable with water flowing over the road.  A car was also stranded on the bridge.
Public sent via social media a video of a flash flood along Big  Bug Creek. The person posting the video said it was the highest flow since 2021.
Public reported, via social media, a video of flash flooding in Big Bug Creek across a low water crossing.
Public reported hail up to the size of quarters.
A social media post showed hail up to the size of quarters.  The location has been estimated.
A USGS stream gauge reported a rise of 5.01 feet on the Agua Fria River near Humboldt.

Public reported a low water crossing at N. Contessa Way flooded and impassible with several feet of flowing water. Radar estimated 1.25-1.75  inches occurred in 30 minutes over the Dry  Beaver Creek Basin just north of McGuireville.
ADOT reported State Route 87 closed due to flooding of an underpass at milepost 342 in Winslow.
A USGS stream gauge on Tonto Creek above Gun Creek (TNRA3) reported a 2 foot rise after heavy rainfall upstream earlier in the morning.
Flooding was reported via AZ511.com on the I-17 Southbound lanes near Stoneman Lake Rd.
The USGS stream gauge on Cataract Creek below Heather Wash measured a 2.8 foot rise in one hour due to upstream heavy rainfall.
Public reported 2 feet of water in Webber Creek with debris from the West Fire scar after heavy rain fell on the scar.
Public reported a minor debris flow in the gully crossing Control Road (FS 64) after heavy rain fell on the West Fire scar.

Multiple trees down. The trees were about a foot in diameter at the base. Fifteen power poles were blown down with about 4000 feet of line. The power was out for about 36 hours in portions of Bridgeport. An above ground pool was smashed to bits and crumpled like an accordion.
Strong winds from passing showers caused significant damage to the Antelope Point Marina on Lake Powell. The wind blew a transformer and caused damage to Dock 3.
A weather spotter 8 miles southwest of Show Low reported 3/4 inch diameter hail.
An employee at the Prescott Love Field air traffic control tower reported seeing a funnel cloud southeast of the airport for 15 minutes.
A funnel cloud was seen northeast of the Petrified Forest National Park.

A man was working on a fence when lightning hit nearby or hit the fence. The jolt knocked the man away and ripped the glove off his hand. He had numbness and tingling in his arm. He was transported to the hospital for observation.

Lightning struck an 80-foot tall ponderosa pine tree and at least one of two golfers on a local golf course. The upper 60 feet of the pine tree was blown apart.  Both men were hospitalized and one was in critical condition.
An area of thunderstorms producing heavy rain (two inches in less than an hour) caused flash flooding over the highway from Snowflake to Concho.
A thunderstorm produced dime to nickel sized (3/4 to 7/8 inch diameter) hail about one mile east-northeast of Payson.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm washed out Hunt Road north of Leupp Corner.
Strong winds from a thunderstorm knocked down an eight inch diameter tree about 10 mile south of the Petrified Forest National Park.

Received social media video of a distant vortex or landspout tornado.  It formed along intersecting outflow boundaries.  Inconclusive whether the rotating column extended to the base of the cloud.  Exact duration unknown but likely very short lived.  Damage unknown but likely none to minimal as it was out in open desert.
A USGS river gauge on the Paria River near the confluence with the Colorado River (PLFA3) measured a 3.3 foot rise.
A USGS stream gage on Jacks Canyon Creek (JCCA3) measured a 2.5 foot rise from  heavy rain upstream.  The rain happened on Sunday afternoon.
Public reported heavy rain near Glen Canyon Dam that closed the Chains and Hanging Gardens trailheads due to flooding.  Rainfall was estimated at 0.5 inches.
Law enforcement reported street flooding at the intersection of AZ Highway 260 and Quail Run Road.  Radar estimated 2 to 3 inches of rain had fallen in a short amount of time in the area.
A thunderstorm produced 3/4 inch diameter hail in Kachina Village with heavy rain.
A USGS stream gauge on the Agua Fria River near Humboldt (AFHA3) recorded a rise of 5.91 feet.

Public reported seven power poles knocked down or snapped over Salt Mine Road due to strong downburst winds.  Power was knocked out for a large area of Camp Verde.  Salt Mine Road was closed for over 12 hours.
Antelope Canyon Tribal Park Service sent photos of water flowing through Antelope Canyon.  High water marks indicated water depth of 1 to 2 feet prior to entering Antelope Canyon.  Time is estimated.

A USGS stream gauge on Granite Creek (GCRA3) measured a 4.6 foot rise in 30 minutes.  A CoCoRaHS observer upstream of the gauge confirmed water nearing a business parking lot in downtown Prescott.  The observer measured 2.05 inches of rain.
An ADOT webcam showed visibility reduced to an estimated 3/4 of a mile on I-17 near Sunset Point.

Forest Service officials report flooding with ash laden water through House Rock Wash along Buffalo Ranch Road (Forest Road 8910).  The road was impassable and blocked access for BAER team members performing work in the area.  The White Sage burn scar was upstream from this location.
The USGS river gauge on the Verde River below Camp Verde (VCVA3) recorded a 4 foot rise (1,650 cfs) in an hour due to heavy rainfall upstream.
A Yavapai County ALERT gauge on the Agua Fria River at Kelton Ranch reported a 2.7 foot  rise in 15 minutes from heavy rainfall in Big Bug Creek.
The USGS river gauge on the Agua Fria River near Cordes Lakes (AFMA3) reported a 2 foot rise (117 cfs) in 15 minutes due to heavy rainfall along Big Bug Creek.
A USGS stream gauge at Lees Ferry (PLFA3) measured a 1.2 foot rise on the Paria River.  Water would likely have been higher upstream closer to the heavier rainfall.  Time estimated by radar.
Public reported, via Facebook, a video of flooded washes and a flooded road. Time and specific location were estimated.
A stream gauge on Tonto Creek (TNRA3) measured a 3.02 ft rise in 45 minutes.  Can infer flash flooding further upstream near the Rye Creek and Tonto Creek confluence.
Law enforcement reported a 3 ft rise on Havasu Creek.  Times are estimated.
A Cocorahs observer measured 2.80 inches of rain at 4 NNW Paulden.  Minor flooding was reported over a private road near Feather Mountain Road.
The ADOT site located on SR-77 at 14 mile hill (AZT12) measured a 60 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
The St. Johns Airport ASOS station (KSJN) measured a 64 mph thunderstorm wind gust.

The National Park Service and USGS provided pictures and USGS stream gage data of a flash flood event that occurred in North Canyon Wash.  The stream gage showed a peak rise of 1.1 feet at 8:55 PM on September 4th, followed by a second peak rise of 0.8 feet at 2:55 AM on September 5th.  The pictures indicated higher flows of water mixed with debris and fire ash from its source in the Dragon Bravo Burn Scar area.

A spotter in Fort Valley Estates (on the northwest edge of Flagstaff) reported 3 inches of rain in 20 minutes. Rio de Flag and other streams were starting to flow.
A spotter reported seeing a funnel cloud for 5 to 10 minutes with a clockwise rotation in the base of the clouds.

A thunderstorm produced heavy rain that caused a landslide in Oak Creak Canyon.  A spotter near the area reported an inch and a half of rain. Road crews were dispatched to clear rocks and dirt from Highway 89A at mile post 378 a few miles north of Sedona.  This area is where the Brins Fire was in June 2006.
A USGS stream gauge in Jacks Canyon (JCCA3) measured a 5.4 foot rise from widespread rainfall of 0.75 to 1.25 inches upstream.  Peak flow was 699 cfs.
A USGS stream gauge on the East Verde River (EVDA3) reported over a 2 foot rise in 90 minutes.  That's an increase in flow from 12 to 630 cfs.
The West Clear Creek stream gauge near Camp Verde (WCLA3) recorded a rapid 6.5 ft rise.  That's an increase in flow from 48 to 6039 cfs.
Public reported, with a video on social media showing flash flooding from swiftly flowing water and debris on West Clear Creek. This made East Verde Lakes Drive impassable beginning at 5pm.

The Wet Beaver Creek  stream gauge near Rimrock (WBVA3) showed a rapid rise from 2.89 feet at 3 pm to peak in the Moderate Flood Stage category at 11.11 feet at 3:30 pm.  This is a rise in flow from 12 to 5068 cfs.
Flagstaff police department reported northbound Milton Road closed due to flooding at the railroad underpass near Phoenix Ave.
A USGS stream gauge on Wet Beaver Creek near Rimrock (WBVA3) recored a 4.2 foot rise from 5 am to 7 am Saturday morning.  That's an increase in flow from 387 to 2992 cfs.
Law Enforcement reported 2 hikers injured from a lightning strike on Humphreys Peak.  Time of event estimated on radar.
A USGS stream gauge on West Clear Creek near Camp Verde (WCLA3) recorded a 3.6 foot rise from widespread heavy rainfall across the basin.  That's an increase in flow from 509 to 4154 cfs.

A USGS stream gage on the Moenkopi Wash (MOEA3) measured an 8 foot rise in 3 hours, from 18.69 to 26.74 ft.  This would put the Moenkopi Wash into moderate flood stage.  The flow increased from 13 to 2860 cfs in that time period.  The Moenkopi Wash would further rise into major flood stage, cresting at a stage of 28.81 ft and 4867 cfs between 6:45 pm and 7:30 pm before beginning to recede.

Heavy rainfall of 2 to 3 fell over the area.  Time was estimated using the Roosevelt Dam SRP station (SRP44) site.

Law enforcement reported a car with 2 men trapped in floodwaters in Big Bug Creek at Cordes Lakes.  One man was rescued while the other was swept away.  The vehicle was later found lodged against a tree about 2 miles from the point of entry into the water. The second occupant was found deceased two days later at the confluence of Big Bug Creek with the Agua Fria River, about 6 miles from where he and his vehicle were last seen.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms over the Cataract Creek and Havasu Creek drainages caused flash flooding that started in the Village of Supai around 11:30 PM on August 16. Radar estimated between 3 and 4 inches of rain over several square miles in the Cataract Creek drainage during the afternoon.  Additional heavy rain from thunderstorms on August 17 continued heavy run off into the canyon. Cataract Canyon/Creek becomes Havasu Canyon/Creek at Havasu Springs about a mile upstream from the Village of Supai. This very popular destination for tourists was closed for at least 6 months because of the heavy damage caused by the flash flooding.

Snow began falling over the area during the afternoon of December 15th. By the morning of December 18th,  there was about two feet of new snow on the ground at the 7000 foot level. The snow caused many traffic accidents, power outages, and business/school closures and/or delayed  openings. The City of Flagstaff Police responded to 80 slideoffs, 61 non-injury collisions, and nine injury collisions during this event. Coconino County sheriff deputies responded to 35 slideoffs and 10 non-injury collisions.  Between Williams and Flagstaff, 10 to 13 inches of snow had fallen by the evening of December 16th.  A spotter at near 9000 feet had a storm total of 38 inches. Munds Park had 14 inches of snow by 8 AM on the 16th with snow still falling.
Five to six inches of snow fell.  Highway 264 was icy.
Five to six inches of snow fell in Christopher Creek and Kohls Ranch.
Fifteen inches of snow fell overnight in Pinetop.
Twelve inches of snow fell with this storm in Show Low and Forest Lakes. The snow was also drifting in places.

Nine to ten inches of new snow fell in Flagstaff from the afternoon of December 22 to the morning of the 23rd.  Eight to ten inches of fell in Williams and Parks. Six inches fell at Sunset Crater visitors center. Snow and blowing snow closed a 15 mile section (mile post 235 to 250) of Highway 180 near Kendrick Park north of Flagstaff on the way to the Grand Canyon.  The Flagstaff Police department responded to 49 vehicle collisions and 30 motorist assists.
Twelve inches of snow fell in the Chuska Mountains near Ft Defiance above 7000 feet and four inches of snow fell below 7000 feet.

A winter storm produced high winds (40 MPH sustained with gusts to 60 MPH), blowing and drifting snow, and very low visibility.  Drifting snow blocked roads. The high wind caused short power outages and electrical sparks/flashes from power lines. Snow and rain from this storm combined with snow and rain already accumulated from other December storms caused the roofs to collapse on at least five businesses in Flagstaff. Many car port awnings in apartment complexes also collapsed under the weight of the snow and rain. Williams and Flagstaff received 6 inches of new snow. Parks reported 7 inches of snow and drifting snow.

A spotter 4.5 miles west of Ash Fork reported 12 inches of new snow by noon on December 16th. It was still snowing hard.
Heavy snow fell even for lower elevations such as Page at about 4300 feet elevation.  Page received about 2.3 inches of snow in less than 12 hours.

Over a foot of new snow fell at the South Rim of the Grand Canyon in 24 hours. Observers reported 12 to 15 inches of snow in 24 hours and 4 to 5 inches of snow between 10 PM on the 17 to 6 AM on the 18th.  Highway 64 was closed from the Grand Canyon Village to Desert View on the morning of December 18th. The storm knocked out power in Indian Gardens for almost two days.
A foot of snow fell in Valle during this storm.
Eighteen inches of snow fell in Jacob Lake during this storm.
At least 6 inches of snow fell in the Pine-Strawberry area on the 16 of December.  Highway 87 was closed until the snow and ice could be cleared.

Heavy rain in the lower elevations of Gila County caused Tonto Creek to be come impassable. Residents were stranded on one side of the creek for several days. Between 400 and 600 people live on one side of the creek and often become stranded when the all three crossings become flooded.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN COCONINO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: A winter storm brought high winds to the Little Colorado River in Coconino.  The ASOS at the Winslow Airport less than 5 miles across the Coconino County line had a peak wind gust of 58 MPH.
A weather spotter in Munds Park reported 14 inches of snow from early Sunday (1/3) to Monday evening (1/5).
Nine to twelve inches of snow was reported from Show Low to Pine Top.  Up to eighteen inches of snow fell above 9000 feet elevation.
Three to five inches of snow fell in the Window Rock area.  Nine inches of snow fell four miles southeast of Sanders.

A Pacific winter storm created hazardous driving conditions on I-40 between Flagstaff and Williams.  The freeway was closed while crews cleared a semi trailer that had rolled over.  Two other semis rolled over in the same area. There were a total of 10 collisions and 12 cars that slid off the road. Travel was also difficult on I-17, Highway 89, and Highway 180 around Flagstaff. There were 5 non-injury accidents and two injury accidents within the Flagstaff City limits.  There were 6 non-injury and 1 injury accidents reported by Coconino County law enforcement.

Snow started falling around midnight and continued through the day with 8 to 12 inches of snow in the Pine and Strawberry area. Eight to nine inches of snow fell in Tonto Village. There were three rollover collisions on State Route 87 because of the storm and there was one fatality.
Eight to twelve inches of snow fell between Clints Well and Strawberry. Forest Lakes received 8 inches of new snow.

Eleven inches of snow fell at the Flagstaff Airport.  Eight inches of snow snow fell in Bellemont. Six inches of snow fell in Munds Park. There were several traffic accidents on I-17 and Highway 89 around Flagstaff. Two people from those accidents were transported to the hospital for treatment.  There were also 10 reported traffic accidents reported in the City of Flagstaff.
A foot of snow fell in Chinle and 10 inches fell in Canyon de Chelly.
Heavy snow temporarily stranded some people before the roads were cleared. Twenty inches of snow fell in Forest Lakes.
Six to 10 inches of snow fell in Window Rock.

Six inches of snow fell in Payson and Star Valley. Fifteen inches of snow fell in Tonto Village.  Highways 87, 260, and 60 were closed because road crews could not keep up with the heavy snow. Schools were closed and trash pick up was canceled. A dozen garbage trucks were used to plow roads instead. School buses couldn't even get out of the parking area on the morning of February 10th.
Eight inches of snow fell by 800 PM in Forest Lakes.

Heavy snow fell across the Western Mogollon Rim. Doney Park received 16 inches, Munds Park 15 inches, Flagstaff 14 inches, Bellemont 13 inches, and Williams 12 inches. Over 50 accidents were reported in the Flagstaff and Coconino County areas with at least nine injuries. There was a 5 mile traffic back upon I-17 south of Flagstaff.

Five and a half inches of snow fell in Prescott by early evening.  Ten inches of snow fell in Hidden Valley south of Prescott. Power and cable lines were broken in the Prescott area leaving as many as 2,500 customers in the dark for hours.

Heavy snow fell across the Western Mogollon Rim. Doney Park received 16 inches, Munds Park 15 inches, Flagstaff 14 inches, Bellemont 13 inches, and Williams 12 inches. Over 50 accidents were reported in the Flagstaff and Coconino County areas with at least nine injuries. There was a 5 mile traffic back upon I-17 south of Flagstaff.
A winter storm caused a 12 mile traffic back up on westbound I-40 near Seligman.

A winter storm dropped 4 inches of snow in Sedona causing school closures and traffic accidents. One roll over accident injured a man and he went to the hospital. A tree along Highway 89A fell and blocked the highway for a short time.
Six inches of snow fell in Payson and Star Valley.

A wind gust to 71 MPH were recorded in Seligman on the southern border of the zone. The Fraziers Well RAWS recorded wind gusts to 58 MPH.

An anemometer on the edge of Meteor Crater recorded a peak wind gust of 91 MPH. The edge of the crater often has much stronger winds than the surrounding area due to the topography of the crater. The visibility down to one mile in blowing dust was common across the Chinle Valley. The visibility dropped down to as low as 4 feet in the community of Many Farms early in the day (840 AM).  Drivers were waiting for the dust to clear along side roads.

A restaurant sign blew off its pedestal in Window Rock, crushed an SUV,  and injured a couple who had stopped for lunch. One person, in critical condition,  was taken to a local health service center then transported to Phoenix once the winds died down and it was safe to fly.

events.event_narrative: High winds (59 MPH and 60 MPH) were reported in both Tuba City and at Two Guns.
A peak wind gust of 67 MPH was reported at the Mogollon Rim Airpark in Overgaard.
The AWOS at the Show Low airport reported a peak wind gust of 63 MPH.
Tourists visiting the Petrified Forest National Park saw a tornado over the central portion of the park.
A tornado was reported by the public around Doney Park about 15 miles northeast of Flagstaff.
Possible tornado reported by Coconino Sheriffs Office.

Heavy rain caused significant flash flooding in and around the city of Page.  Several roads were temporarily closed with street flooding in much of the city. One normally dry wash had flowing water 5 feet deep. Copper Road and Highway 98 were impassible for a period of time. Mud and debris were flowing across roads. The greatest amount of rain reported was 3.27 inches from an automated rain gage.  The Page Airport ASOS reported 2.01 inches of rain in 24 hours.

Lightning started the Point Fire at around 3 PM on May 31st about 3 miles northeast of Pine, Arizona on the Mogollon Rim.  The fire was managed for resource benefits and was allowed to burn to a final size of 1300 acres by the time it was contained on June 23rd.

Lightning started the Point Fire at around 3 PM on May 31st about 3 miles northeast of Pine, Arizona on the Mogollon Rim.  The fire was managed for resource benefits and was allowed to burn to a final size of 1300 acres by the time it was contained on June 23rd.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding along portions of Route 59 about 6 miles northwest of Rough Rock.
Flash flooding from heavy rain covered parts of Highway 99 between 6 and 11 miles south of Leupp.

Heavy rain from a thunderstorm fell over the Cottonwood area.  Rainfall rates exceeded 2.00 inches an hour in some reports. Street flooding was reported all over town by the Cottonwood Police Department.
Dime sized (3/4 inch diameter) hail was reported in south Cottonwood with very heavy rain.
A trained spotter reported nickel sized hail.
Nickle sized hail was reported on the north side of Prescott.
Three quarter inch diameter hail was reported in Cottonwood.
The lightning cause Pioneer fire burned over 1,300 acres on the eastern side of the Pinal Mountains about 8 miles south of Globe. Total suppression cost was three million dollars.

The lightning caused Pioneer Fire burned about 1,300 acres on the eastern side of the Pinal Mountains (East Mountain) about 8 miles south of Globe. The total cost for suppression was three million dollars.
The Ruby was started by lightning on May 25 about six miles southeast of Tusayan on the Kaibab National Forest.  The fires merged and became the Ruby Complex.
The Game Reserve fire was started by on May 29 about nine miles southeast of the Grand Canyon Village in the Grand Canyon National Park.
The Ruby Complex continued to burn with low intensity within the management area for much of the month of June. The Complex burned more than 4,600 acres.
Heavy rain caused widespread street flooding in Prescott Valley.  Water reached the front doorstep of one house.

A strong thunderstorm produced as much as 1.30 inches of rain in just 50 minutes across Globe which resulted in minior flooding. Pea size hail was also reported at the time of the heavy rainfall. One spotter in Miami reported a wall of water coming towards him shortly after 7 PM.
A thunderstorm over Globe produced wind gusts to 57 MPH on the north side of town.
Very heavy rain caused landslides on the hills around Globe and Miami. The official observer in Globe had 0.97 inches in less than an hour.
Spotters reported flash flooding and land slides in and around the Globe-Miami area.
Lightning stuck one house and also knocked out power to street lights.
A thunderstorm produced nickel to quarter sized (0.88 to 1.00 inch diameter) hail in Overgaard.
A spotter in Heber-Overgaard reported one inch of rain in just 30 minutes with dime to nickel sized hail. There was standing water in his yard.
A thunderstorm over Lake Powell produced wind gusts to 54 MPH and waves up to 7 feet high.  One houseboat and 13 other boats were swamped.  Four law enforcement boats responded to 16 distress calls.
The Winslow ASOS reported a 50 knot wind gust with a thunderstorm.  Police in Winslow reported strong winds from 120 PM MST through at least 138 PM MST.
A plot reported a funnel cloud over Black Canyon City.
Four feet of water covered the road at the intersection of Copper Basin and Peavine Roads.  Water was up to the rail road tracks.
A spotter and public reported quarter sized (one inch diameter) hail in Skull Valley hail.
Lightning started the Wildhorse Fire about 16 miles north of Williams.  It burned about 1,149 acres by the end of July.  It then became part of the Wildhorse Complex with the Red Fire.
Lightning started the Red Fire about one mile south of Red Mountain.  It burned about 130 acres before it became part of the Wildhorse Complex.
The Wildhorse Complex started as two fires (Wildhorse and Red) on July 21,  2009.  This natural fire was managed for resource benefits.  The fire was contained on August 27th at 13,790 acres.
Streets in a small area of Miami were closed early on Thursday morning due to the runoff from heavy rains late Wednesday.

Power outage on Wednesday evening at the Frazier substation was due to very strong winds. Spotter reports included debrs blowing around due to the strong wind. Heavy rain was also reported, with .98 inch in 45 minutes at Roosevelt Dam.
The winds from a thunderstorm gusted to 64 MPH at the St Johns ASOS.
Heavy rain fell over Sedona and flooded a portion of Highway 179 blocking traffic.
Heavy rain in Prescott caused street flooding.  Highway 69 and Emerald Trail were closed due to high water.

Heavy rain,  with rates up to 4 inches in an hour,  fell on the Red Rocks on the northwest side of Sedona.  With virtually no infiltration,  the water quickly flowed into normally dry channels and washes.  There were reports of numerous flooded homes, widespread street flooding, over flowing stream beds,  large boulders washed into streets, eroded paved roads, and cars moved and stacked by flood water.  A 4 foot wall of water swept through the Los Abrigados Resort parking lot and moved parked cars.  One normally dry gully filled with 6 feet of rushing water. Several people were rescued after their cars started floating in the rapidly raising water in parking lots. City officials estimated that clean on public roads and drainage would cost  over $600,000.
Two to three feet of flowing water in a low water crossing trapped one car.  A swift water rescue was performed on the driver.
Heavy rain and flowing washes were reported by a spotter 3 miles southwest of Cottonwood.
A trained spotter one mile north of Winslow reported heavy rain,  flooded fields, and water entering the first floor of her house.
An off duty NWS employee and members of the general public reported possible funnel cloud over Flagstaff.

A strong cold front produced strong winds across northern Arizona.  Limestone Canyon, Tuba City,  Show Low, and Winslow all reported wind gusts in the lower 50 MPH range.  Window Rock reported a peak wind gust of 58 MPH.
Thunderstorms produced up to 2.50 inches of rain in just over two hours.  The heavy rain clogged a drainage ditch, flooded a yard, and flowed into a basement.
Thunderstorms also produced hail from pea to not quite dime/nickel sized (1/4 to  under 7/8 inch diameter).  The hail covered the ground and was piled two inches deep on a deck.

events.event_narrative: The Arizona Department of Transportation weather station at Two Guns recorded sustained winds of 40 MPH or higher from 11 AM through 5 PM.  The highest sustained wind was 46 MPH around 5 PM.  The highest measured wind gust was 65 MPH.

A strong cold front produced strong winds across the Eastern Mogollon Rim.  The Show Low ASOS recorded sustained winds around 40 MPH from late morning to mid afternoon.  The peak wind gust was 58 MPH.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: A strong cold front brought strong winds to the Little Colorado River Valley around Winslow.  The Winslow ASOS recorded sustained winds around 40 MPH with a peak wind gust of 59 MPH from around noon to mid afternoon.

High winds knocked down tree limbs and power lines in Prescott,  Groom Creek, and Walker.  As many as 6,300 customers lost power 5 to 6 times.  The downed power lines also caused a several small grass fires. Cable and phone lines were also knocked out.

The Twin Fire began as a prescribed burn that jumped containment lines.  The fire was moving towards the town of William where 64 homes were evacuated.  The fire threatened over 100 homes and businesses.  Smoke from the fire impacted travel on I40 by lowering the visibility. The fire reached a final size of just over 900 acres. Resources assigned to the Twin Fire included: a Type I Incident Management Team, 7 helicopters, several air tankers, 6 Hot Shot Crews, 4 Hand Crews, 33 engines, 2 dozers and 7 water tenders.  In all, over 450 personnel were assigned to the fire.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: A strong cold front produced strong winds across northern Arizona.  Limestone Canyon, Tuba City,  and Show Low all reported wind gusts in the lower 50 MPH range.  The Winslow ASOS reported sustained 40 MPH winds.

A departing low pressure center brought snow showers and cold conditions to the Flagstaff area during the afternoon and early evening.  These conditions lead to icy roads and few dozen car wrecks. The Department of Public Safety reported 11 collisions,  Coconino County Sheriff's Office reported 7 traffic accidents with injuries, and the Flagstaff Police Department reported 14 traffic accidents.  A parked DPS patrol car was hit and totaled by a truck that slid on the ice on I-40 just west of Flagstaff. The officer was out of his vehicle investigating a single vehicle roll over and was not hurt.

The early stages of an approaching winter storm caused a bridge to ice up on I-17 near Munds Park.  A Department of Public Safety officer was stopped to investigate a single van roll over.  The van had been traveling northbound, slid on the ice,  and crossed over the median into the southbound lane.  A northbound semi slid on the bridge,  crossed the median, and stuck the officer and the van.  The officer was pinned under a third vehicle that had stopped to avoid being hit by the semi.  People from other stopped vehicles were able to lift the vehicle off the officer,  free him, and call for help.  He was taken to a local hospital where he was listed in critical but stable condition.

Four motorcyclist stopped on the shoulder of a roadway because of the heavy rain.  One of them hid in a near by culvert.  While stopped,  lightning hit the ground near the three cyclists knocking them on the ground.  All three were air lifted to hospitals.  The woman had badly burned feet.  One man was very disoriented.  The third man was unconscious.  The current had entered his feet and exited his head in three places.  He died two days later in the hospital.
A weather spotter reported 2.20 inches of rain in 20 hours in Sedona.  Heavy rain in Prescott caused flooding and $15,000 damage to Skyview School in Prescott.
A weather spotter in Bagdad reported 3.88 inches of rain in 24 hours.

Very strong winds knocked over a 70 tall-two foot thick-ponderosa pine tree about 20 miles east of Camp Verde.  The tree fell on a man sleeping in a tent.  The man was struck in the head and died instantly.  A friend in the tent was not injured.  Measured wind speeds include:  Prescott Love Field: 74 MPH, Crown King (Horsethief Basin RAWS) : 69 MPH,  and Mingus Mountain 70 MPH.  About 5000 homes lost powers during the storm.  At least 60 large trees fell throughout Prescott.  Thirty trees had to be cut and removed from roadways.  At least six trees fell on homes. Other trees fell on parked cars. Many homes and businesses reported roof damage or destruction.

Spotters and Mesonet sites across the lower elevations of Yavapai County reported very strong winds as the cold front moved through.  Some of the highest wind gusts include:  Chino Valley 78 MPH (screen door torn from house in Chino Valley),  66 MPH in Camp Verde, Crown King and Sunset Point 77 MPH.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN COCONINO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: A Highway Observing site at Two Guns reported peak wind gusts of 69 MPH.
Wind gusts to 60 MPH were measured in the Heber-Overgaard area.  The Mogollon Airpark reported a peak wind gust of 70 MPH.

Blizzard conditions developed as the cold front moved through Bellemont.  The winds were sustained up to 50 MPH with gusts to 70 MPH with zero visibility in snow and blowing snow. Over 20 inches of snow had fallen in the 20 hours before the front arrived and was piked up by the strong winds.  There were power outages in Flagstaff.  Trees and tree branches were knocked down by the winds.  I-40 was shut down from Ash Fork to Winslow.  The Flagstaff Airport had a peak wind gust of 53 MPH and Doney Park 65 MPH.

Heavy snow fell across the Western Mogollon Rim.  One neighborhood in southwest Flagstaff reported 26 inches of snow with other locations in town came in with 20 inches.  Parks received 19 to 24 inches, Munds Park 18 to 24,  Williams 20 inches,  and the Arizona Snowbowl 21 to 32 inches (9200 and 10,800 feet elevation). I-17 was closed several times about 40 miles south of Flagstaff when vehicles wrecked because of the snow.  There were at least 52 calls to the Department of Public Safety for slide offs, 18 collisions, and 8 injuries.  Flagstaff Police Department responded to at least 42 collisions in the city with two minor injuries.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The ASOS at the Winslow Airport reported a peak wind gust of 69 MPH.
Northern Gila County received up to 18 inches of snow with this storm.  A man froze to death about a mile and a half from his truck north of Young.
Seven inches of snow fell in Seligman.  Six to fifteen inches of snow fell in the Ash Fork area.
Ten inches of snow fell in Keams Canyon.

events.cz_name: NORTHEAST PLATEAUS AND MESAS FROM HIGHWAY 264 NORTH
events.event_narrative: Eighteen inches of snow fell in Pinyon.
Two feet of new snow was reported with this storm.
Eighteen inches of snow fell at the South Rim of the Grand Canyon.

The Eastern Mogollon Rim received significant snowfall:  Clay Springs 12 to 13 inches, Forest Lakes 24 inches, and Heber 8 inches. Forest Lakes had 55 MPH wind gusts at 200 AM with downed power lines and trees.  As many as 50 hunters were trapped in the woods due to the deep snow.  Some of the hunters needed assistance while others were able to wait out the storm.
Snow reports from the White Mountains include: Show Low 6 inches,  McNary 16 inches,  and Pinetop 10 inches.
Payson received 6 inches of new snow.

Strong winds caused extensive damage to the roof and porch of the Humane Society of Central Arizona in Payson early morning on December 8th as a strong cold front passed.  The winds peeled the tin roof back, tore off shingles,  and blew off two swamp coolers.
Jacob Lake received 15 to 16 inches of snow.  The North Rim Village reported 12 inches of snow.

A spotter 4 miles south of Williams reported 9 inches of new snow.   Munds Park received 9 inches of new snow. Parks received 10 to 12 inches of new snow while a spotter 12 miles north of Parks reported 21 inches of new snow. Up to 10 inches of snow fell in Flagstaff.
Grand Canyon Dispatch reported 6 to 8 inches of snow.
Clints Well received 8 inches of new snow.  Heber received 6 to 7 inches of snow with blowing and driving snow.  Highway 260 westbound was closed for a time due to icy conditions.
It is extremely likely (due to sound meteorological reasoning) that the Coconino Plateau exceeded its criteria for heavy snow.  George Howard, WCM.
Heavy snow fell along the Eastern Mogollon Rim.  Snowfall totals for this one storm include:  Clints Well 16 inches,  Heber 13 inches,  Clay Springs 14 to 15 inches, and Forest Lakes 16 inches.

Heavy snowfall spread across the White Mountains overnight and into the morning hours.   Some of the snowfall reports include:  Lakeside 8 to 12 inches,  Sunrise Mountain 10 inches and Alpine 9 inches.
Heavy snow and strong winds were felt across northern Gila County.  The snow level remained above 5000 feet.  Tonto Village received 6 inches of snow. Power went out in the town of Pine.
Heavy rain and melting snow caused flooding along Tonto Creek in Gisela south to Tonto Basin. The heavy rain caused a mud slide that temporarily closed Highway 87.

Heavy rain and melting snow caused major flooding in Black Canyon City.  Evacuations orders were issued for communities along the Agua Fria River and Black Canyon Creek.  One trailer park had damage to all 50 trailers.

A strong winter storm produced 4.01 inches of precipitation in 24 hours. Rainfall over a three day period ranged from 6 to 10 inches across Gila Country.

Other locations closer to the edge of the Mogollon Rim received close to 60 inches of snow.  Elevations above 8000 feet had all snow...between 40 and 80 inches (at 10,800 feet).  At least four businesses had their roofs collapse due to the weight of the snow and rain soaked snow. A very large tree blew down on two homes in Williams.
Between 36 and 48 inches of snow fell across the Eastern Mogollon Rim.  The roof of a fire station and a water office collapsed in Pinetop-Lakeside.
