The Eagle Rock Fire was started by lightning late afternoon on Friday June 11th near Eagle Rock on the east side of Sitgreaves Mountain on the Kaibab National Forest.  The fire made very little movement and the fire went undetected until Red Flag conditions were experienced on the fire June 15th.  Fifty residences in the area were evacuated when the winds fanned the fire. No homes were lost in this fire.  However, there were two out buildings that were destroyed. As many as 664 people were assigned to the fire during the peak activity.  Fire fighting efforts cost close to 4 million dollars.

The Hardy Fire started when a transient dumped ashes from a cooking fire onto the ground.  Strong winds pushed the fire toward the southern edge of Flagstaff and prompted the evacuation of homes, businesses, hotels, and an animal shelter in the area.  At least 120 personnel were assigned to the fire with at least two heavy air tankers and three heavy lift helicopters.

The Schultz Fire was started by an abandon campfire.  Wind enhanced by topography and steep slopes on the eastern side of the San Francisco Peaks (also known as Kachina Peaks) greatly enhanced the spread and severity of the fire. Highway 89 was closed because of the fire. A Type I Incident Management Team was called to organize fire fighting efforts. Close to one thousand people were called out to fight this fire. Fire fighting equipment included  8 air tankers, 7 helicopters, 62 fire engines, and 13 water tenders.  Firefighting efforts alone cost around $10 million dollars.  No homes or buildings were damaged by fire.  However,  flooding and debris flows that resulted from the fire damaged landscape caused damage to close to 100 properties and homes once the rainy season started in July and lasted through August.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm triggered a mudslide eight miles west of Kohls Ranch.  Mud crossed Highway 260 at mile post 264.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm caused several rock slides on Highway 60 in southern Navajo County.
A weather spotter in Flagstaff reported 1.41 inches of rain in 45 minutes.  Small hail covered the ground 3/4 inch deep.
Torrential rain was reported just outside of Heber-Overgaard.  Water was ponding on area roads and parking lots.  An estimated three inches of rain fell.

Heavy rain from a thunderstorm over the northern portion of the Schultz Fire burn area caused flash flooding and debris flows.  Mud, silt, and debris between 4 inches and 18 inches deep flowed across roads and private property in the Timberline and Hutchinson Acres neighborhoods northeast of Flagstaff.
Hail covered the ground with hail stones as large as quarters.  Two inches of rain followed the hail.
A thunderstorm produced 3/4 inch diameter hail and heavy rain.  There was minor street flooding.  No damage was reported.

Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire burn area caused extensive flash flooding on both sides of Highway 89 northeast of Flagstaff.  A 12 year old girl was swept away in the flood waters and drowned.  Two rain gauges within the burn area reported 1.48 and 1.78 inches of rain  in 52 minutes and 62 minutes respectively.  The flood waters, ash, mud, debris, and rocks 2-3 feet in diameter covered roads,  properties,  and entered homes.  Highway 89 was closed as were the main roads west of Highway 89.  The water slowed down once it crossed Highway 89.  However,  the heavy silt prevented the water from percolating into the cinders east of Highway 89. The flood waters flowed across the road leading to the Flagstaff City Dump and eventually into a few dozen homes south of the dump. In all, as many as 85 homes were damaged by the flooding.

Heavy rain from a thunderstorm caused another round of flash flooding, mud and debris flows, closed roads,  and more damage to homes. Water flowed over Highway 89, Land Fill Road, and entered homes on the east side of Highway 89.  Some homes had  two to three feet of water inside.
A thunderstorm produced hail from 1/2 to 1 inch in diameter.
A thunderstorm produced 2.45 inches of rain in just 45 minutes.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm caused flooding over Indian Route 12 near Cibecue.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm caused flash flooding across Highway 191 between mile post 389 and 391.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused flash flooding across Navajo Route 60 from milepost 1 to 13.5 and on Navajo Route 87 around milepost 367.

Several thunderstorms pounded areas of Flagstaff with torrential rain.  One spotter measured an inch of rain in just 15 minutes.  The most rain reported by a spotter was 2.75 inches.  A public report came in with over twice that amount.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm produced flash flooding in the community of Polacca and Highway 264 between milepost 390 and 393.
Another round of flash flooding impacted the Schultz Fire burn area eastward into Doney Park.
Heavy rain, 0.93 inches in 29 minutes, hit western portions of Prescott.  Roads were covered with water and the creeks were running full.

A thunderstorm produced heavy rain over portions of the Schultz Fire burn area.  This produced minor water flows across at least two roads and two properties. Otherwise, the water was staying in the wash banks.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms flooded area roads in Linden.  A trained weather spotter recorded 2.50 inches of rain.

A thunderstorm produced heavy rain in Prescott.  A spotter reported 1.01 inches of rain in 45 minutes.  Another spotter reported 0.90 inches of rain in just 20 minutes.  Small streams overflowed their banks.
A spotter reported 1.65 inches of rain in one hour.
Weather spotters in Payson reported between 2.20 and 2.30 inches of rain.  Heavy street flooding was reported with some structures threatened by over a foot of runoff.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused flash flooding in Antelope Canyon. People were stranded on ledges in this slot canyon when a four and a half foot wall of water came rushing through the canyon.  Five members of a 12 member Swiss tourist group were injured. A woman and her 9 year old son sustained scrapes and busies as they were washed downstream. Three men were also injured.  A second wall of water came rushing through the canyon after the people were rescued.

Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire burn caused more flash flooding.  Washes were running full and over topping roads.  Several local roads were closed.  Highway 89 was closed for 20 minutes due to the flooding.
A funnel cloud was sighted about 10 miles east of Holbrook.  The funnel descended and ascended twice.
All major roads in Holbrook were flooded.
One inch of rain fell at Green Base Lookout Tower in 20 minutes.  The storm total was 1.10 inches.

Heavy rain fell across large areas of west, central, and east Flagstaff.  Rainfall rates were close to 3 inches per hour.  One spotter reported 1.40 inches of rain in the first 30 minutes.  Roads around town became impassible.  Five cars were stalled in one intersection.  Several cars became stuck in an underpass with water up to the hoods.  One car started to float. It took two hours for pumps to drain the water in the underpass.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Sycamore Canyon.  Four people became stranded near a swimming hole and had to be rescued.
Two normally dry washes  flooded.  One quarter of a mile of the roadway was covered in water.
Three and a half inches of rain fell overnight four mile south of Williams.  Most of that (2.90 inches) fell from 500 AM to 700 AM.
Over one and half inches (1.60) of rain fall overnight. Most of that fell from 645 AM to 838 AM.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Cataract Creek.  The water level went from a dry stream bed to 4 to 5 feet deep in just 15 minutes.
A mudslide slid across Highway 191 at milepost 416 near Nutrioso.
Several roads were flooded in and around Taylor.  Part of Airport Road washed out near Highway 77.

Heavy rain produced flooding in and around Concho. Two feet of water covered County Road 5020 at mile marker 15.  Water flowed over Highway 61 at milepost 375 three miles east of Concho.  Forest Service Roads became impassable.
Water flowed over Highway 12 and stopped traffic north of Lupton near Oak Springs.
Flowing water from Wide Ruin Wash stopped traffic as it flowed over Highway 191.
Heavy rain produced flooding in the Vernon area.  County Road 3144 had water flowing over the top.

A family of four partially crossed the bed of the Agua Fria River in a truck (SUV) when flash flooding occurred.  They became stuck in the flood waters. A swift water rescue was in possible and a helicopter could not be dispatched due to the weather conditions. The 6 year old boy was subsequently swept downstream and drown.
Heavy rain and flooding caused road closures along Highway 264 and Highway 87.
Heavy rain (2.60 inches in 3 hours) caused some damage to culverts in the area.
Navajo Police Department observed a funnel cloud west of Many Farms.
A land spout type tornado was confirmed via a photograph.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding in and around the Wheatfields area.  Roads were washed out in several areas and a bridge or two was washed out.  Portions of Canyon de Chelly were evacuated as a precaution.
Law enforcement officials reported flash flooding over Highway 160.
The tour company at Antelope Canyon reported flash flooding in the canyon after midnight.
The Bureau of Land Management reported flash flooding along House Rock Road--the road was river of water.  Coyote Wash flooded over House Rock Road.
Penny sized hail was reported in the Buckskin Gulch and Coyote Buttes areas.

Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire burn area caused flash flooding in the neighborhoods to the east. Several roads were flooded including Highway 89.  There was a large debris flow though Siesta Wash making roads impassable.  Berms that were made to redirect flood waters east of Highway 89 were temporarily breached.
A river gage on Havasu Creek showed a three foot rise.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding across Highway 97 at Skunk Creek (MP 158) and Boulder Creek (MP 163).
Heavy rain and flooding made Route 4 impassable due to high water between mile marker 40 and 43.
The Wepo Wash flooded near Pinon.
An observer in Bagdad reported 1.45 inches of rain in 45 minutes.
Damaging thunderstorm winds hit the Petrified Forest National Park.  Stop signs were blown down and small trees were snapped.  A wind sensor measured a peak wind gust of 107 MPH.
Winds from a thunderstorm knocked down large trees in Bagdad.
A thunderstorm produced 2.20 inches of rain at Hart Prairie Lodge at Arizona Snowbowl. Small hail accumulated to a dept of one inch.
Water flowed over Snowbowl Road near the ski lodge.  No significant damage was reported.
Heavy rain in and around Woodruff caused area washed to run high.  The main road through Woodruff was closed due to running water.
Heavy rain fell across central Navajo Country.  Rainfall amounts include: 1.75 inches (15 miles south of Holbrook), 1.50 inches (north of Joseph City), and 0.93 inches (north of Snowflake).
Heavy rain fell across Gila County.  A spotter a mile east of Payson reported 1.20 inches of rain overnight.

Supai Police reported a two foot wall of water moving down Hualapai Canyon toward the Village of Supai. The Suapi USGS river gage reported a peak flow of about 600 CFS at around 500 PM.   Flash flooding was reported in the campground at around 320 PM. This flood water may have been from side canyons and from Havasu Creek. Campers, 143 in all, in the campground were air lifted to safety. Three tribal pack animals were killed by the flash flood. The canyon was closed to tourists indefinitely due to the damages caused to the trail and campground. The President of the United States declared the Havasupai Canyon a major disaster area and ordered Federal aid to supplement State, Tribal, and local recovery efforts. The estimated cost to replace and repair the damaged or destroyed infrastructure is $1,630,000.
Dime sized hail fell for ten minutes before quarter-sized (1 inch in diameter) started to fall.  The hail dented cars and shattered plastic vents on RV trailers.
Penny sized hail accumulated to a depth of one inch.
A narrow strip of hail covered the pavement on Interstate 40 near mile post 180.  Two cars lost control and slid off the road.
Possible funnel clouds observed west of Hard Rocks.
Dime to nickel sized (3/4 to 7/8 inch diameter) hail fell near Bagdad.  Roads were also flooded in the area.
Quarter sized (1 inch in diameter) fell in Bagdad.  Minor street flooding was also reported.
Large hail fell near Payson. The majority of the hail was 1.25 inches in diameter with the largest stones were 2.25 inches in diameter.
Hail and strong winds were reported with a thunderstorm.  Nearby power lines were damaged.
Hail on the road caused a roll over near mile post 130 in Interstate 40.
A funnel cloud was reported west of I-17 by a motorist traveling on the interstate.
A thunderstorm produced hail across Cornville that ranged from quarter to golf ball sized (1 to 1.75 inches in diameter).

The US Forest Service and NWS reported significant tornado damage near Blue Ridge Ranger Station and NWS Radar site. Hundreds of ponderosa pines were blown over or snapped off along a 14.8 mile path. At least one alligator juniper that was 2 and a half feet in diameter was snapped off.  Trees were down across Highway 87 between mile markers 296 and 298.  NWS Storm Surveys and aerial surveys contributed to the event analysis.

Considerable structural damage in and around the community of Bellemont; significant forest damage and treefall in forest north and south of Bellemont. This tornado was from the same storm that produced Tornado #2.  Aerial and ground surveys verified a semi-continuous tornado path from 8 miles south of Bellemont, extending northward for 26 miles, crossing Interstate 40 and Highway 180 (three times- near mileposts 230, 234, and 240). Tornado passed 2/3 mile east of the NWS Bellemont Weather Forecast office. Damage from this tornado included:|-7 minor injuries.|-Over 100 homes damaged in Bellemont, 21 homes sustaining significant damage (deemed uninhabitable).|-At least one business (RV Sales) with damage with 30+ RV units demolished and tossed onto Interstate 40. Interstate closed for several hours.|-At least one overturned truck on the Interstate.|-Numerous forest roads blocked, campers stranded by fallen trees. |-Around 75 power poles knocked down.

This tornado caused extensive forest damage (primarily south of Bellemont), along a discontinuous track which extended from 15 miles south of Bellemont, eventually crossing Hwy 180 northwest of Flagstaff.  The path of this tornado was parallel to, and approximately 1 mile west of Tornado #2.  Very wide, severe and complete forest damage occurred in the forest south of Bellemont. Tornado visually sighted by NWS staff at the Bellemont Weather Forecast Office.||Tornado passed 1/3 mile west of the NWS Bellemont Weather Forecast office. Additional damage stats include:|-28 rail cars derailed in Bellemont.|-Semi trucks and trailers were overturned on I-40.|-Power poles and numerous trees snapped on Camp Navajo.  Some structures damaged.|-Numerous forest roads blocked and campers were stranded by fallen trees.

Garjon Tank Tornado (6:50 - 7:14 AM MST): This tornado caused extensive forest damage south of Bellemont, blocking several forest roads. Path of tornado was parallel to, and 1-2 miles west of the paths of Tornado #2 and Tornado #4.  There was some evidence of tornadic cycling with three individual tornadoes possible. Tornado passed 2 miles west of the National Weather Service Office as it dissipated.  Aerial surveys and imagery were also used in the analysis.
A 50-yard wide tornado was observed in grassland east of Interstate 17. Dissipated shortly afterward.

A tornado collapsed three 500 KV electrical transmission towers. The towers were of metal truss construction. One tower was completely flattened. Photographic evidence and first-hand reports were provided by Arizona Public Service. Tornado damage intensity is rated at EF-3. Damage path length indeterminable.
Munds Park / Cosnino tornado (12:05 - 12:20 PM): This tornado was seen crossing Interstate 17 moving northbound.
Golf ball sized (1.75 inches in diameter) fell in Parks.
Baseball sized (2.75 inch diameter) hail fell about 11 miles south of Bellemont.
One inch diameter hail fell in Cottonwood.
Large hail 1.75 inch in diameter fell around mile post 312 on Interstate 17 or about 11 miles south of Munds Park.
A thunderstorm produced 1.25 inch diameter hail.  The  trail at Lake Montezuma was closed due to the hail.
One inch diameter hail covered the ground in Munds Park.
One inch diameter hail fell about two miles south of Mountainaire with heavy rain.
One inch diameter hail fell in Kachina Village.
Two inch diameter hail fell in Corneville with minor damage to vehicles.
Golf ball sized (1.75 inches in diameter) knocked out several windshields on Highway 160 and in Four Corners National Monument.
Siding was blown off houses and into cars.  At least two trees were blown down.
A tornado was observed touching down between Cottonwood and Blue Gap.  Trees and bushes were knocked down.

Accumulating hail on Interstate 40 about 5 miles west of Williams caused at least 9 crashes. Three cars rolled over and six cars slid off the road.  One person was ejected from their car.  Two people had serious injuries and four people had minor injuries.  The Interstate was closed for about 70 minutes while the wrecks were cleared.
Two women were struck by lightning while standing on the South Rim of the Grand Canyon east of the Visitors Center.  Both women were taken to medical facilities, treated, and released.
Short path of significant tornado damage between two other tracks near the Mogollon Rim.  Aerial imagery was also used in the analysis.  Start and end times estimated from radar data.

Rain and snow started falling over the high country of the Western Mogollon Rim late in the evening on November 20th. Snow on roadways began impacting travel by daylight on November 21st. There were numerous vehicles that slid off roads and several vehicles rolled over because of the slippery conditions. The Flagstaff Airport received about 3 inches of snow.

Several days of low clouds, freezing temperatures, and steady winds produced large accumulations of rime ice on trees and radio towers above 8500 feet in the mountains around Flagstaff. Several hundred trees toppled at elevations of 9000 feet in the Kachina Peaks outside of Flagstaff.  Radio equipment atop Mt Elden near Flagstaff also sustained damage. Several radio stations were knocked off the air including the NWR. There were 49 traffic accidents due to snowy and ice roads.  There were 13 minor injuries. Eight inches of snow fell in Bellmont and 12 miles north of Parks and 6 inches fell at the Flagstaff Airport.

Heavy snow, strong winds, and blowing snow moved across the western Mogollon Rim from early morning on December 29th through much of the day on the 30th. Some snowfall totals include: 4 miles south of Williams 30 inches, 12 miles north of Parks 24 inches, Munds Park 19.5 inches, Bellmont 18.8 inches,  Williams 18 inches, Flagstaff Airport 17.2 inches, Kachina Village 16 inches, and 15 inches in north Fort Valley. Over 150 motorist needed emergency assistance in the Flagstaff area with roll overs, slide offs, and wrecks.  Both I-17 and Highway 89 south of Flagstaff were closed due to the dangerous conditions.
Heavy snow fell across the eastern Mogollon Rim.  Snowfall totals include (inches): Forest Lakes 30, Clints Well 18, Heber Overgaard 12, and Clay Springs 10.
Heavy snow fell across the White Mountains area December 29th through the 30th.  Total snowfall amounts include: Pinetop-Lakeside 16.5, and 3 miles southeast of Pinetop-Lakeside 14.

Heavy snow fell across northern Gila December 29th through the 30th.  Total snowfall amounts include: Pine and Christopher Creek both had 16, 18 miles east of Payson 12,  Star Valley 9, and Payson 6.5-7.3.  State Route 87 was closed just south of Payson while a multiple car collision block both north and south lanes of traffic.

Heavy snow fell across the mountains of Yavapai County December 29th through the 30th.  Total snowfall amounts include: Crown King 17, 5 miles northwest of Prescott 11.5,  1 mile west of Prescott 9, and 2 miles northwest of Prescott 8.  I-40 near Ash Fork had delays and was closed periodically during the storm.
Heavy snow fell across the Grand Canyon Area with 16 inches reported at the Grand Canyon Village.
Heavy snow fell across the Kaibab Plateau with 12 inches reported at Jacob Lake.
Heavy snow fell across Oak Creek Canyon and Sycamore Canyon with 11 inches reported in Oak Creek Canyon 7 miles north of Sedona.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Heavy snow fell across the Little Colorado River in Navajo County with 7 inches reported in the town of Snowflake and 6 inches 10 miles south of Holbrook.
High wind on the eastern side of the Kachina Peaks blew down a fence. An anemometer measured frequent wind gusts over 50 MPH with a peak gust of 60 MPH.
Very cold temperatures in the Prescott area caused pipes to freeze and burst in over 120 buildings. Local plumbing and restoration businesses received over 400 call just as the New Year started.
The Payson Roundup newspaper reported at least 48 cases of frozen water pipes in and around the Payson area.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Cold temperatures froze and broke a water valve in the Navajo County Complex.  Employees were sent home early as water flooded the areas around the buildings. Two water towers released approximately 400,000 gallons of water after the shut off valve broke.

Very cold temperatures caused water pipes to burnt in the South County Health Complex in Show Low.  The flooding that resulted caused the clouser of the complex for at least a week. The new buildings were still under warranty.

Clear skies, no surface winds, fresh snow, and an arctic air mass allowed the temperature to plummet on New Years Morning.  The temperature at the Flagstaff Airport dropped to -19F and down to -30F at the WFO in Bellemont. Frozen pipes and flooding impacted many buildings across the Western Mogollon Rim. Seven buildings on the Northern Arizona University campus, two Flagstaff Unified School District buildings, a crafts store, and 40 to 60 more homes and apartments were affected by burst pipes.  The two boilers and a generator were destroyed ($450,000 replacement cost) at Sinagua Middle School when pipes burst and flooded the boiler room with 5 feet of water.

The temperatures stayed well below freezing for over 36 hours with strong northeasterly winds.  The Flagstaff airport experienced the 7th coldest recorded high temperature (12F) and had a windchill of -23F.  The sensor at top of Arizona Snowbowl (11,500 feet) had a wind chill of -64F.  The Flagstaff Fire Department received over two dozen calls on the 3rd for frozen pipes, busted pipes, and flooding.  Several schools were closed and several buildings on the Northern Arizona University campus were closed when sprinkler pipes froze and broke.
Very cold conditions lead to freezing and burst pipes in the White Mountains.  About two dozen businesses,  schools, and homes had frozen pipes.

Heavy wet snow began to fall early Saturday morning February 19th.  By the time snow stopped falling Sunday afternoon between one and 3 and half feet of snow had piled up around the area. Some snowfall totals include(in inches) : Snowbowl 44, Flagstaff Airport 17.9, Bellemont (WFO) 15.3, 4 miles south of Williams 14.8,  Munds Park area 8 to 13, Kachina Village 12.4,  Parks 12, and Williams 11.  Northbound Interstate 17 was closed for a hour and a half south of Flagstaff. Highway 89 was closed between Sedona and Flagstaff and 12 mile stretch of Highway 180 north of Flagstaff was also closed due to snow and blowing snow.

Ten inches of snow fell 3 miles southwest of Prescott.  The City of Prescott reported 4.5 inches of snow. The weather contributed to a three vehicle wreck on Interstate 40 just west of Ash Fork. Several cars slid off Interstate 40 between mile marker 100 westward to the Coconino County line.
Nine inches of snow fell 14 miles northeast of Payson.
Almost nine (8.8) inches of snow fell at the Grand Canyon South Rim.
Twelve inches of snow fell in Clints Well and 10 inches of snow fell in Forest Lakes.
Eight inches of snow fell 3 miles southeast of Pinetop-Lakeside.
Seven inches of snow fell in Young at an elevation of 5200 feet.
Six to 9 inches of snow fell around central and west Flagstaff with only 3 to 5 inches in Doney Park.  Nine and a half inches of snow fell around Williams.
An average of 5 inches of snow fell in Fredonia at an elevation of 4700 feet.

Heavy snow fell to below 5000 feet (this zone boundary) all across Yavapai Country.  Seven to nine and a half inches of snow fell in and around Prescott and Prescott Valley. Six inches of snow fell 9 miles west of Ash Fort at an elevation of around 5300 feet. Twelve and a half inches of snow fell 7 miles south of Prescott. Eleven inches of snow fell in Ponderosa Park (about 5 miles south of Prescott).

Heavy snow fell across the lower elevations (below 5000 feet) of Yavapai County where heavy snow warning criteria is only 2 inches in 12 hours. Bagdad received 8 inches of snow at 3800 feet.  Paulden and 8 miles northeast of Camp Verde had 2 inches of snow. Cottonwood and Rimrock both had 3 inches of snow.  Three miles west of Dewy-Humboldt received 6.2 inches of snow. Three miles northwest of Dewy-Humboldt received 7 inches of snow. Seven miles northeast of Dewy-Humboldt received 10 inches of snow at 4525 feet elevation.

Heavy snow fell across the lower elevations (below 5000 feet) of Yavapai County where heavy snow warning criteria is only 2 inches in 12 hours. Bagdad received 8 inches of snow at 3800 feet.  Paulden and 8 miles northeast of Camp Verde had 2 inches of snow. Cottonwood and Rimrock both had 3 inches of snow.  Three miles west of Dewy-Humboldt received 6.2 inches of snow. Three miles northwest of Dewy-Humboldt received 7 inches of snow.
Two miles south of Sedona received 5 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN COCONINO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Wind gust exceeded 58 MPH at the ADOT anemometer near Two Guns along I-40 for about half an hour.  Wind gusts of over 40 MPH lasted for about 4 hours.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Wind gust exceeded 58 MPH for about 20 minutes at the Winslow Airport. Wind gusts exceeded 40 MPH for over 5 hours.  Blowing dust reduced the visibility below 2 miles during the strongest winds.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Strong and damaging winds were felt across Navajo County as a strong cold front moved from west t east across the area. Blowing dust also caused travel difficulties. Some of the strongest wind gusts reported were Petrified Forest National Park 66 MPH and Lupton 62 MPH.

Strong and damaging winds were felt across Navajo County as a strong cold front moved from west t east across the area. Blowing dust also caused travel difficulties. Some of the strongest wind gusts reported at Window Rock was 60 MPH.

Snow falling across the Western Mogollon Rim made travel on area roads hazardous.  Interstate 17 was closed from about 6 miles south of the Coconino/Yavapai to Flagstaff due to a multiple car pile up and Highway 89 was closed from Sedona to Flagstaff due to a snow plow crash. An SUV rolled about 6 miles west of Williams and a passenger died in the crash.  The Department of Public Safety responded to over 18 crashes and 20 slide offs.  Ten of the crashes involved injuries. The Flagstaff Airport received 7.4 inches of snow, in the town Flagstaff 8 to 9 inches of snow, 4 miles west-northwest of Flagstaff 12 niches, Kachina Village/Mountainaire 7.0 to 9.4 inches, 3 miles north of Parks 6.0 inches, Bellemont 6.9 inches, southwest side of Williams 10 inches, and Snowbowl 5 (at 9500 feet) to 10 inches (at 10,800 feet).
High winds were felt in Doney Park east of the San Fransisco Peaks along Highway 89.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN COCONINO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Wind gusts to 65 MPH were observed at the Leupp School and an ADOT sensor at Two Guns.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The ASOS at the Winslow Airport reported wind gusts to 62 MPH.

Snow began to fall in the Flagstaff area early morning (5AM) on April 8th. Snow became during the late morning and through the night. Snow in and around Flagstaff ranged between 10 and 13 inches. At 10800 feet, 28 inches of snow fell. Kachina Village picked up 9 inches and Doney Park had 4 inches.  Northbound Interstate 17 was closed about 40 miles south of Flagstaff.  There was a two fatality crash on Interstate 40 about 15 miles east of Flagstaff.  Police and the Department of Public Safety reported numerous other slid offs and collisions around the Flagstaff area. Most were non-injury.

Snow began to fall over the Grand Canyon Country around daybreak on April 8th. Much heavier snow fell during the afternoon and evening.  Twelve inches fell at the South Rim and 9 inches fell over the North Rim.
Snow reports around northern Gila County ranged form 3 inches in Payson to 7 inches in Pine.
Snowfall across the Eastern Mogollon Rim ranged from 6 inches in Forest Lakes to 7 inches in Clints Well.
Six to seven inches of snow fell around Show Low.
Snowfall reports ranged from 7-12 inches in the Seligman/Ash Fork area to 4-7 inches in the Prescott area.
Two to four inches of snow fell across Yavapai County between 3500 feet and 5000 feet. Snow is rarely this heavy at these lower elevations.
Nine to Twelve inches of snow fell over the Kaibab Plateau.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The Saint Johns Airport recorded a peak wind gust of 65 MPH with winds gusting over 58 MPH for over 3 hours.  Blowing dust was also observed.
The Mesonet wind sensor at Linden recorded wind gusts go 59 MPH.

Snow, blowing snow, and icy roads caused several accidents along Interstate 40 and Interstate 17 around Flagstaff.  There was a vehicle roll over on Lake Mary Road.  A SUV lost control on the snow and collided with a school bus that was carrying children. Seven inches of snow fell about 5 miles south of Williams at an elevation of 7200 feet.  Two to three inches of snow fell in and around Flagstaff.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN COCONINO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Blowing dust along Interstate 40 between Flagstaff and Winslow reduced the visibility to the point where the Department of Public Safety began escorting vehicles along a 5 mile stretch of the freeway.
The RAWS at House Rock reported wind gusts in excess of 60 MPH for several hours during the night.
The RAWS at Limestone Canyon reported high wind gusts from about noon to 9 PM MST.|A spotter in Linden reported a peak wind gust of 59 MPH.
The Show Low Airport reported high wind gusts for several hours during the evening.

A weather station in Doney Park measured wind gusts to 58 MPH or higher between 11:25 and 11:32 AM and again between 2:50 and 3:00 PM.  The peak wind gust was 60 MPH.  The peak wind gust at the Flagstaff Airport was 64 MPH.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The ASOS at Winslow measured wind gusts 58 MPH or higher for about half an hour.  The peak wind gust was 63 MPH.

The Window Rock ASOS reported wind gusts of 58 MPH or higher from about 1250 PM to 110 PM.  The peak wind gust was 60 MPH.  The ADOT wind sensor at Lupton reported wind gusts of 58 MPH or higher off and on from about 1:30 PM to 6:10 PM.  The peak wind gust was also 60 MPH.

events.cz_name: NORTHEAST PLATEAUS AND MESAS SOUTH OF HIGHWAY 264
events.event_narrative: The Petrified Forest National Park reported a peak wind gust of 62 MPH. A wind gust to 60 MPH was reported in Kykotsmovi Village.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The Petrified Forest National Park reported a peak wind gust of 62 MPH.
The Grand Canyon ASOS reported peak winds of 58 MPH.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN COCONINO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The ADOT weather station at Two Guns reported wind gusts of 58 MPH or higher from late morning into early evening.  The peak wind gust was 58 MPH. Blowing dust dropped the visibility at times...down to 5 miles around 1:00 PM.
The visibility was down to 25 feet in blowing dust at times in the community of Many Farms.

events.cz_name: NORTHEAST PLATEAUS AND MESAS FROM HIGHWAY 264 NORTH
events.event_narrative: The Hopi RAWS reported sustained winds of 41 MPH with peak wind gusts of 60 MPH.
A trained spotter just east of Chinle estimated wind gusts to be 65 MPH.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The ASOS at St Johns Airport recorded a peak wind gust of 51 Knots (59 MPH).

The Wallow Fire entered Apache County around 200 PM on June first.  The fire burned a total of 313,103 acres in Apache County. The fire did not spread after June 30th (it was contained). The fire was declared out (controlled) on July 13th. It cost an estimated 58 million dollars to fight the fire in Apache County alone.

The Willow Fire was human caused on June 19th approximately 13 miles northwest of Forest Lakes, AZ.  The fire was turned back to the local district at 600 PM on June 23rd. Full containment was achieved by the end of June. Crews still patrolled the fire into mid July.
The Wash Fire burned about 1,955 acres 	8 miles NE of Heber-Overgaard.

The Locust fire was reported at 1145 AM on the west side of the Community of White River. The fire was human caused.  The main impact of the fire was the removal of vegetation and ground cover on the steep hillside above 137 homes. This would lead to flooding issues during the 2011 rainy season and beyond.
The Engineer Fire was human caused on the Camp Navajo Army Depot base.  Containment was achieved at 601 acres on Tuesday June 7th at 600 PM.
A spotter in Hutchinson Acres reported moderate flooding of roads and washes.
Flash flooding was reported along Campbell Avenue.
The Greer Fire Department reported flash flooding on Butler Creek in Greer. Water and debris flowed to a dept of 1 to 2 feet.
A 64 MPH wind gusts was measured at the Mesonet site in Clarkdale.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm caused flash flooding and debris flow over Paintbrush Lane below the Schutlz Fire burn area.
A RAWS station near Congress reported peak wind gusts of 60 MPH from a thunderstorm.
Spotters reported water, mud, and burn area debris/ash flowing across residential properties and threatening homes.
Heavy rain caused Colter Creek to overflow the banks and flood yards. One quarter of an inch of rain fell in just 15 minutes.
Several intersections along Campbell Avenue were impassable due to small debris, rocks, with shallow surface water overflowing intended drainages.
Colter Creek in Nutrioso was flooding.

Minor flooding was reported in the Greer area. Drainages were flowing 20 to 50 feet wide and 12 to 18 inches deep in Bulter Canyon and East Fork of the Little Colorado River. Water was flowing across the southern portion of East Fork Road. The Little Colorado River was up 18 inches.
A Department of Public Safety worker reported a funnel cloud northwest of Eager. Radar showed an approximate distance of 10 miles northwest of Eager.
The Department of Public Safety reported a rockfall on Highway 89 about 4 miles northeast of Congress.

Heavy rain from a thunderstorm caused a flash flood in Matkatamiba Canyon.  A group of rafters was hiking in the side canyon of the Grand Canyon when a 13 foot wall of water came crashing through.  They were trapped in a wide spot in the canyon above a narrow spot (3 to 5 feet wide) where the flood water was raging 35 to 40 feet deep. Their boats were tied at the mouth of Matkatamiba Canyon.  Two of their boats flipped when the flood hit. Other boats broke loose and floated down the Colorado River and were recovered later.

Tuba City Police received a report that there was a high volume of water flowing through Antelope Canyon. The water flowed for 9 hours in this normally dry slot canyon. Five feet of sand washed out of the upper portion of the canyon.
A flash flood and mud slide crossed Highway 191 just south of Alpine.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm over the Locust Burn area produced significant debris flows and street flooding. Large rocks and sand were carried onto roadways and all drainages were full.
The remote weather station on Promontory Point picked up 2.97 inches of rain in less than two hours.
The remote weather station on Promontory Point picked up 2.97 inches of rain in less than two hours.

Heavy rain over Escudilla Peak area caused flash flooding and mud slides over sections of Highway 180/191 north and southeast of Alpine. Mud, trees, and rocks temporarily blocked the highway between Alpine and Nutrioso.  The Alpine Ranger District Office experienced minor flooding in front of the office. Flooding and erosion on private property was also reported.  Rainfall amounts of around an inch to one and a half inches was reported.
A thunderstorm produced 1.53 inches of rain in Heber-Overgaard.
A thunderstorm produced 1.43 inches of rain on the southeast side of Heber-Overgaard.
Over 2.50 inches of rain fell about 8 miles northwest of Heber-Overgaard. There was lots of water everywhere.
Possible tornado sighted.
Flash flooding covered State Route 99 with at least two feet of water at mile marker 29.  The water covered the road (depth unknown) at mile marker 27.
Thunderstorms produced 2.25 inches of rain in an hour in Pinetop-Lakeside.
A 46 year old man was stuck and killed by lightning at a National Forest Campground at a National Forest campground near Big Lake, Arizona.
Apache Country Road 2153 (unmaintained) near Alpine flooded and was impassable.
Apache Country Road 1126 near Greer flooded. There was over an inch of standing water in the Greer Fire Station.

Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire area caused flash flooding in the community below the fire area.  Baseball to soft ball sized rocks were washed across some roads, a culvert was plugged with rocks/debris, some residents lost power, and the flooding cut new channels through previous alluvial fans.  County and city crews worked for over two hours to clean and open roads.

Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire area caused flash flooding in the community below the fire area.  Baseball to soft ball sized rocks were washed across some roads, a culvert was plugged with rocks/debris, some residents lost power, and the flooding cut new channels through previous alluvial fans.  County and city crews worked for over two hours to clean and open roads.
The Willow Fire was human caused and burned about 213 acres with 292 people assigned to the fire.

The Wallow Fire entered Apache County around 200 PM on June first. The fire burned a total of 313,103 acres in Apache County. The fire did not spread after June 30th (it was contained). The fire was declared out (controlled) on July 13th. It cost an estimated 58 million dollars to fight the fire in Apache County alone.

Heavy rain (0.28 to 0.98) over the Schultz Fire area caused flash flooding in several of the neighborhoods below the burned area. Several roads were covered with water (up to 12) and debris.  These roads were closed until they were cleared.  Some private driveways were destroyed.
A trained spotter in Tonto Village reported approximately 1.50 inches of rain in 30 minutes.

Arizona Department of Transportation reported flooding on Highway 180 from mile post 419 to 425.  A motorcycle was swept away.  The driver was able to escape. Water was flowing over subdivision streets on the north side of Alpine.

Lightning killed a 64-year-old woman visiting the Grand Canyon National Park. It is unclear if the lightning directly hit the victim. Five additional park visitors, ages 45 to 68,  were also injured.  The event took place at Mohave Point.
Minor flooding was reported across Arizona State Route 160 near mile post 365 about 25 miles southwest of Kayenta.

Heavy rain (1.50 inches) was reported in east Flagstaff.  Rain gages in the Schultz Fire burned area reported between 0.39 and 0.83 inches of rain. Most of the water flowing off the burned area remained in ditches with minor street flooding. Three streets experienced higher flows and large amounts of debris were deposited on the roads.
US Highway 160 near Kayenta was close for about an hour due to heavy rain and flash flooding at low water crossings near Kayenta.

Flash flooding flooding and debris flows were reported along side canyons and over road ways in the eastern side of Greer. Rocks one foot in diameter washed over roads. The creek in Butler Canyon over flowed its banks.

Flash flooding was reported in Nutrioso with sheet flow over fields on the east side of town. Nutrioso Creek was running bank full with black water (ash) and debris. Over an inch and a half (1.60 inches) of rain fell between 11 AM and Noon.

Rain gages across the Schultz Fire Area received between 0.59 and 2.68 of rain. Several roads were closed due to flash flooding and debris flows in Hutchison Acres and Timberline neighborhoods downstream from the Schultz Burn Area. Eighteen to 24 inches of water was flowing across Pi��on Road and other roads in the Timberline area.

Wind from a thunderstorm knocked down several trees.  The trees were up to 18 inches in diameter.  A few septic storage tanks about 15 feet in diameter blew across Highway 89.  One vehicle was damaged by the blowing tanks.
A few side streets were impassible in Chino Valley due to heavy rain from a thunderstorm. Highway 89 had four inches of standing water on it at times.
A business in Greer reported heavy rain (0.50) with water flowing down the street. A Mesonet station at Hay Lake recorded 0.87 inches of rain.
A foot of water was running down Butler Canyon which is normally dry.

Heavy rain from a thunderstorm over the Wallow Burn area caused flash flooding,  debris flows, and mud flows across Highway 180 about a mile north of Nutrioso. There was a motorcycle accident due to the mud on the roadway.
Heavy rain fell for about 45 minutes with a total of 0.65 in Alpine.  Several County/Forest Service Roads and Highway 180 were flooded south of Alpine. One road was closed.
Thunderstorms produced 1.70 inches of rain in just 45 minutes. Minor street flooding was reported.
A tornado briefly touched down 1 mile east of milepost 384 on State Route 77.
Heavy rain exceeding rates of 2 inches an hour, produced heavy local street flooding 2 miles north of Prescott Valley.
Heavy rain (1.35) and hail up to 1/2 inch was reported 1 mile east of Highway 89 in Chino Valley.
The National Forest Service reported wind damaged juniper trees with needles missing along a 3/4 mile stretch of State Route 277 about a mile west of Forest Service Road 332.
A rain gage at the Locust Fire burn just west of White River measured 1.05 inches of rain between 630 PM and 715 PM.
Law Enforcement Officials reported flash flooding and debris washing over neighborhood streets and Highway 73 adjacent to the Locust Fire Burn Area.
One inch diameter or larger hail cracked windshields on State Route 277 near Forest Service Road 322.
Flash flooding made parts of roads though Timberline and Hutchinson Acres impassible. Moderate water flows were also reported through Paintbrush Wash.
Heavy rain and flash flooding caused mud and debris flows to cross Highway 180 at mile post 416 near Nutrioso.
Pea to quarter sized hail dented roofs in RVs at Lake Mary Campground. The hail lasted 30 minutes and covered the ground at least one inch deep.
A funnel cloud was sighted west of Chino Valley.
One inch diameter hail was reported by a trained spotter in Chino Valley.
An off duty NWS Employee reported 1 inch diameter hail in Munds Park.
A mud slide along Highway 89 in Oak Creek Canyon partially closed the highway near mile post 378 for approximately four hours.
Quarter sized hail covered the ground.
One inch diameter hail covered the ground at University Heights neighborhood.
One inch diameter hail covered the ground two inches deep along Lake Mary Road.
One inch diameter hail was reported on the Northern Arizona University Campus.
Quarter to ping pong ball sized hail (1 to 1 1/2 inch diameter) were reported on the east side of Flagstaff.
One inch diameter hail was reported from the Interstate 40/17 interchange into West Flagstaff. Cars and roofs were damaged.
Workers at the Gray Mountain ADOT Maintenance yard reported a funnel cloud.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding and debris to flow across roads in Hutchinson Acres and Timberline Estates. Damage to private roads and driveways was also reported. Several roads were impassible.
A trained spotter in Snowflake reported 1 1/4 inch diameter hail and wind gusts of 35 to 40 MPH from 1416 to 1426 MST.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding in many of the neighborhoods below the Schultz Fire burn area.  Three primary roads were closed and most roads in the affected area were impassable. Water was running 35 feet wide and two feet deep through one residential property.  A County Declaration of Emergency was signed in response to this flooding. Portions of rock filled wire baskets that lined one drainage canal collapsed into the the canal and had to be removed and replace.
Quarter sized (1 inch diameter) hail covered the ground 1 mile south of Schnebly Hill Road Exit on I-17.
An official from the Sedona Police Department reported that creeks in the Tlaquepaque area had overflowed. The flood water covered road ways and forced the closure of several roads.
An official with the Lake Powell Tribal Park reported flash flooding of Rattle Snake and Owl Canyons.
Law Enforcement officials reported flooding on Zalesky Road.
Law Enforcement officials reported an ongoing swift water rescue on Spring Creek.
A trained spotter reported flash flood debris covering roadways in Page Springs.
A storm survey revealed that significant forest damage occurred along the Humpherys Trail near the Snowbowl Ski Area around 10,000 feet elevation. Preliminary rating was EF2.
Dilkon Police Officers reported 2 inch diameter hail 3 miles west-southwest of Dilkon.
Dilkon Police Officers reported a brief Funnel Cloud with possible touch down (tornado).
A trained weather spotter reported a funnel cloud off of Highway 89A north of Flagstaff (three miles east of Milepost 440 on Highway 89A).

A flash flood 6 feet deep flowed out of Phantom Canyon and into Bright Angel Creek/Canyon.  The creeks were rearranged, boulders were moved, trees were ripped from the banks of Phantom Creek and deposited at the intersection of Bright Angel Creek. This water then flowed into the Colorado River in the Grand Canyon. This was the highest flood in Phantom and Bright Angel Creeks since 1997.
The RAWS at House Rock reported wind gusts above 58 MPH for about 8 hours. The highest wind gust was 77 MPH.

Wind gusts to 60 MPH were measured in Doney Park down wind from the San Francisco Peaks.

Snow began to fall by mid morning and increased in the afternoon.  Interstate 40 was closed in both directions for the afternoon Thursday as Arizona Department of Transportation worked with officers from the Arizona Department of Public Safety to remove the debris from a number of crashes in the eastbound lanes.  There were five different collisions with the largest involving nine vehicles. The was a 16 mile backup. One driver reported being delayed 11 hours. West bound lanes became blocked when vehicles could not make it up the hill just west of the I-17 interchange.  Eight people were transported to the Flagstaff Medical Center.  North bound I-17 was also blocked for a time due to collisions blocking the roadway.  Highway 180 north of Flagstaff was blocked for a time because of a jack-knifed semi.  Some snowfall totals include (inches): Bellemont 10.5, Flagstaff Airport 6.5, Mormon Lake 5, Munds Park 4, and 4 miles south of Williams 4.
Heavy snow fell over the Kaibab Plateau. Jacob Lake reported around 12 inches of snow and the North Rim of the Grand Canyon reported 14 inches of snow.
Eight inches of snow fell at both the South Rim and Desert View.
Heavy snow fell over the White Mountains area.  Two feet of snow was reported at the  Show Low airport and eight inches fell in McNary.
Heavy snow fell over the Eastern Mogollon Rim.  Snowfall totals include (inches): Linden 15.5 and Heber-Overgaard 10.5.

Interstate 17 south of Flagstaff was close for about two hours because of other traffic accidents.

Snow covered roads and unsafe winter driving lead to at least ten slide offs and collisions in the Flagstaff area on Interstate 40.  At least one vehicle rolled over and one person had to be extracted and was transported to the Flagstaff Medical Center. There were also multiple slide offs and collisions on Interstate 17 near Flagstaff. Both Interstates were blocked for a while. The east bound lanes of I-40 were backed up for as much as 10 miles. State Highway 64 north of Williams was also close for a time due to the weather.

A wind sensor in Linden recorded sustained winds above 40 MPH and/or wind gusts above 58 MPH for close to three hours.  The peak wind gust was 69 MPH. THe Mogollon Airpark reported a peak wind gust of 60 MPH.
Two different wind sensors in Doney Park (northeast of Flagstaff on the lee side of the San Francisco Peaks) reported peak wind gusts of 61 MPH.

Six inches of snow fell in Lukachukai at an elevation of about 6400 feet above mean sea level. Delivery trucks had to turn around because of the snow before they could reach town.  Three inches of snow fell in Dennehotso at an elevation of 5000 feet.
Three inches of snow fell in Page at an elevation of 4200 feet. This much snow at this elevation meets the heavy snow criteria.

Eight inches of new snow fell in Jacob Lake overnight.  ADOT reported a total of 12 inches of new snow about a mile north of Jacob Lake by noon.

An approaching cold front brought high wind to the Eastern Mogollon Rim during the early morning hours.  The peak wind gust in Linden was 61 MPH.  The Limestone RAWS recorded peak wind gusts between 57 and 59 MPH between 100 AM and 5 AM.

Blowing dust was reported in Many Farms.  The visibility was about 120 yards and below 50 yards at times.  The Police Department in Chinle reported poor visibility in blowing dust all day.  At least one employee had to stop on the road while driving to work because of the blowing dust.  The wind was estimated to be 40 to 50 MPH with gusts to 60 MPH.  Employees at a hotel in Kayenta reported 1/2 mile visibility in dust with estimated gusts to 70 MPH.
The House Rock RAWS reported wind gusts of 58 MPH or higher for several hours during the afternoon.  The peak wind gust was 69 MPH.

events.event_narrative: The Arizona Department of Transportation wind sensor at Two Guns along Interstate 40 reported wind gust around 58 MPH or higher for around two hours and sustained winds of 30 MPH or higher for about 6 hours.  The peak wind gust was 65 MPH.  Wupatki National Monument had a peak wind gust of 63 MPH.
A weather spotter two miles north of McNary reported 12.5 inches of snow with this storm. Show Low received 9 inches of new snow.

Heavy to very heavy snow fell across the Western Mogollon Rim.  Areas around Flagstaff picked up 18 to 28 inches of snow.  A local ski resort reported an impressive 53 inches of snow above 9000 feet elevation. Northern Arizona University, Coconino Community College, and most other schools cancelled classes in the Flagstaff area.  A 200 mile section of Interstate 40 was closed in both directions between Kingman and Winslow.  A 42 mile section of northbound (up hill) Interstate 17 was closed from the Sedona exit to Flagstaff. The Coconino County Sheriff's search and rescue unit warned people of the avalanche danger in the San Fransisco Peaks.
A spotter in the community of Parks reported a peak wind gust of 61 MPH.
The Mogollon Rim Airpark reported a peak wind gust of 62 MPH around 255 PM and Linden RAWS reported a peak wind gust of 61 MPH around 540 PM.
Eighteen inches of snow fell in Forest Lakes. Seven inches of snow fell 3 miles southeast of Linden and 8.5 inches of snow fell in Heber-Overgaard.
Payson and Pine both received 7 inches of snow.

The Prescott area received 5 to 14 inches of snow depending on elevation. The City of Prescott is at about 5280 feet and the snow level started out above that level and then dropped through the night.  Ash Fork received 12 inches of snow.
Chino Valley (4570 feet elevation) received 4 inches of snow. Wilhoit received 8 inches of snow at around 4500 feet elevation.
Sedona received 4 inches of snow at an elevation of about 4500 feet.
The ASOS at the Show Low Airport recorded a peak wind gust of 58 MPH at 2:15 PM.  The sustained wind also exceeded 40 MPH several times between 12:55 PM and 3:40 PM.
Strong winds caused blowing dust and sand that reduced the visibility down to 1/2 mile at times along Highway 160 in Cow Springs. The wind speed was 50 MPH.

Seven inches of snow fell 5 miles west of Prescott.
Eight to twelve inches of snow fell in and around Flagstaff.
Seven inches of snow was reported in Pinetop-Lakeside.

events.event_narrative: A shower passing to the east of Meteor Crater caused a down bust with a peak wind of 60 MPH and blowing dust.
A trained spotter in Concho reported 0.40 inches of rain in thirty minutes.
The Cottonwood Wildfire was reported about 15 miles north of Whiteriver. The fire was about 15 acres at the time that it was reported.
A wildfire was reported near Wide Ruins at about 10 acres. Fire crews were on-site for at least 5 days.

The Grand Fire was reported at 1230 PM on May 12th. The fire burned a total of 480 acres in the Grand Canyon National Park and in the Kaibab National Forest. The fire was declared contained by the end of the day on May 18th.

The Poco Fire was reported at 233 PM on June 14 about six miles northeast of Young, Arizona.  The fire grew to 11, 950 acres before it was declared contained on July 5. Containment cost were estimated to be 9 million dollars. This area experienced several flash floods and debris flows as the rainy season became active in July and August. Fire fire fighters were injured during containment efforts.
The Dinnebito Wash Fire was reported on June 16 about 15 miles south of Kayenta.  It was contained by the end of the day on June 20.
The Turkey Fire started about 10 miles northwest of Heber and was reported around 230 AM on June 25.  The fire was contained at about 80 acres by the end of the day on June 26.
The Canyon Fire was reported in Jacks Canyon about 30 miles southwest of Winslow just after 700 AM on June 29. The fire was contained at 6935 acres on July 5.

The Gladiator Fire began burning on May 13 when a structure fire spread.  A total of six structures were destroyed by the fire.  Eight people suffered injuries. The fire, which covered approximately 16,240 acres, cost $14 million to contain.

A climber in Jacks Canyon downstream from the Canyon Fire area reported heavy rain and hail started around 1215. He also stated: The primary stage of the flood was from 1245-1430. Secondary stage from 1430-1630 and tertiary 1630- until we exited around 1845. The next morning the water was still flowing but had decreased by 80% or so. During the storm we were having lightning strikes with in a mile every 90secs between 1230-1430. Hail and high winds for 15-30 minutes around 1300. Hail stones around 4-8mm.||I would guess that the size and energy of the flood had to do more with the fact that it was a recent fire area. The storm did move from the East to the South West which pretty much follows the topography of the canyon. The debris was mostly fire damage trees and soil.||No other reports of flooding in that area were received.
Trained spotters reported 1.17 and 1.70 inches of rain in Williams.
A thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 69 MPH four miles north of Prescott.
Just over an inch of rain fell in 35 minutes. A mud slide was reported on Gladiator Road between mile post 26 and 27. The road was still passable.
The Prescott Police Department reported many major stream and creek road crossings were closed due to flooding. One house in Williamson Valley started to incur non-life threatening flooding.
A thunderstorm produced heavy rain and flash flooding over the Gladiator Fire area. A main road was washed out and there were also mud slides.
Two vehicles were washed off the Crown King Road (possibly Poland Creek) near the community of Cleator. The occupants were rescued.
A trained spotter reported 5.47 inches of rain in 14 hours about ten miles southwest of Cordes.
A trained spotter reported heavy flows though Dripping Springs and Turkey Creek. It was the worst flooding in eight and a half years.

Havasupai Tribal Police reported a four foot rise in Havasu Creek. Bridges over the creek washed out.  River runners on the Colorado River recorded a flash flood in National Canyon that dumped rocks, trees, mud, and 2 foot deep foam into the Colorado River.  This enhanced the rapid at the mouth of National Canyon.
Alert gages around Crown King reported between 2.84 and 4.52 inches of rain in an 18 to 20 hour time period.
Quarter sized hail and some slightly larger stones were reported in Lakeside.
Thunderstorms produced 3 inches of rain in just over three hours in Pine.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused Pine Creek to overflow Bradshaw Road making it impassible.
Golf ball sized (1.75 inches in diameter) fell at the Cameron Trading Post.
A RAWS at Sunset Point measured a 67 MPH thunderstorm wind gust. A truck was blown over on Interstate 17 about 4 miles north of the Sunset Point Rest Area.
Heavy rain filled several washes and closed several road crossings for a while.
Wind from a thunderstorm broke a branch out of a tree and it fell on power wires and knocked out power.
Lightning struck a power pole and the pole caught fire.
Water was flowing over Highway 260 at milepost 218.
Between 1 and 1.32 inches of rain fell in an hour in and around Payson. Flooding was reported everywhere. The worst was Forest Drive with two feet of water on the road.
Between 1.22 and 2.50 inches of rain fell across the South Rim of the Grand Canyon westward to Supai Village in 5 to 8 hours. Rockslides were reported on Bright Angel Trail.

Supai Village Police reported a 3 to 4 foot rise in Havasu Creek near Supai Village. The campground was evacuated. The trail bridges were compromised and the people on the west side of Havasu Creek were stranded.

Heavy rain from a thunderstorm closed the intersection of Dupont and Leroux. Flooding was also reported at Agassiz St and Rt 66. Lightning strikes caused power outages in Downtown Flagstaff.  1/4 inch hail was reported on the NAU Campus.
Heavy rain (2.10 inches) fell in Dewey-Humbolt. The intersection of Agua Fria and Prescott Street was close for a while due to high water.
Whiteriver Police reported 0.90 inches of rain in 40 minutes and debris on Route 73.
Heavy rain caused street flooding in Tuba City with water entering homes. Highway 89 had water and debris on the roadway. Water was flowing in Moenkpi Wash.

Heavy rain from a thunderstorm washed debris across Interstate 17. The water and debris were about four inches deep. The road was closed after several vehicles punctured tires on the debris. The road opened after the flow stopped and the roadway was cleared.

A cinder block flew through a wand in a house and poked a hole in the sheet rock inside. Another cinder block fell into the sheet metal roof. Possible micro burst lifted building material (4X8 foot plywood) with the cinder blocks on top...lofting the cinder blocks into the house. Three power lines were also blown down. The heavy rain from the thunderstorm was a foot deep in places.
A funnel cloud was seen form the community of Rough Rock.
A funnel cloud was seen for seven minutes about two miles west of St Johns. Wind from the thunderstorm blew a trampoline about 800 feet.
Hail (0.2 to 0.8 inches in diameter) covered the ground one inch deep.

Flood waters from heavy rain that fell on Tuesday evening (July 31) reached Supai Village between 230 and 300 AM. Water up to several feet caused trails and bridges to become impassible. This stranded several hikers and flooded area campgrounds.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused damage to the River Trail on the south side of the Colorado River about a mile from Phantom Ranch.  The heavy rain also caused a rock fall that injured a 19 year old hiker in a narrow canyon about 5 miles north of Phantom Ranch.
A river gage in Paria Canyon measured a four foot rise in less than 30 minutes on the Paria River.
Heavy rain fell for 30 minutes northwest of Alpine. Three feet of water covered a country road. Highway 180 was also closed until the water receded and the debris was cleared.
Heavy rain over the Fire area caused a mud and rock slide over Road 512 (Heber-Young Road). Road crews were called to clear the mud and debris from the road.
Heavy rain (2.23 inches) fell over the Bagdad area. This caused flash flooding in the Bagdad Mine area. Portions of Highway 97 where washed out from mile marker 159 to 165.
Heavy rain caused two feet of water to flow over Navajo Route 15 near the community of Cornfields.
Street flooding was reported in St Johns. Manhole covers were being displaced because there was so much water.
A peak wind gust of 70 MPH was recorded at the St Johns Airport.  Law enforcement also reported that trees were blown down in town.
Sunset Wash overflowed on to Sunset Drive. Police set up barricades to close the road.
Heavy rain over the Schultz Fire area washed out a couple of driveways and a portion of Brandis Way.
Heavy rain (0.62 inch) fell in Doney Park with ponding water around the property.
Spotters reported 3/4 inch diameter hail that stripped leaves from trees and ruined a garden.
There were numerous reports of street flooding in Chino Valley. Some roads were washed out. Some of the impacted roads included Yuma Road, 3 North, Son Shine Land, and Buffalo Run at Highway 89.
Water was flowing across Highway 89A in West Sedona. Sunset Drive and Shelby Drive were close to do water on the roadway. Between 1.00 and 1.50 inches of rain was recorded in Sedona.
Very heavy rain fell along Oak Creek Canyon. Debris fell onto the road at the upper end of the canyon.
Heavy rain caused minor damage to some of the less traveled road in the Gladiator Fire area. One of the automated rain gauges around the fire reported 1.90 inches of rain.
Yavapai County Sheriff Department reported debris along State Route 97 near mile post 163 (about 5 miles south of Bagdad).
Tuba City Police reported minor flooding from heavy rain in the Kerley Valley.  Water covered Highway160 and caused a temporary road closure.

Heavy rain fell over the Schultz Fire area.  Heavy run off covered subdivision streets. Runoff covered one lane of Highway 89 with debris and that lane was closed until the water went down and the debris was cleared.
Thunderstorms with heavy rain caused minor flooding in much of Tuba City with damaged landscaping and washed out driveways.
Highway 264 was washed out by a flash flood at mile marker 323 just southeast of Tuba City.

events.event_narrative: The Winslow ASOS reported less than 3 miles visibility in blowing dust for over two hours. A trained spotter one mile east of Winslow reported one mile visibility in blowing dust at 1255 PM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN COCONINO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The Arizona Department of Transportation anemometer at Two Guns reported a peak wind gust of 70 MPH.  A wind sensor on the edge of Meteor Crater reported sustained winds of 60-70 MPH with a gust to 111 MPH. This location is not representative of the conditions away from the crater rim.

Between 0.30 and 0.70 of rain fell in about 15 minutes over the Schultz Fire area and the neighborhood below the fire area. Water was flowing over Brandis Road with rocks up to baseball sized rolling over the road. The maximum flow across the road was about 10 feet wide and a foot deep. Road crews were able to clean the road off. Water was still flowing in the ditches 5 hours later.

A weather station at 11,526 feet above sea level on Agassiz Peak reported wind gusts over 60 MPH for over 10 hours. The peak wind gust was 88 MPH.  Arizona Snowbowl reported two snags (large dead trees) blew down near on or the lodges.  Other trees blew down on the 777 acre ski area.

Snow started to fall late afternoon on Thursday December 13 across the Western Mogollon Rim including the Flagstaff area and tapered off Friday afternoon. The storm generally left 3-6 inches of snow with one report of 7 inches. Arizona Department of Public Safety reported about 20 slide offs, two minor collisions, and a jack-knifed semi trailer on Interstate 40.  The Flagstaff Police Department reported 8 traffic accidents. One of those accidents had injuries. The Coconino Country Sheriff's office reported one accident.
Eighteen to 20 inches of new snow fell in Forest Lakes. Clints Well area received 9 inches and Heber-Overgaard received 8 inches of new snow. Eighteen inches of new snow was reported on Dane Ridge.
Between 10 and 16 inches of snow fell above 8000 feet. Four to 5 inches of new snow fell between 6000 and 7000 feet.

The Flagstaff Airport received 11.7 inches of new snow. Munds Park received 7.3 inches, Bellemont 10.8 inches, and Mountainaire 12.5 inches.  Interstate 40 was closed in both directions between Ash Fork and Williams because there were so many drivers having problems driving and staying on the road. The largest collision involved three semi trucks and two passenger vehicles. Interstate 17 south of Flagstaff remained open even though there were numerous slide offs, spin outs, and collisions. Law enforcement officials received hundreds of calls for assistance.
A spotter at the North Rim of the Grand Canyon (over 8200 feet elevation) reported 11.5 inches of snow.

A wind sensor at 11,526 feet on Agassiz Peak reported wind gusts over 80 MPH for 30 minutes. The winds gusted over 60 MPH for close to 6 hours.  The wind sensor was damaged by the wind. Trees were knocked down near that elevations.  A local ski resort employee said that the wind likely gusted over 100 MPH before the sensor was damaged.
Over eight inches of snow fell just north and northeast of Payson.
A spotter two miles north of McNary reported 8.3 inches of snow at an elevation of around 7400 feet.

Rain showers developed over Apache County during the early hours of January 26 and continued through the 28th. The heaviest rain fell over orographically favored areas.  The greatest rainfall totals include: 2 miles north of McNary 1.65 inches, Tsaile 1.15 inches, Canyon de Chelly 1.11 inches, and Window Rock Airport 1.09. The snow level remained high for most of this event. Snow reports include: Sunrise Ski 6.0 inches and Window Rock 3 inches.

Light to moderate rain fell across Coconino County for several days with the snow level above 8500 feet for much of the time. Some rainfall amounts (in inches) include: Flagstaff Airport 2.56, Fort Valley 2.44, Kachina Village 2.23, Bellemont 2.48, Limestone Canyon 1.78, Valle 1.59, Blue Ridge 1.49, Page 0.72, and Lees Ferry 0.59.
Heavy rain fell across Northern Gila County.  Some of the rainfall amounts (in inches) include: Tonto Creek Fish Hatchery 4.97, Red Lake 3.22, Pleasant Valley 2.36, and Payson Airport 2.13.

Heavy rain fell across Navajo Gila County.  Some of the rainfall amounts (in inches) include: 15 miles south of Heber 2.32, Navajo National Monument 1.61, Show Low Airport 0,84, Winslow 0.84, and Petrified Forest National Park 0.34.

Heavy rain fell across Yavapai County. Some of the rainfall amounts (in inches) include: Crown King 3.60, Humbug Creek 3.23, Sedona Airport 2.77, Sunset Point 2.48, 5 miles northwest of Prescott 2.24, Cottonwood/Tuzigoot 1.36, and Prescott Airport 1.82.

Mountainaire and Williams reported 7.5 and 6.8 inches of new snow by 600 PM February 9 with the first round of snow in a series of disturbances moving across northern Arizona. Both locations are between 5000 feet and 7000 feet.  By the morning of February 11 the storm moved east and left a blanket of snow across the area. Total snowfall amounts include:  Snowbowl Ski Resort 19 inches at 10800 feet and 10 inches at 9000 feet, 18.2 inches 5 miles south of Williams, 11 inches in Williams, 14 inches in Mountainaire, 13.3 inches at the Flagstaff Airport, 10.4 inches in Kachina Village, and 9.2 inches in Bellemont.
Happy Jack Ranger Station reported a storm total of 24 inches of new snow, Forest Lakes had 15 inches, and Clints Well reported 10 inches, Linden (2ESE) had 16 inches.

Heavy snow fell across northern Gila County with the lower elevations reaching heavy snow criteria sooner than higher elevations. Snowfall totals include (in inches): Whispering Pines 20, Tonto Village 16, Pine (5800 feet) 10,  Payson (14 NNE) 12, Tonto Natural Bridge 9.2, and Payson (4900 feet) 7.9.

Sunrise Ski Resort had 14 inches of snow by 800 AM on February 10. By the time the storm ended, Pinetop-Lakeside had 11.8 inches, Show Low had 10.5 inches, Show Low Airport 7.4 inches, and McNary (2N) had 8.1 inches.

events.event_narrative: A weather spotter in Vernon reported 10 inches of snow from this storm.
Eleven inches of snow was reported in upper Oak Creek Canyon.
Thirteen inches of snow fell in Jacob Lake.
Eight inches of snow fell in Munds Park at an elevation of around 6500 feet.
Six inches of snow fell in Rimrock at an elevation of around 3600 feet.

Strong upslope flow enhanced snowfall over Northern Gila County along the Mogollon Rim. Snowfall amounts (in inches) include: Strawberry/Pine 8-10, Payson 6-9, Tonto Village 8.5, and Whispering Pines 8-9.
Forest Lakes received 12 inches of snow. Nine inches of snow was reported in Blue Ridge.
Sixteen inches of snow fell at Sunrise Ski Resort.  Twelve inches of snow was reported 10 miles west of Greer.
Snowfall totals (in inches) include: Forest Lakes 26 and  Heber-Overgaard 6-9.  Power outages were reported in Heber-Overgaard because of the heavy wet snow.
Nine inches of snow fell around Jacob Lake.
Thirteen inches of snow fell at the North Rim of the Grand Canyon.
Pine and Payson both received 6 inches of snow.  An area 15 miles northeast of Payson received 10 inches of snow.

Six inches of snow fell in an area 3 miles north of Sedona at an elevation of 5000 feet. 5.2 inches of snow fell in Oak Creek Canyon at the Junipine Resort at an elevation of 5075 feet. It rained for several hours before the snow level lowered to below 5000 feet.

Snowfall totals (in inches) include: Arizona Snowbowl 21, Flagstaff 16, Flagstaff Airport 15.2, Williams 6, Kachina Village 12, Bellemont 12, and Munds Park 10.8. The Department of Public Safety reported at least 60 slide offs, 20 collisions, 14 motorist assists, and three injuries.
Pinetop-Lakeside received 12 inches of snow.  Sunrise Ski Park received 23 inches of snow.
Prescott Valley (4880 feet) received 2 inches of snow.
Strong winds brought blowing dust to the Chinle Valley with visibility down to 1/2 mile at times.

A Skywarn Weather spotter relayed reports that several people saw a tornado touch down at the Winslow City Park.  No damage was reported.

At approximately 1:00 p.m. on Monday, July 15 a lightning strike near Mather Point resulted in several visitors reporting injuries to the Grand Canyon Visitors Center. The group of visitors was standing near the Rim when the lightning strike occurred. Four individuals were transported to the South Rim Clinic for evaluation of non-life-threatening injuries.
The Grand Canyon Airport set a record low of 7F.  The previous record of 12F was set in 2008.
The Flagstaff Airport set a record low of 15F.  The previous record of 16F was set in 1978.
The Show Low Airport set a record low of 22F.  The previous record of 24F was set in 1986.
The Page Airport set a record low of 37F.  The previous record of 38F was set in 2006.

events.event_narrative: The Winslow Airport set a record low of 19F.  The previous record of 24F was set in 2007 and 1998.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The Winslow Airport ASOS reported wind gusts higher than 58 MPH from around 730 AM to 330 PM and sustain winds 40 MPH or higher from 530 AM to 500 PM MST.  Blowing dust was also reported between 800 AM to 200 PM MST. The dust reduced the visibility to 3 miles right around 900 AM MST. A weather spotter in Winslow reported that his sheet metal roof blew off his manufactured home. A Co-Op observer in Snowflake reported broken limbs from trees, roof shingles blown off homes, siding blown off homes, and blowing dust.  Interstate 40 was closed between Winslow and Twin Arrows for 12 hours (600 AM to 600 PM MST) because of the blowing dust and high winds. Traffic was backed up for more than 12 miles.  The Petrified Forest National Park South Entrance Visitor Center reported a peak wind gust of 61 MPH at 1115 AM MST.

events.event_narrative: Interstate 40 was closed between Twin Arrows and Winslow and for 12 hours (600 AM to 600 PM MST) because of the blowing dust and high winds. Traffic was backed up for more than 12 miles.

A wind sensor in Doney Park reported a peak wind gust of 65 MPH at around 600 AM MST.  Sustained winds of 40 MPH or higher lasted from around 1000 PM on April 14 to 115 PM on April 15.  Wind gusts of at least 58 MPH lasted from around 1245 AM to 8 AM MST on April 15.  Arizona DOT reported that a tree fell across Highway 89 and blocked one lane of traffic north of the Sunset Crater turn off at 519 AM on April 16.
Blowing dust reduced the visibility to near zero at times from early morning through the afternoon from Kayenta to Many Farms to Chinle along US Highways 160 and 191.

The AWOS at the Show Low Airport reported sustained winds of 40 MPH from around 800 AM to 300 PM MST.  The wind gusted over 58 MPH from around 900 AM to 200 PM MST.  The peak wind gust was 61 MPH around 1030 AM MST.

The Grand Canyon ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 58 MPH at 928 AM.  The wind gusts were above 40 MPH between 854 AM and 1128 AM when it started to snow.

events.event_narrative: The Winslow ASOS reported blowing dust that reduced the visibility down to 1.5 miles at times between 1056 AM and 156 PM.

events.event_narrative: The Winslow ASOS reported wind gusts over 58 MPH from 932 AM to 156 PM. The peak wind gust was 66 MPH at 1222 PM. A power line snapped on the east side of town around 1218 PM.  The police department in Holbrook reported that part of a roof blew off and took out a power line, a tree was blown down, and a trailer home skirting peeled off by the wind.
The Flagstaff ASOS reported wind gusts of 58 MPH or higher from 1108 AM to 1257 PM. The peak wind gust was 63 MPH at 1157 AM.

The Limestone RAWS reported wind gusts 58 MPH and higher from 924 AM to 524 PM. The peak wind gust was 80 MPH at 1224 PM. This RAWS is in an exposed location near the south side of the Mogollon Rim and my measure higher winds than are experienced in much of the rest of the zone.
The Sedona AWOS measured a peak wind gust of 58 MPH at 1135 AM.  Wind gusts over 50 MPH were recorded from 1055 AM to 1235 PM.

The Show Low Airport AWOS reported a peak wind gust of 64 MPH at 1255 PM.  The wind gusts were above 58 MPH from 1135 to 255 PM. Police reported that a large tree snapped and a light pole was blown down in a parking log in Show Low at 215 PM.
The Humbug Creek RAWS reported a peak wind gust of 62 MPH at 1148 AM.  The wind gusts were over 58 MPH from 1148 AM to 148 PM.
Strong wind caused blowing dust to reduce the visibility to near zero at times all afternoon in Chinle.  The visibility dropped down to 1/2 mile in Kayenta and 1/4 mile in Many Farms.

Strong wind caused blowing dust to reduce the visibility to near zero at times all afternoon in Chinle. The southwest winds blew this dust from Chinle into the Chuska Mountains. The Window Rock ASOS reported reduced visibility in haze (dust) down to 2.5 miles at times between 100 PM to 4 PM MST.
The Window Rock Airport reported a peak wind gust of 60 MPH at 253 PM.  Wind gusts of at least 58 MPH were reported at times from 153 PM to 438 PM.
