The stream gauge at Supai showed a rapid rise on Havasu Creek at 200 AM.
Forest Drive in Payson was closed with barricades because swiftly running water covered the road. A nearby rain gauge reported 1.82 inches of rain between 2:06 and 3:37 PM.
Cedar Creek had a 5 foot rise below the Cedar Fire scar after a thunderstorm dropped heavy rain over the area.  The water was receding by 329 PM.
Heavy rain fell over the Goodwin Fire scar east of Mayers. This resulted in flash flooding in Mayers and East Central Avenue was closed.

Heavy rain over Interstate 40 between Sanders and Lupton caused up to one foot of water to accumulate on the road (between mile markers 354 and 359).  Initial reports indicated that several cars were stopped along the highway.  However,  DPS only saw one car stopped when they arrived and the water had receded.
The Big Bug Creek gauge in Mayer at SR-69 showed a 2.9 rise between noon and 130 PM MST.  The water level was falling slowly at 233 PM MST. The flood crest reached Cordes Lakes at 345 PM MST.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm caused flash flooding and rock falls. State Route 69 was closed in both directions at mile post 302 south of Prescott.  One lane was opened after 30 minutes.

The Flagstaff airport received 19 inches of snow from January 5 through January 7th. Hart Prairie (at 9200 feet) received 32 inches. Schools were closed in the Flagstaff area including Northern Arizona University. Law enforcement officers responded to over 180 slide offs and motorist assists, over 90 collisions, and over a dozen minor injuries in the Flagstaff area.
Water in Lynx Creek over-topped the intersection of Walker Road and New Strike Lane in Walker.
Several driveways were washed out in town because the water flow from the heavy rain was more than the culverts in the ditch could handle.
Flash flooding one mile east of the Blue Gap Store badly damaged Highway 4.
The Paria River Gauge at Lees Ferry showed a 3 foot rise at 645 AM. It is estimated that this flood crest entered Arizona (from thunderstorms in Utah) around 345 AM.
Flash flooding washed out Indian Route 6330 north of Highway 98.

Heavy rain over the Polacca Wash basin caused a rise of 1.61 feet between 300 AM MST (4 AM MDT) and 325 AM MST (325 AM MDT) at the river gauge (POLA3) near Second Mesa. The maximum gauge reading was 7.42 feet. By 1030 AM MST, the water had receded to a level of 6.91.  The gauge is normally dry with a baseline reading of 5.81 feet.

A trained spotter reported 2.05 inches of rain between 1220 PM and 220 PM. This caused flash flooding in parts of Flagstaff.  Another spotter measured 3.20 inches of rain in an hour and fifteen minutes at the corner of Elder and King Street (noon to 115 PM MST).
Heavy rain from thunderstorms flooded urban roadways and low-lying areas in much of east Flagstaff.  A wash (Switzer Canyon Wash) flooded the intersection of Butler and 4th Street.

The Arizona Department of Transportation reported flooding of State Route 264 at milepost 438 near Burnside due to heavy rain that fell in the region. The road was closed for a couple hours as a preventative measure.

A trained spotter in Ash Fork reported 1.76 inches of rain between 200 PM and 4:36 PM. This led to flash flooding of Double A Ranch Road with 3-4 inches of standing water on the roadways. Portions of dirt roadways were washed away as a result of the localized flooding.

Lynx Creek immediately upstream from Fain Lake (in Fain Park) was experiencing flash flooding conditions that were causing the creek water to flow out of the banks. The flooding continued upstream to Costco. Flooding in the Diamond Valley area. Diamond Drive was washed out with significant flooding over roads in the neighborhood.
A trained spotter in Hotevilla measured 1.75 inches of rainfall in an hour. Water was flowing over local roads with some flood damage to private roads.

Big Bug Creek experienced flash flood conditions during the mid-afternoon which lasted for approximately two hours. Water rose out the banks and flooded East Antelope Road. Much of the rain fell over the Goodwin Fire scar. Winds also gusted up to 45 MPH between 315 and 415 PM MST. The flood waters continued on down the Agua Fria Wash for another 6 to 9 hours.  This water eventually flowed into Black Canyon Creek near Black Canyon City. The Agua Fria River gauge at Old Black Canyon City Highway showed a rapid rise of 2.2 feet at 230 AM on July 16.
Glassford Hill Road was close next to Bradshaw High School due to mud from new subdivision. Brawshaw High School had water in the gym, likely from area flooding.
The City of Sedona closed Sunset Drive at the low water crossing just north of Sunset Park. There was about two feet of water running over the road.
Taylor Police reported that East Willow Lane was closed due to water running over the roadway.
Arizona Department of Transportation reported standing water along State Route 277 and advised against driving through flooded sections.

A trained spotter reported flooding and debris over roads in the Diamond Valley subdivision. The entrance road was washed out.  ||Arizona Department of Highways reported that flowing water washed rocks on State Route 69 at mile post 290.  They estimated that 1.30 inches of rain fell in less than an hour.||The spillway gauge at Fain Lake showed 3 feet of water flowing over the Spillway.  Water does not frequently flow over the spillway.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms over the Goodwin Fire scar and the surrounding areas created flash flooding in the Big Bug Creek and the Agua Fria River system all the way down to Lake Pleasant. ||0540 PM     FLASH FLOOD      MAYER                   34.40N 112.23W|07/16/2018                   YAVAPAI            AZ   MESONET          ||           |The Big Bug Creek gauge at Mayer reported at 1.9 foot rise at 540 PM MST.  ||The Agua Fria gauge at Humboldt rose from 1.7 feet to 11.7 feet at 545 PM MST.  ||The Agua Fria river gauge at Kelton Ranch reported a 4.7 foot rise at 940 PM MST.  ||The Agua Fria river gauge near Black Canyon City a 3 foot rise in 10 minutes at 210 AM on July 17.  This gauge showed another 3.31 foot rise between 500 AM and 600 AM MST.
The stream gauge at Big Bug Creek at Mayer reported a 3.1 foot rise at 1040 PM MST.

Heavy rain in Utah caused a flash flood that flowed into Arizona in the Paria River.  The gauge at Lees Ferry (Colorado River) reached a peak flow of 1,436 CFS at 430 AM MST in a normally drive river bed. The flood took several hours to travel from the Utah border to the gauge.
The Yarnell Remote Automated Weather Station reported a peak wind gust of 65 MPH at 1101 PM MST.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused flash flooding in the northern drainages of the Schultz Fire scar.  The impacts were along Copeland Avenue northward to Wupatki Trails. Water was flowing over roads and drainage ditches were overtopped.  ||A public rain gauge reported 1.80 inches of rain in less than 3 hours ending at 0400 PM     MST.||Radar and other rain gauges estimated between 3 and 5.90 inches of rain over parts of the area. This represents between a 100 year and a 1000 year rainfall event. ||Three homes had flood damage inside, other structures and outbuildings suffered flood damage, and 2 residences requested debris removal.  Coconino County road crews spent up to 2 weeks removing debris, mud, and rocks from water channels and roads.

Arizona Department of Transportation reported flooding on State Route 264 in several locations between Steamboat (mile marker 430) and Burnside (mile marker 438). The road was closed for several hours as a preventative measure. ADOT was clearing debris off the road.
Heavy rain was reported on Highway 89 with water running across the roadway.  Cars could still make it through the flooded section of highway.
One inch diameter hail was reported by a NWS employee 3 miles south of the Flagstaff Mall.
An alert rain gauge near the Flagstaff Mall reported 4.57 inches of rain in 1 hour and | 45 minutes.

Pictures on social media showed flooded parking lots at car dealer ships with water up to the hood of vehicles one mile east of the Flagstaff Mall. Other pictures showed 2.5 to 3 feet of water flowing in the normally dry Switzer Wash at 4th Street and Butler Avenue.
Quarter-sized hail (1 inch in diameter) was reported by a trained spotter at 345 and 400 PM MST in Ash Fork.
A trained spotter reported 1.61 inches of rain in around an hour. Dime sized (3/4 inch diameter) hail also fell.
Hail damaged approximately 1000 cars in shopping centers and car dealerships.
The river gauge on Big Bug Creek at Mayer showed a 2.1 rise  at 620 MST due to heavy rain from a thunderstorm over the Goodwin Fire scar. A second flood wave of the same height came at 1050 PM MST.
Emergency Manager reported that flooding was impacting homes and shut down westbound lane of Interstate-40. Emergency shelter for people and large livestock established in Holbrook.
South Verde Lakes Drive in Camp Verde was closed due to flash flooding.
State Route 377 was close due to flooding at mile marker 7.
Police reported flooding on Highway 260 at milepost 224.
Heavy rain over the Cedar Fire scar caused a flash flood in Cedar Creek.  The water reached 5 feet deep. Rainfall over the the town of Cedar creek also washed out private driveways.

The MESONET station in Camp Verde measured a 72 MPH wind gust at 405 PM from a thunderstorm in the area. A large cottonwood tree was snapped by wind 1 mile south-southwest of Cornville at 515 PM. Several 5 inch diameter tree branches were downed by wind in Cornville around 530 PM. The National Forest Service District Office had significant wind damage to solar panels. Several were ripped from the support beams around 600 PM MST.
One inch diameter hail was reported in Camp Verde. The hail put holes in solar panels at the US National Forest District Office.
One inch diameter hail fell in Sedona (3/4 of a mile south of the intersection of Highways 89A and 179.
The river gauge on Beaver Creek indicated at 4.5 foot rise starting at 800 PM.
A thunderstorm produce one inch diameter hail in Fernwood.
Several trees and power poles were blown down in the Chino Valley around 530 PM.
The gauge on the Verde River indicated a sudden rise of 4 feet.
The gauge on the Agua Fria River indicated a rapid rise of 3 feet at 800 PM MST.
The gauge on Agua Fria River near Mayer reported a rapid rise of 6 feet.
A peak wind gust of 70 MPH was observed at the Sunset Point RAWS. The time was estimated.
Heavy rain caused a mud slide that closed the south bound lanes of I-17 south of Sunset Point Rest Area.
Quarter-sized (1 inch in diameter) hail was reported in the Prescott area.
Heavy rain caused flowing water on Highway 69 at Lee Boulevard.
The gauge on Havasu Creek rose from 7.46 to 11.24 feet in 15 minutes (500 to 515 PM MST). The peak flow was 1157 CFS (base flow is less than 90 CFS).

Heavy rain in Utah caused flash flooding on the Paria River that flowed into Arizona and then into the Colorado River just below Lees Ferry. The river gauge on the Paria River at Lees Ferry showed a rapid 1.5 foot rise at 245 AM MST.  It takes about 6 hours for water to reach the Colorado River once it enters Arizona from Utah.

The RAWS at Humbug Creek reported a peak wind gust of 75 MPH around 648 PM MST.  The Yarnell RAWS reported a peak wind gust of 52 MPH (0701 PM).   The Sunset Point RAWS reported a peak wind gust of 56 MPH (553 PM).
A lightning strike started a house fire. No injuries were reported.

A thunderstorm produced 1 to 2 inch diameter hail between Flagstaff, Camp Navajo/Bellemont, and Parks. The hail last about 10 minutes at any give location. Significant ponding of water on roads was also reported in Parks.

A thunderstorm produced golf ball sized (1 3/4 inch diameter) hail between 10 miles west of Ash Fork to near Perkinsville road and Drake Road.  Wind gusts to 39 MPH and 0.45 inches of rain were also reported with this storm.  The event lasted up to 20 minutes as it moved through the area.
Heavy rain caused 6 to 8 inches of water to flow across normally dry ranch land 7 miles southwest of Ash Fork. Eightmile Creek was overflowing the its banks south of Interstate-40.
An eight inch diameter fruit tree was snapped in half because of a thunderstorm gust front.
A thunderstorm produced 1 3/4 inch hail 3 miles west of Seligman.
Pea sized hail started at 350 PM MST and then progressed in size to quarter sized (1 inch diameter) y 355 PM MST.
Hail damaged (dimple) the hood of a car as it traveled through the town of Young.
Flash flooding closed Gene Taylor Ranch Road at Dobson Wash.
Hail up to golf ball sized (1 3/4 inch diameter) was reported at the KOA Campground 6 miles north of Williams. Another storm produced penny (3/4 inch).
Soft hail up to 1 inch in diameter shredded some plants. Metal structures were not damaged.
Hail the size of quarters to half dollars (1 to 1 1/5 inch diameter) fell in The Village of Oak Creek.
A swift water rescue was conducted along Prescott Street at the low water crossing of Agua Fria Wash. A motorist tried to cross the flooded roadway.  The water was about 12 inches deep.
One inch diameter hail was reported in the west part of Show Low.
An inch of rain fell in 45 minutes in Cornville.
The low water crossing at Maggie Lane was covered with three feet of water.
The Verde River gauge above Horseshoe Dam rose from 7.43 feet at 600 PM to 10.34 FT at 7:45 PM.
Wet Bottom Creek rose from 2.21 feet at 600 PM to 4.23 feet at 730 PM.
A thunderstorm wind gust of 71 MPH was measured at the Humbug Creek RAWS site.
A thunderstorm wind gust of 61 MPH was measured at the Yarnell RAWS site (4 miles south of the town of Yarnell.
Pictures of a funnel cloud were relayed to the National Weather Service. The time and location of the funnel cloud were estimated by using radar.
A thunderstorm brought 2.01 inches of rain (county automated gauge) in just over an hour in Prescott. Street flooding was reported in northwest Prescott.
A stream gauge on Martinez Creek showed a two foot rise from dry to 1,400 CFS.  Flooding was reported on Matthie Ranch Road.
A trained weather spotter reported an estimated wind gust to 60 MPH.
Gap Creek flooded across Forest Road 574 making it impassable.
A stream gauge on Granite Creek in Granite Creek showed a 4.6 foot rise with a peak flow of 2,500 CFS (normal flow is less than fifty cubic feet a second).
Flash flooding was reported over Road 5 N just east of Reed Road. Road  1/2 N was also closed near Malapai Drive because of the flooding.
A picture posted on social media shows that the East Verde River was flooding over Beaver Flat Road.
Time lapse video shows a narrow tornado at approximately 30 degrees angle to the ground persisting for several minutes.
Heavy rain over portions of the Grand Canyon north of the Colorado River produced flash flooding in Bright Angel Creek.
The Havasu Creek gauge near Supai rose 2 feet in an hour and 45 minutes. The crest was at 1030 PM.
The river gauge on Big Chino Wash at Highway 89 measured a 4 foot rise at 5:40 PM.
The river gauge on Dry Creek measured a 1.25 foot rise between 545 PM and 652 PM.

Big Bug Creek at Mayer rose 5 feet between 550 and 610 PM.  This flood water continued |down stream into the Agua Fria River.  The gauge on the Agua Fria River near Cordes Junction measured a 3.7 foot rise between 8:30 and 9 PM.
Highway 89 was closed in both directions at mile marker 277.4 because of flooding.

At 554 PM, the stream gauge on Big Bug Creek in Mayer measured a 5 foot rise. At 630 PM, South Spring Lane was closed due to flooding near East Trails End Road. There was a 5 foot rise on Agua Fria River near Cordes Junction at 8:40 PM.
Rye Creek flooded Highway 87 at mile marker 241.
Park Service personnel at Wupatki National Monument reported a flash flood and debris flow of volcanic cinders that caused damage to park housing. A vehicle was buried 1 to 2 feet deep in cinders.
The stream gauge on Big Bug Creek recorded a 2.1 foot rise at 140 PM MST. The Agua Fria gauge showed a 2.7 foot rise (730 CFS increase) at 613 PM.
Heavy rainfall caused Granite Creek in Prescott to rise 2.65 feet in 30 minutes.

Big Bug Creek rose 2.1 feet in 70 minutes due to heavy rainfall near and over the Goodwin Fire scar upstream from the town of Mayer.  Big Bug Creek flowing through Cordes Lakes rose by 3 feet in 45 minutes (415 PM).
Tonto Creek near Rye measured a 1.5 foot rise (1000 CFS increase) at 725 PM.
Pictures on social media showed 6 to 8 inches of water running over urban roadways and other land surrounding structures near Steamboat and State Route 264.
The Arizona Department of Transportation reported that State Route 264 was impassible in both directions at milepost 439 due to flash flooding caused by heavy rain.
Ten inches of water and debris were flowing across a roadway north of the town of Grease wood.
Sycamore Creek near Dugas rose 2.71 feet in 70 minutes starting at 120 PM MST.

Swift water rescue was conducted around 350 PM to rescue a driver in 2.5 to 3 feet of water on Interstate 40 due to flooding of Black Creek near Houck.  The I-40 frontage road (dirt) on the north side was impassible due to flooding through at least 630 PM.
Arizona State Route 71 southbound was closed at milepost 95 west of US 93 due to a wash flowing over the roadway.
The Agua Fria gauge (up stream from Big Bug Creek/Goodwin Fire scar) rose 3.6 feet in 70 minutes.
Several roads in Cottonwood were closed with as much as 3 feet of water covering them. Two of the intersections included 6th Street at Boulder Lane and  South Camino Real Road at East Fir Street.
Heavy rain (2.20 inches) fell in one hour in Cottonwood. Nickle hail also fell. This rain lead to flash flooding in town.
Posts from social media indicate that golf ball to half-dollar sized hail (1 1/4 to 1 3/4 inch) fell in St Michaels.
Post on social media indicate that one inch hail fell 6 miles east of Grey Mountain. Time and location estimated.
A storm chaser estimated that 2 1/2 inch hail fell eight miles north of  Tolani Lake.

The Hopi Travel Plaza northeast of Holbrook sustained significant roof damage due to the large hail (up to 2 1/2 inch diameter).  The hail stones punched through the drop ceiling tiles. Multiple vehicles were damaged by the hail as well. Two miles away (8 miles NE of Holbrook), 1 3/4 inch diameter hail was reported.
A trained spotter reported golf ball sized hail (1 3/4 inch diameter) four miles south of Jakes Corner.
Webber Creek rose 4 to 5 feet and had a with of 10 feet due to the heavy rain.
Black Canyon Creek rose 3 feet was observed in about two hours (920 AM to 1120 AM) at Maren Avenue (a low water crossing).  Reported by Yavapai County Flood Control District.
The stream gauge along Agua Fria River east of Cordes Junction recorded a rise of 3.5 feet in three hours.
Heavy rain dislodged boulders that fell on Highway 89A in Oak Creek Canyon near mile post 382 and 388 north of Sedona.  The highway was closed until the mess could be cleaned up.
A car was up to the door handles in a low water crossing on South Leroux Street (Rio de Flag) near Cottages Street. A picture of the car was taken at 921 PM.

Pumphouse Wash crested at 2.92 feet above normal due to moderate daytime and heavy nighttime rain in and around Kachina Village. Pictures that were shared showed 6 to 10 inches of water flowing out of the wash and down a low-laying roadway.

The Oak Creek river gauge in Sedona recorded a crest of 7.24 feet at 145 AM MST due to heavy rain between there and Flagstaff. This crest is about 4.9 feet above the average normal flow at that location.
The Dry Creek river gauge recorded a crest of 6.98 feet at midnight due to heavy rain during the day and evening. The crest is about 5 feet rise in the normally dry creek bed.
The Oak Creek river gauge at Page Springs recorded a crest of  9.88 feet at 215 AM MST due to moderate daytime rain and heavy evening rain. This is 7.78 feet above the normal flow.
The river gauge on Oak Creek just upstream from West Fork recorded a crest of 3.64 feet at 1050 PM due to moderate to heavy rain.  This is about 3 feet higher than the normal flow.
Two feet of water flowed through Big Bug Creek.  Prolonged moderate to heavy rain over the area and the Goodwin Fire scar caused this flood.

Heavy rain and flowing water through a box culvert under US Highway 89 caused the roadway to collapse. The collapsed road caused a fatal vehicular collision. A 15 mile section of Highway 89 (from Cameron to the Highway 160 Junction) was closed while the road could be repaired.

The police in the Village of Supai reported a 3 foot rise in Havasu Creek at 430 PM MST. The river gauge on Havasu Creek near the Colorado River (at least 10 miles downstream) showed a 2 foot rise at 545 PM MST.
The river gauge on the Paria River at Lees Ferry recorded at 2.9 foot rise at 430 PM.
Heavy rain caused a 6.4 foot rise on the normally dry Agua Fria River northeast of Black Canyon City.
A spotter reported a funnel cloud northwest of Wickenburg.
A well developed landspout tornado was reported along Interstate 40 near mile marker 235.
A spotter saw a funnel cloud about two miles north of Interstate 40 and Deer Farm Road.
A steam gauge on Tonto Creek measured a peak stage of 6.14 feet at 630 PM. This is about 4.5 feet above normal flow.

An Arizona Department of Transportation wind sensor on Interstate 40 near Lupton reported a wind gust of 58 MPH at 632 PM. A cold front was moving across the area and there were thunderstorms in the vicinity at that time.
Ten inches of snow fell at the North Rim Lodge in the Grand Canyon National Park.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The ASOS at the Springerville Airport recorded a peak wind gust of 59 MPH at 335 AM MST.
Four inches of snow fell in Page at an elevation of 4,360.
Pictures on Facebook showed 9 inches of snow in Chilchinbiito at around 5,960 feet elevation. Snow was still falling. Roads were icy and snow-packed.
Eight inches of snow fell in Show Low/Pine Top.  Some locations had as much as 10 inches in town.
Eight inches of snow fell in Forest Lakes during the storm.

Between 3 and 4.5 inches of snow fell in the Verde Valley between 3,300 and 4,000 feet.  There was one 5 inch report a mile south of Middle Verde slightly lower than 3,200 feet. Four inches of snow fell about 1 mile southeast of Chino Valley a about 4,750 feet elevation. Five inches of snow fell at Lake Montezuma at an elevation of around 3,600 feet. Prescott Valley received 4.8 inches right at 5,000 feet elevation.
Five inches of snow fell in The Village of Oak Creek at around 4,320 feet elevation. West Sedona received 4.5 inches of new snow.

Four inches of snow was reported in Payson at an elevation of 4,920 feet elevation. Five inches of snow fell 4 miles southeast of Payson at an elevation of about 4,680 feet. Five inches of snow fell 2 miles northeast of Star Valley at an elevation just below 5,000 feet. Seven inches of snow fell in Strawberry at just below 6,000 feet elevation. A foot of snow fell 9 miles north-northeast of Young at an elevation of 6,400 feet.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Five inches of snow fell in Joseph City at just above 5000 feet elevation by 1000 PM.  Two more inches fell by midnight. Seven inches of snow fell in Holbrook at an elevation of around 5,160 feet above sea level.  Six inches of snow was reported in Winslow at about 4920 feet elevation.
Nine inches of snow fell in Munds Park.
Eleven inches of snow fell in Tsaile.

Nine inches of new snow fell in Forest Lakes at an elevation of 7,600 feet between 600 AM and 930 PM. By the time the snow stopped falling on at 900 AM on New Year's Day, Heber received 7.5 inches of new snow.
Snow began fall around 700 AM on December 30 at the Desert View at the Grand Canyon. By 930 PM on New Year's Eve, 8.4 inches of snow had accumulated.

Snow started falling in Greer at around 700 PM and a foot of new snow fell by 1115 PM. Ten inches of fresh snow fell in Pinetop-Lakeside by 1030 PM. Fifteen inches of snow fell in Alpine at around 8,000 feet elevation. Thirteen inches of snow fell 3 miles north of McNary (a total of 18 inches of snow fell with this storm by the afternoon of New Year's Day).

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Snow began falling in the Taylor area on New Years Eve.  By 900 PM, five inches of new snow had fallen. Five more inches of snow fell between 900 PM and 700 AM on New Year's Day at an elevation of 5,600 feet.

Eight inches of snow fell in Pinetop-Lakeside by around 1000 PM on New Year's Eve. Six more inches fell after that (14 total). Sixteen to eighteen inches of new snow fell around  McNary. One report indicated that over a foot of that fell before midnight.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Snow began to fall New Year's Eve during the evening. Eight inches of new snow fell by 1100 AM on New Year's Day at an elevation of 5,640 feet in St Johns.

Heavy snow fell across the Western Mogollon Rim south of Flagstaff.  Eight inches of snow fell in Mountaire by 1000 AM on the 6th.  Ten inches to a foot of snow fell by the time the snow ended in Mountaire and Munds Park early on the 7th.
Eight inches of snow fell between 1000 PM on the 12th and 9 AM on the 13th in Forest Lakes.  Light snow was still falling at the time of the observation. Ten inches of snow fell in Heber-Overgaard.
Snow started falling in Lakeside (near Show Low) around 1000 PM and 8.0 inches of new snow fell by 655 AM on the 13th. Eleven inches of snow was reported on the east side of Show Low.

A public report from the Timberline neighborhood (northeast Flagstaff) indicated that 7.5 inches of snow fell between midnight and 730 AM on the 13th.  Light snow was still falling at the time of the observation.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Eight to ten inches of snow fell in the Vernon area.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Eight inches of snow fell 5 miles northwest of Taylor. Nine inches of snow fell about 10 miles northwest of the town of Snowflake. Four inches of snow fell in Winslow at an elevation around 4900 feet.   Eight and a half inches of snow fell in Shumway.
Ten to twelve inches of snow fell along the South Rim of the Grand Canyon.
Barney Well Camp/Yolo Ranch reported 5.20 inches of rain in about 17 hours.
Snow started falling on the North Rim of the Grand Canyon (Kaibab Plateau) around 11 PM and continued through 5 PM on January 15.  Just over a foot of snow was observed.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The Springerville Airport ASOS measured sustained winds above 40 MPH between 710 AM and 215 PM, wind gusts above 58 MPH between 755 AM and 235 PM, and a peak wind gust of 68 MPH at 155 PM.  The St Johns Airport ASOS measured sustained winds above 40 MPH between 910 AM AM and 135 PM, wind gusts above 58 MPH between 1025 AM and 120 PM, and a peak wind gust of 64 MPH at 135 PM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The Winslow Airport ASOS measured sustained winds above 40 MPH between 840 AM and 105 PM, wind gusts above 58 MPH between 956 AM and 1040 AM, and a peak wind gust of 64 MPH at 1143 AM.  The Taylor Airport ASOS measured sustained winds above 40 MPH between 1150 AM and 200 PM, wind gusts above 58 MPH between1155 AM and 135 PM, and a peak wind gust of 70 MPH at 1255 PM. An ADOT wind sensor at Jackrabbit along I-40 reported a peak wind gust of 63 MPH at 0952. A wind sensor in Woodruff along SR-77 reported a peak wind gust of 62 MPH at 952 AM.

Oak Creek in Sedona rose 7 feet between 615 AM and 830 AM. Numerous low water crossings in Oak Creek Canyon were flooded. The creek dropped below bank full by 700 PM on February 4 in Sedona.  The river gauge at Page Springs rose 9 feet between noon and 230 PM.  At the peak of the flooding at the Page Springs RV Park, a foot of water was flowing through the park. at the peak of the flooding.  One large treek and several small trees came down.  Red mud was deposited throughout the RV park.  The water continued to flow downstream from Sedona into the Verde River where it was no longer a flood issue.
Dry Beaver Creek rose 6 feet between 11 AM and 2 PM. This water flowed into Wet Beaver Creek and then the Verde River.
Wet Beaver Creek rose 6.5 feet from 415 pm TO 7 PM.  This water flowed down into the Verde River where flooding was not an issue.
Between 9 and 10 inches of snow fell at the Flagstaff Airport and Kachina Village.
Eighteen inches of snow fell in Jacob Lake. The bulk of the snow fell between the evening of February 4 and the evening of February 5.
Eight inches of snow fell in Forest Lakes between the evening of February 5 and the morning of February 6.  Happy Jack Ranger Station reported 7.5 inches of new snow.

There was a naturally caused avalanche in Snowslide Canyon in the San Francisco Peaks (also called Kachina Peaks Wilderness Area--just north of Flagstaff) during the February 5-6 storm cycle. The time was estimated.

The stream gauge on Wet Beaver Creek near Rimrock reported a 7 foot rise between 6 PM and 8 PM.  The river gauge on Wet Beaver Creek at Montezuma Castle showed a 15 foot rise in two hours (945 PM to 1145 PM). Officials estimate about 25 homes were damaged as a result of the flooding, and some were declared unsafe. Multiple rescues performed in the Montezuma and Rimrock areas.
Seven tenths (0.70) of an inch of rain fell in less than ten minutes 10 miles west of Ash Fork.

Rain began falling around 600 AM and continued all day. The heaviest rain fell during the afternoon. Total rain for the day 4 miles southwest of the Prescott Airport was 1.31 inches. The rainfall report from 2 miles west of the Prescott Courthouse was 2.11 for February 14th.  Iron Springs reported 2.76 inches of rain for the day.
Oak Creek in Sedona rose over 9 feet. Evacuations took place in Sedona (Blackhawk Lane) due to water flowing over roadway.
The river gauge on Tonto Creek above Gun Creek showed a 4.5 foot rise in just over 4 hours (from 1:45 AM to 6:00 AM).
The Verde River near Childs had a 10 foot rise in six hours (from 745 PM to 110 AM).
Agua Fria River at Old Black Canyon Highway showed a 2 foot rise in 6 hours (130 AM to 720 AM).
West Clear Creek near Camp Verde showed a 5.7 foot rise in 45 minutes (11 PM to 1145 PM).
A report from social media indicated that Pumphouse Wash was flooding in Kachina Village.  This flows into Oak Creek.
Black Canyon Creek at Maren Avenue river gauge showed a 2 foot rise in four hours (830 PM to 1230 AM).

Snow began to accumulate just after midnight across the Western Mogollon Rim early on February 17.  Snow showers increased and became heavy snow by nightfall. Snow began to tapper off during the day on the 18th. Snow totals include (in inches): Flagstaff Airport 14.5, Mountainaire 12-14, Williams 10-14, Munds Park 11-14, Kachina Village 11-13, Flagstaff 6-11, and Bellemont (NWS Flagstaff) 6.9. The Flagstaff Police Department reported 54 traffic collisions. Four of those resulted in resulted in injuries. Schools were not in session due to President's Day.

Heavy snow fell across the Eastern Mogollon Rim starting early in the morning on February 17th. Snow fell through most of the day on the 18th. Some of the snow totals include (in inches): Forest Lakes  21, Happy Jack 6, Clay Springs/Pinedale 15, and Heber-Overgaard 8-11.

Heavy snow fell across Northern Gila Country from early morning on February 17 well into the evening of February 18. Here are some of the snowfall totals in inches: Washington Park 6-11, Tonto Village 7-9, Payson 6-7,  Kohls Ranch 6, and Star Valley 4. The elevation in Payson is right around 5000 feet (=/- 200 feet), Star Valley 4,800 feet, and Washington Park is 6,000 feet. This is on the southern slopes of the Mogollon Rim so upslope played a very important roll in the distribution of the snowfall amounts in this zone.
People at the Grand Canyon Village reported 9 to 10 inches of new snow.

This cold storm brought accumulating snow below 5000 feet where heavy snow criteria is 4 inches. Here are some of the snowfall totals at elevations below 5000 feet (in inches):  Chino Valley 4-6, Paulden 4-5, and Mayer 4-5.
Four inches of snow fell in Sedona at an elevation of around 4520 feet.
Nine inches of snow was reported near McNary. Six inches of snow fell in Pinetop-Lakeside.

The city of Flagstaff and Coconino County closed all non-essential offices. Mountain Line bus  service in Flagstaff was canceled for the day and flights to and from Flagstaff Pulliam Airport were grounded.

Snow started falling late evening on February 20 at elevations below 5000 feet.  By 430 AM, 4.5 inches of snow had fallen in Paulden at around 4,400 feet and 5.5 inches in Bagdad by 530 AM at 3,800 feet elevation. A two day winter storm caused the Klagetoh Chapter of the Navajo Nation to declare a state of emergency.  The Chapter began using emergency money to plow roads and make home visits.  Up to 18 inches of snow fell in Ganado.
Heavy rain caused streams and creeks to flow across Yavapai County. A freight truck was swept sideways and got stuck in Miller Creek. The driver  was rescued by firefighters.
A picture of a funnel cloud was posted on social media. The location was estimated from radar at that time. The funnel was observed for at least 13 minutes from near Williams.
A tornado was reported by the public southwest of Tuba City. The time and location was estimated by the report, video, and radar.
Heavy late season snow began to fall around 415 PM until around 730 PM. Four inches of snow fell at 8000 feet elevation.
The ASOS at the Winslow Airport reorted wind gusts over 58 MPH for 10 minutes. The peak gusts was 61 MPH (more than once).
A trained spotter reported 1 inch diameter (quarter sized hail) with larger sized hail intermixed falling in Nutrioso.

The Museum Fire started about 4 miles north of Flagstaff on Sunday July 21 at around 1115 AM. The fire grew to 1,962 acres in the Dry Lake Hills area. The burn severity was 12% High, 28% moderate, 48%, and 12% very low.  Much of this area drains into the Spruce Wash which runs into several communities of Flagstaff. An initial estimate of $9 million was spent on fire suppression.  Extensive flood protection measures (200,000 sand bags and many jersey barriers) have been put in place below the fire scar.
A picture of one inch diameter hail on the north side of Payson was shared on social media.
Black water (ash) and debris flowed over North Primrose Circle and down Spruce Wash to between East Park Way and East Linda Vista Drive.
A pilot reported a funnel cloud west of St Johns.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms flooded roads making them impassible in Whiteriver.
Social media photos show greater than 18 inches of runoff flowing through Grandpa Wash at the intersection of Middle Verde Road. Time was estimated using on radar and social media post.
The river gauge on the Verde River near Camp Verde showed a 2 foot rise.
Multiple reports from public and law enforcement of flooded roads in the Tuba City area.
Quarter sized (1 inch diameter) was reported just south of the Parks Exit on I-40.
Law enforcement officials reported that numerous power poles were blown down by thunderstorm winds.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm produced flash flooding in the Agua Fria River near Poland Junction. A river gauge reported a 2.27 foot rise from 5:15PM MST to 7:00PM MST.
A trained spotter reported 0.90 inches of rain in about 15 minutes 2 NW Dewey-Humboldt.
The river gauge on Cibecue Creek showed a 2.15 foot rise from 1:15AM MST to 1:30AM MST.

Snowfall amounts across the Western Mogollon Rim include: Bellemont 10 inches, Flagstaff 10 TO 14 inches, Hart Prairie 19 inches, Mormon Lake 18 to 22 inches, Munds Park 11 to 14 inches, Sunset Crater 15 inches, and Parks 12 inches.
Snowfall amounts include: Clints Well 27 inches, Forest Lakes 24 inches, and Heber 15 to 18 inches.
Snowfall amounts include: two miles north of McNary 13 inches, Nutrioso 6 to 8 inches, Pinetop/Lakeside 16 to 18 inches, Show Low 18 inches, and White River 5 inches.

Snowfall amounts include: Payson 6 to 8 inches, Star Valley 10 inches,  Strawberry 12 inches, and Cedar Creek 2 to 3 inches. Highway 87 was closed because of slippery conditions for close to nine hours from the night of the 4nd to the morning of the 5th.

events.cz_name: NORTHEAST PLATEAUS AND MESAS SOUTH OF HIGHWAY 264
events.event_narrative: Petrified Forest National Park received 9 inches of new snow.
Navajo National Monument received 11 inches of snow and Rough Rock received 4 inches of snow.
Kayenta received 5 inches of snow and Chinle received 3 inches of snow.
A thunderstorm produced 1.60 inches of rain with some nuisance flooding and pea sized hail.
Over 3.00 inches of rain from thunderstorms produced flash flooding that damaged some roads and buildings in and around Show Low.
The Jacks Canyon River Gauge showed a 4.4 foot rise (780 CFS) at 538 PM.
One and a half inches of rain fell in 30 minutes near downtown Flagstaff.

The Spruce Wash rain gauge measured 0.83 inches of rain from  1:26 to 2:41 PM. At 2:47 PM, ash and twigs were in the runoff from the Museum Fire scar. Water flow was between 3 and 8 inches deep through the drainage.  All water was contained within the ditches.
Hail almost the size of a quarter fell from 1120 to 1140 AM.  This storm removed leaves off trees and knocked down branches and fruit around town.

Training thunderstorms produce at least 4 inches of rain over desert and rocky terrain. This caused flash flooding in Tappan Wash up to 20 feet deep in the narrow gouge under Highway 64. A river gauge on the Little Colorado River downstream measured a  5 foot rise 15 minutes (730 to 745 PM). This was an increase of 2,911 CFS.  A total rise of 5.7 feet was measured in an hour and 45 minutes (a total rise of 3213 CFS rise).
The Payson ASOS reported a peak wind gust of 68 MPH at 335 PM. The Payson Police reported multiple trees and power poles down in the city.
The Agua Fria river gauge near Humbolt showed a 4 feet rise between 815 and 845 PM.
A thunderstorm caused lots of wind damage (mostly downed tree branches) and 0.75 to 1.10 inches of rain in the Prescott and Dewey areas.
Big Bug Creek in Mayer rose 2.5 feet between 1230 and 130 PM.
Nickle to possibly quarter sized hail fell in Sedona between Bell Rock and Uptown.
A spotter in Black Canyon City reported 3.50 inches of rain 120 PM (in around 8 hours).

Agua Fria River near Old Black Canyon Highway rose 3 feet by 940 AM and was continuing to rise.  Water was flowing across Squaw Valley Road (a low water crossing) in Black Canyon City. A spotter in the area had reported 1.80 inches of rain in around 4 hours by 940 AM.
Tonto Creek rose 5.6 feet at the USGS Gauge near Jakes Corner.
Jefferson Road near Mayer near Mayer was flooded and impassable around 11 AM due to heavy rain in the area.
Street flooding was reported in Cordes Lakes due to the heavy rain in the area. Streets had water 6 inches deep at 500 AM.

Approximately 20 mobile homes were damaged by very strong thunderstorm winds. One home was so damaged that it was no longer habitable. Four homes suffered moderate damage.  Power poles were snapped off with many with out power. Close to 100 trees were damaged as well.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN COCONINO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The ADOT wind sensor at Two Guns reported sustained winds above 40 MPH from 1003 AM to 1213 PM MST.  Wind gusts over 58 MPH were reported from 1053 AM to 1115 AM. The peak wind gust of 63 MPH was reported at 1113 AM MST.

A public report of 2.47 inches of rain in Black Canyon City was received. This rain fell in Black Canyon City from early morning until 842 PM. The Agua Fria River and Black Canyon Creek experienced high water flows and were receding by the time of this report.
The Agua Fria River at Black Canyon City rose 5.5 feet in less than 3 hours.
The Show Low area received 2.47 inches of rain and melted snow in a 24 hour period.  There was 2.2 inches of snowfall.
Eight inches of snow was reported in Alpine by 0600 AM.  Nutrioso received 12.5 inches of snow by 300 PM.

Heavy rain fell over the Cataract/Havasu Creek drainage. The stream gauge at Supai peaked started to rise at 1100PM and peaked at 17.1 feet (245 AM), just above flood stage (base flow is 14.7 feet). There were reports on social media of flooding in the campground with personal gear being swept way.

Black Canyon Wash was flowing over Maren Ave about 1.5 feet deep by 1250 PM (from a river gauge reading of about 3.25 feet). The river eventually rose to 16 feet on the river gauge (a 13.5 foot rise).  The river dropped to around 5 feet on the river gauge by around 8 PM on December 4.

The snow level lowered to around 7000 feet and rain turned to snow across the Western Mogollon Rim population centers by 400 AM on November 29.  Many areas had received 8 inches of snow by 800 AM.  Here is a storm total (in inches): Hart Prairie (9000 feet) 30,  Flagstaff Airport 16.8, Flagstaff 14 - 19, Parks 15 - 18,  Bellemont (NWS Flagstaff) 17.0, Munds Park 12.2, and Williams 15 - 18. A storm total of 22 inches fell 5 miles west of Parks. Thirty inches of snow fell at 11,800 feet elevation. Interstates 17 and 40 and Highway 89A through Oak Creek Canyon were close as a preemptive measure around Flagstaff during the storm to allow crews to keep the roads clear (local traffic was still allowed to use these roads).  Several wrecks and collisions were reported in the interstates after the roads re-opened.

The snow level lowered and rain changed to snow over some of the observation sites around midnight.  Here are some of the snowfall totals (in inches): Groom Creek 12, |Seligman  10 - 13, 10 miles west of Seligman 8.0, Prescott Courthouse 7 - 10, Skull Valley 7, and Chino Valley 6. Several large tree branches broke around Prescott due to the heavy wet snow. A foot of snow was reported 10 miles west of Ash Fort at about 5200 feet elevation.

The Grand Canyon Village received 13 - 15 inches of snow (above 6800 feet elevation).   A light dusting of snow fell at the bottom of the Canyon at Phantom Ranch (2460 feet elevation). The Grand Canyon National Park  and the near by City of Tusayan lost power during the storm impacting more than 1,000 people.  The city declared a state of emergency.

Eighteen inches of snow fell in Fraziers Well area. The Valle area had 10-14 inches of snow by 700 AM. Thirteen inches of snow fell 10 ENE of Seligman. Eleven inches of snow fell 4 miles north of Ash Fork at an elevation of 5100 feet above sea level. A foot of snow fell at Grand Canyon Caverns at an elevation of 5600 feet.

Seven inches of snow fell in Skull Valley  by 842 AM at an elevation of about 4500 feet. Wilhoit received 6 inches of snow by 944 AM at an elevation of 4800 feet. State Route 260 from Camp Verde to Cottonwood was closed during this storm...at an elevation of around 3,200 feet above sea level.
Sedona received 4.5 inches of snow at an elevation of 4500 feet by 900 AM.

A trained spotter in Forest Lakes received half an inch of rain before the precipitation changed over to snow. at around 300 AM. Ten inches of snow fell by 1000 AM...with snow still falling. Sixteen inches of snow was reported in Forest Lakes by the time it stopped snowing around noon on November 30. State Route 87 from Payson to Winslow was closed for a period of time during the storm.
Seven inches of snow was reported at Buffalo Pass (8,400 feet elevation) at 1000 AM November 29. It was still snowing.
Seven inches of snow was reported at Buffalo Pass (8,400 feet elevation) at 1000 AM November 29. It was still snowing.

Rain changed over to snow around 600 AM on November 29 in Star Valley at 48000 feet. Five inches of snow was measured at 1120 AM. A public report of 9.9 inches of new snow was received from Washington Park at 5,400 feet elevation. Twelve inches of snow fell in Strawberry at about 5,900 feet elevation. Three to five inches of snow fell in Payson right around 5000 feet.

Eight inches of snow fell in Show Low by 1230 PM with snow still falling.  A spotter 4 miles northwest of McNary reported 10.5 inches of snow. The Pintop-Lakeside ended up with 9.5 inches of snow (1.49 total melted snow/rain).

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Nine inches of snow was reported 2 miles east-northeast of Concho. A trained spotter measured a foot of snow 8 miles north of Vernon at 6,600 feet. More than an inch of rain fell before changing to snow around 300 AM on November 29.
Five inches of snow fell in Fredonia at an elevation around 4700 feet.

Avalanche debris were seen from two different natural avalanches at around 11,700 feet in the San Francisco Peaks in the Kachina Peaks Wilderness about 13 miles north of the Flagstaff Airport.  The sides were on the north-northeasterly aspects.

Heavy rain caused Silver Creek to flood. A woman driving on a street had to be rescued when her car got stuck in the rising flood water.||Show Low Creek ran up to the bottom of a bridge became a lake. Show Low Public Works closely surveyed the situation but, did not have to close the bridge. Show Low Lake filled and was running uncontrolled over the spillway 30 inches deep.||Water flowing over the earthen spillway of Bootleg Lake into Corduroy Creek prompted the evacuation of several homes downstream in the town of Carrizo.||The Three Pipes land bridge in the town of White River was breached and a foot bridge was washed away. Some families in the area were evacuated.
Heavy rain caused rock slides on Highway 89A in Oak Creek Canyon closing the road from Flagstaff to Sedona.

Heavy rain (nearly 4 inches) on Jan 27 and 28th forced the evacuation of at least 60 people from the east side of Tonto Creek near Jakes Corner. Other residents were stranded on the east side of Tonto Creek until the water subsided. The rising water washed out three power poles and about 2,300 customers without power.

The stream gauge (BCMA3) on Beaver Creek near Montezuma Castle National Monument reported a rise of 2.37 feet in one hour between 345 PM and  445 PM on December 4.   The stream continued to rise over 9 feet. A successful swift water rescue was conducted |along Reay Road in the community of Montezuma Castle. The rescue was completed by 1845 MST December 4.

Tonto Creek rose to above action stage for several days due to heavy rain and melting snow. During the initial increase in flow, a vehicle attempted ford the creek at a low water crossing. The vehicle was washed downstream and one person in the vehicle died.  This happened around 621 PM.
Eight inches of snow fell at Navajo National Monument at about 7000 feet.

Heavy rain fell across the lower elevations of Yavapai County. A public report of 0.93 inches of rain was received in the  McGuireville area by 800 AM on Tuesday (December 24) morning. Rain continued to fall in that area through Christmas Day.

Snow began to fall in the greater Flagstaff area around 900 PM on December 23. Eight inches of snow was reported in Kachina Village by around 200 PM on December 24. A spotter in Munds Park reported 7.8 inches of new snow at 700 PM on Christmas Eve. A foot of snow fell in Parks by 900 AM on Christmas Day.  Storm totals include (in inches): Kachina Village 19-20, Flagstaff Airport 14.1, Bellemont (NWS Flagstaff) 12.2, |Parks area 8-12, Williams area 8-16,  Munds Park 10, and West Flagstaff 5-10.
A trained spotter just east of Forest Lakes reported 8.5 inches of snow by 830 PM Christmas Eve. Thirteen inches of new snow fell by the evening of December 25.
A foot of snow fell in Alpine overnight with eighteen inches total by 430 PM. Eight inches of snow fell in Nutrioso by 1230 PM.
Ten inches of new snow fell in Forest Lakes.

Up to nine inches of snow fell in the Flagstaff area. Some locations received about half that amount. Total snow amounts include (in inches): Doney Park 8-9, Munds Park                    7, Cosnino 8, East Flagstaff 6-9, and Williams 5-8.
Ten inches of snow fell 5 miles east of Kolhs Ranch at about 5,800 feet above MSL.

Snow began to fall again on during the afternoon of December  27. New snowfall totals by the evening of December 28 (in inches) were: Pinetop-Lakeside 6-8, Show Low 4-6, and                                                                           |Shumway (just north of this zone) 8.

The wind sensor at the Mogollon Airpark near Heber reported a peak wind gust of 58 MPH at 155 PM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: Very strong winds were felt across the Little Colorado River Valley Apache County. Sustained winds over 40 MPH were felt for over 9 hours in St Johns and Springerville. Peak wind gusts include Springervile 78 MPH at 135 PM, St Johns 70 MPH at 243 PM, and Lupton 60 MPH at 212 PM. There were multiple reports of downed power poles in Springerville and Eagar.  Trees were blown down in Concho and Show Low.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN COCONINO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The ADOT wind sensor at Two Guns reported a peak wind gust of 64 MPH at 353 AM. Wind gusts exceeded 58 MPH from 330 AM to 220 PM.
The peak wind gust at the Show Low Airport Show Low was 64 MPH at 1035 AM. The winds gusted over 58 MPH between 1015 AM and 3 PM. The sustained winds were above 40 MPH between 930 AM and 430 PM.

Ten inches of snow fell in Walker at an elevation of 6,400 feet.  Nine inches of snow fell in Crown King at an elevation of 5,800 feet.  Four to eight inches of snow fell in the Prescott and Prescott Valley area.
Eight to nine inches of snow fell in the Alpine area.

Two people were canyoneering in Bull Canyon (also known as Water Slide Canyon) near Cherry Creek when one was swept away by rushing waters. An inch and a half to two inches of rain had fallen in the drainage in the previous 11 hours.

The wind sensor on Agassiz Peak at 11,555 feet measured sustained winds above 40 MPH from 7 AM February 25 until 200 AM on February 26. Wind gusts above 58 MPH were measured from 320 AM until 200 AM.  The peak wind gusts of 84 MPH were measured between 11:10 and 11:20 AM (inclusive). The wind sensor at 9,969 feet measured a peak wind gust of 62 MPH at 11:00 AM.
West Clear Creek flooded and caused the closure of Verde Lakes Drive.
Four and a half (4.50) inches of rain fell over a four day period in Pine. Pine Creek was flowing over two low water crossings. The deepest was 10 to 18 inches on March 13.

The Agua Fria River reached flood stage (15.8 feet) at around 500 AM after around a 12 foot rise at the Old Black Canyon Highway Bridge. Over three and a half (3.62) inches of rain fell in about 3 days.  The river was above flood stage until around 4 PM.
A funnel cloud was observed (filmed) approximately 4 miles west-southwest of Joseph City.

The East Verde River rose 4 feet in East Verde Estates.

ADOT reported at least 14 collision on Interstate -40 west of Flagstaff that caused major delays and road closures (one section of the interstate was closed for over 13 hours).

The North Rim of the Grand Canyon received 11.5 inches of snow by the evening of March 19.

A trained spotter in Forest Lakes reported 12 inches of new snow.
Eight inches of snow fell in Nutrioso by 900 AM on March 19. Nine inches of snow fell in Alpine. Pinetop-Lakeside received 8.5 inches of snow by 700 AM on March 19.

Heavy snow fell over the Western Mogollon Rim. Some of the snowfall totals were: Bellemont 5.8 inches, Flagstaff Airport 6 inches, Hart Prairie 9.0 inches, and Parks 6.0 inches. Area law enforcement responded to 22 non-injury or very minor injury vehicle accidents during and shortly after this storm.
Storm total snowfall across the Eastern Mogollon Rim included: Forest Lakes 9.0 inches, Happy Jack 6 to 8 inches, and Heber 12 inches.
Snowfall amounts across Northern Gila County include: Kohls Ranch 8.0 inches and Payson 3.1 inches.  Schools in Pine and Strawberry closed for on February 15th because of the snow.

events.event_narrative: Four to five inches of snow fell at Meteor Crater.
A video on social media showed a whirl of dust at or near the ground near the gust from from a storm. There was no condensation funnel. The wind in the circulation was estimated to be 50 MPH.
A wind gust of 60 MPH was recorded at the Winslow Airport at 555 PM.

Strong tornado in the forest south of Bellemont. Two forest roads were completely blocked by fallen trees, with several areas along the path exhibiting complete destruction of the forest with all trees felled for hundreds of yards. The supercell thunderstorm that produced this tornado also produced Tornado #3.
This tornado was determined via aerial photography and surveys, correlated with the tornadic radar signatures.  The start and stop times were estimated from the radar data.
This tornado was observed 4 miles south of the Country Club neighborhood on the east side of Flagstaff.  Little damage reported.
A dust devil uprooted a one foot diameter tree and destroyed a shed.

Much of the 30 mile pipe line used for providing water to the over 300 head of cattle was burned on just one ranch. Many miles of fence posts were burned. The Mangum Fire (pronounced Mang-Um) was ignited on the afternoon of June 8th, 2020 approximately 7 miles SW of Jacob Lake, AZ. As of 6/29/20, the cause is still under investigation. In the period from the start of the fire through the end of June, the area experienced a prolonged dry period with afternoon humidity routinely below 15% and poor overnight humidity recovery. Temperatures generally trended upward, with high temperatures ranging from the low-70s to mid-80s for the majority of the period. No precipitation was observed during the Month of June, although is not abnormal as June is climatologically the driest month of the year.||The fire area was included in a Red Flag Warning on June 12th, 13th and 16th. Afternoon humidity in the low-teens to single digits was observed, with wind gusts into the 30 to 40 mph range  On June 12th, the fire made an approximately 10 mile run to the northeast. The fire put up impressive, but sheared, pyro-cumulus columns on several occasions.||Following the Red Flag Conditions on June 16th, winds shifted to the west behind a dry frontal boundary. High pressure led to warm, dry and breezy conditions that generally persisted through June 27th. Another round of Red Flag Conditions due to the passage of a potent, but dry low pressure system occurred on June 28th and 29th. The fire showed very little activity during these latter Red Flag events, and the team transitioned with a Type 3 Team on June 30th.

The fire started on 7/3 as the result of lightning from isolated thunderstorms in the area. The fire is only accessible by helicopter and 2 hotshot crews were shuttled into the fire by helicopter on 7/3. High sustained winds out of the southwest and low humidity in the fire area caused increased fire behavior on the afternoon of 7/4 pushing the fire north and northeast. Airtankers and helicopters supported the hotshot crews on the fireline through the day. A pilot died on July 7 when his helicopter crashed while transporting supplies for fire fighting operations.

An intense snow shower lead to a massive pileup in both directions on I-10 about 7 miles west of Flagstaff.  A total of 139 vehicles were involved over a 4 mile stretch on both sides of the highway. The east bound lanes were closed for over 14 hours and the west bound lanes were closed for over 16 hours. A total of 20 miles of I-40 were closed in both directions. This was one of the worst traffic accidents (most cars) in northern Arizona history. Two people died, 10 people had serious injuries, and another 35 people received treatment. A total of 53 people were transported to the Flagstaff Medical Center. Other patients were taken to Williams Health Care Center and Yavapai Regional Medical Center.  Fifteen people were extracted from their vehicles with specialized rescue equipment. About 40 people went to a Red Cross shelter that had been set up.

Flash flooding covered the roads (including Highway 160) with water, mud, and rocks near Tonalea and Cow Springs.
McClaws Road was close in Holbrooke due to the flash flooding of the Little Colorado River.
The Agua Fria River came up 7.2 feet at the gauge on Tara Springs Road near Black Canyon City. The flood waters came from as far away as Dewey (20 straight miles).
Kirkland Creek was flowing 4.5 feet deep (estimated) and was flowing over Highway 89. Water had begun to recede by 0630 AM.
Local Law Enforcement reported that Polacca Wash was overtopping State Route 264 just east of First Mesa.
Major flash flooding was reported on a widely used dirt road between Whippoorwill and Low Mountain.
Heavy rain dislodged rocks that fell on Highway 89 between Flagstaff and Sedona (switchbacks near FR-237).

A vehicle was caught in the flood waters of Dinnebito Wash near Route 6720 and Saltwater Wash. There was one fatality and two others trapped in the water. This was located about 72 air miles downstream from the headwaters of this wash.
Heavy rain caused the Verde River to rise 2 feet (near the junction of the Verde River and Sycamore Creek).

Flood waters swept a vehicle away in a low water crossing on Camino Real near Rocky Knolls Road. The flood water was estimated to be 8 feet deep. The body of the driver was found several days later at the confluence with the Verde River.
Heavy rain over the Paria River drainage (in Arizona and Utah) caused the river gauge at Lees Ferry to rise 2.5 feet.
Major portions of the Twin Arrows Casino were flooded. Flood debris went all over their roads.
A thunderstorm with heavy rain produced heavy runoff into washes and roadways. One barn northeast of Shumway had water running through it (2 inches in 45 to 60 minutes). .
Flooding was reported on McLaws Road in Holbrook.
About two inches of rain fell between 1810 and 1854 near the community of Parks.  Rain gauge measured 3.31 inches of total rain during the day.
There was a 9.7 foot rise on the Moenkopi River gauge near Tuba City starting at 1500 on  7/29/21 and peaking at 0445 on 7/30/21.

The Chapter House in the community of Cornfields reported flash flooding in five areas along Indian Route 15 between the communities of Greasewood and Burnside, including  near the community of Cornfields.  The road was covered with more than two feet of water, heavy debris, and thick mud.
State Highway 60 was close due to flooding about 14 air miles south of Cibecue.
Four feet of water was flowing through Poquito Wash. Flooding was also reported in near buy near-by homes in north Prescott Valley.
Local Law Enforcement reported that the flash flooding left large rocks, trees, bushes, and debris on area roads. Public works was called out to clean up the mess.
Heavy rain fell 4 miles south of Washington Park with 1.10 inches measured in 40 minutes.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding from Washington Park to Tonto Village. Water was cascading through yards and flooding roadways. The East Verde River rose 3 feet near Washington Park at 540 PM MST.
A picture of a funnel cloud from the community of Pinon was posted on Social Media.
The Verde River gauge  12 miles north-northwest of Jerome showed a 2.5 foot rise.
A family of 5 was hit by a flash flood in  Labyrinth Canyon that drains into Lake Powell. The wife and mother drowned.
Substantial flooding was reported within Vernon. County Roads 3131, 3137, and 3187 were impassable.
Water and debris were flowing over the roadways in Polacca/Second Mesa.
A creek in Payson rose 19 inches. Water was flowing across one lane of Highway 87.
A video showed a significant rise of water flowing through the wash.
A photo on social media showed a dirt road that was partially washed out north of Greasewood Springs Chapter House. A video on social media also showed a significant rise on wash.
A picture of one inch (estimated) hail was posted on social media from the Munds Park area.
A trained spotter reported that Lynx Creek in Walker was running four to five feet deep in spots.

A stream gauge on Granite Creek (northeast of downtown Prescott--GRCA3) reported a 6.7 foot rise with a peak flow of 3,558 CFS.  At least five roads were closed in Prescott due to flooding between 2:50 and 3:50 PM.  Several roads were also closed in Wilhoit due to flooding.  Two cars were stuck in flowing washes near Chino Valley/Paulden. Water was beginning to move the vehicles so Law Enforcement was called to the scene.
There were several roads closed in the Prescott area due to flash flooding.

The Humbug Creek RAWS(QHBA3) had a peak wind gust of 67 MPH at 9:40 PM.  The  Stanton RAWS (QSTA3) had 60 MPH winds at 10:00 PM. Arizona Department of Transportation reported that State Route 89 south of Prescott (mile marker 308) was closed in both directions due to fallen trees at 11:35 PM.  The exact time of tree fall was unknown.

A trained spotter reported hail the size of a quarter (1 inch diameter) 7 miles north-northwest of Williams.  Other people reported golf ball sized hail (1 3/4 inch diameter) around the Williams area.
Hail the size of a quarter (1 inch in diameter) was reported in the community of White Cone.
A weather station north-northeast of Iron Springs recorded a peak wind gust of 58 MPH at 11:29 PM MST from a thunderstorm. Wind gusts to 56 MPH continued for another 10 minutes.
Quarter sized hail (1 inch diameter) was reported by three different sources around Chino Valley.
A trained spotter reported one inch diameter hail near Heber-Overgaard.

A trained spotter reported one inch diameter hail 8 miles east of Mountainaire at 2:48 PM MST. One and a half inch hail was reported in Mountainaire at 3:01 PM. Two inch diameter hail was reported 4 miles east of the Flagstaff Airport at 3:13 PM MST. Two and a half inch hail was reported along Lake Mary Road. Several homes had roof damage.
Numerous low water crossings were flooded and roads were closed due to flash flooding  in the Heber area.
Many roads were flooded in Concho. Water was up to the door steps of businesses.
Arizona Department of Transportation reported that Highway 180A was closed due to flooding at mile post 347.  Pictures on social media showed water at least a foot deep on roadways in this area.

Heavy rain over the Museum Fire scar (2019) produce significant flooding down Spruce Wash and into north central Flagstaff and down into the Rio de Flag on the south and southeast Flagstaff. The flood water first entered developed area around 1245 PM with trees, logs, and other debris 60-70 feet wide over topping a road about 2.5 - 3 feet deep. The flood waters were over 9 feet deep in some channeled areas through the forest. Many roads were flooded and closed. The flood barriers were overtopped in some places.

Heavy rain over the Fort Valley Trail System (2-3 inches in an hour) caused flash flooding through some yards north of Highway 180, the Rio de Flag in the Cheshire Subdivision (crossed two roads--first time in at least 27 years)m and all the way through Flagstaff.
The river gauge on Dry Beaver Creek near The Village of Oak Creek rose 4.5 feet.  Downstream, Dry Beaver Creek rose 4.4 feet between 430 PM and 530 PM MST.
Bright Angel Creek rose 6 feet at Phantom Ranch.
The Little Colorado River gauge near Cameron (LCCA3) showed a 2.9 foot rise between 815 PM and 1100 PM MST.
The Wet Beaver Creek gauge near Montezuma Castle showed a 2.7 foot rise between 830 PM and 1045 PM.
The Paria River gauge at Lees Ferry showed a 4 foot rise between 6:00 AM and 7:00 AM MST. The Paria River drainage originates in Utah and flows into the Colorado River near Lees Ferry.
The East Verde River near Childs (EVDA3) had a 2.9 foot rise between 0800 and 0845 MST.
The Tonto Creek stream gauge above Gun Creek (TNRA3) measured a 3.1 foot rise between 0845 and 1000 AM MST.
The water was flowing 4.85 feet deep (normally dry) in Munds Canyon under Interstate 17 and about 25 feet wide. The estimated flow was 900 CFS.
Golf ball sized hail (1.75 inches diameter) was reported near the entrance to the North Rim of The Grand Canyon National Park.
Granite Creek in Prescott (GCRA3) rose from 7.17 to 10.22 feet in 45 minutes.

Pictures on social media show at least 10 inches of water flowing in Dinnebito Wash near Hardrock. The water had been flowing for at least 2 hours. Road going into Hardrock were not passible due to the water flowing over the roadways.
Granite Creek (GRWA3) below Watson Lake rose 2.2 feet to 3.97 feet in one hour and 44 minutes. Water crested at 7:20 PM MST.
The Wet Beaver Creek gauge (BCMA3) near Montezuma Castle National Monument rose from 1.0 to 3.03 feet in 65 minutes.  It crested at 11:13 PM MST.
The Verde River near Clarkdale rose over 17 feet in 58 minutes (VDCA3). The water crested at 19.49 feet at 942 PM MST.
The Verde River near Camp Verde rose just over 10 feet in 4 hours (VAVA3).  The water crested at 14.23 at 9:30 AM MST.
Emergency Management reported a 4 foot rise on Black Canyon Creek at 8:08 PM MST.  This creek is downsteam from parts of the Tiger Fire (2021).
Pictures posted on social media showed a funnel cloud about a mile south of the Flagstaff Mall.  Location estimated based on known landmarks.
The Verde River near Camp Verde rose almost two feet with a crest of 4.39 feet at 6:00 PM MST (VAVA3).
Carrizo Creek near Carrizo (CRZA3) rose from 1 to 3.7 feet in less than an hour. The water dropped back below 2 feet about 3 hours later.
Heavy rain flooded a wash which created a waterfall over the rim and into Glen Canyon just below/south of Glen Canyon Dam.
Water was flowing over a 40 foot section of Highway 87 at Mile Post 343 near Coyote Wash.

Highway 191 was closed due to flooding over the highway at Mile Post 491.8 between Round Rock and Rock Point (by Whale Rock) at 1135 PM. A social media video post showed a dangerous swollen wash along Highway 191.

The East Verde River near Childs (Gauge EVDA3) rose from 10 to 12.4 feet in less than 30 minutes at 930 AM on September 1.  It dropped below 12 feet about 3 hours later. At 830 PM,  it rose to 13.8 feet.  The water dropped back to around 11.6 feet by 900 AM on September 2.

Heavy rain over the Little Colorado River Basin and tributaries created a surge of water at the river gauge (LCCA3) on the Little Colorado River near Cameron.  The water rose from 1.8 feet to 5.43 feet on the gauge in less than 15 minutes at 1245 AM on 2 September.  The water was still above 4.7 feet at 945 AM.

The stream gauge on Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City rose from 17.6 feet to 20.8 feet in less than half an hour at 430 PM on 1 September. The gauge went down to 18.4 feet then rose again to 23.7 feet in less than half an hour at 900 PM on 1 September.  The water rose a third time to 22 feet in less than half a hour at 3:00 AM on 2 September. The water receded below 18 feet by 800 AM on 2 September.

Granite Creek in Prescott (GCRA3) rose around 4.15 feet between 445 PM and 615 PM. The waster began to decrease after 700 PM.  A video posted on social media showed ongoing flooding in Granite Creek Park a mile north of Prescott Courthouse at 632 PM.
Jacks Canyon Creek near Winslow rose 2.8 feet in 90 minutes from 2.2 feet to 5 feet at 945 AM.
Heavy rain caused Dry Beaver Creek to rise 3.6 feet in 30 minutes cresting at 1215 PM.
A 3.9 foot rise was recorded on the Agua Fria River (AFMA3) east of Cordes Junction.
Kaibab National Forest reported that flooding closed Forest Road 22 from Forest Road 422A to Big Springs.
A thunderstorm produce hail up to 1 and 3/4 inches in diameter about 9 miles west-southwest of Jacobs Lake.
Persistent large hail was reported.
A tree fell across some cars near Thumb Butte Road in Prescott. No thunderstorms were reported in the area at the time. The wind gusts were 30 to 45 MPH at the time.
A peak wind gust of 59 MPH was reported at the Sedona Airport at 715 PM MST.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The Taylor Airport ASOS reported a peak wind gust of 62 MPH at 1120 PM MST. The winds gusted over 58 MPH from around 110 AM to 130 AM MST. Petrified Forest National Monument reported a peak wind gust of 71 MPH at 153 AM MST. The highest gust at the Winslow Airport was 59 MPH at 1156 PM MST.
The Humbug Creek remote automated weather station measured a peak wind gust of 62 MPH at 948 PM MST.
The weather station at Limestone Canyon measured a peak wind gust of 72 MPH at 324 AM MST. The wind gusts exceeded 58 MPH between around 1115 PM to around 340 AM MST.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN COCONINO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The peak wind gust at the Winslow Airport was 59 MPH at 1156 PM MST. The weather station at Two Guns reported a peak wind gust of 58 MPH at 1123 PM MST.
Twelve inches of snow fell between Jacob Lake and the Grand Canyon National Park along Highway 67.
Rim ice coated NWR transmission equipment on Mt Elden just northeast of Flagstaff. This caused transition problems to at least one NWR station (Mt Ord near Payson).

A weather station in Page had peak wind gusts of  63 MPH from 1106 to 11016 PM MST. The wind gusts were at least 58 MPH from from 1052 TO 1116 PM.  The wind gusts  briefly picked up to 60 MPH around 248 AM and even stronger from 430 to 700 AM. The peak wind gust after midnight was 67 MPH at 634 AM.

A wind sensor at Snowbowl had a peak wind gust of 67 MPH at an elevation of around 9,300 feet. Another sensor at 9969 feet had a peak wind gust of 61 MPH at 950 PM.  A wind sensor 5 miles west-southwest of Williams along Interstate 40 had a peak wind gust  68 MPH at 1023 PM. Williams Airport (KCMR) had a peak wind gust of 59 MPH at 1015 PM. The Flagstaff Airport had a peak wind gust of 59 MPH at 1110 PM. Over 1000 costumers in the Doney Park area were with out power as a result of the high winds.

A weather station on Highway 260 near the junction of Highway 273 reported a peak wind gust of 68 MPH at 1043 PM and a stronger wind gust of 75 MPH at 243 AM. Wind gusts exceeded 58 MPH between 920 PM and 400 AM. Nearby Greens Peak measured wind gusts 58 MPH or higher between 145 AM and 245 AM. The peak wind gust there at 10118 feet elevation was 66 MPH at 149 AM. The Show Low Airport had a peak wind gust of 61 MPH at 135 AM. At least seven homes were without power in the Pinetop-Lakeside area due to the winds.
The Sedona Airport recorded a peak wind gust of 59 MPH at 955 PM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The St Johns Airport reported a peak wind gust of 59 MPH at 230 AM MST. The Springerville Airport had a peak wind gust of 61 MPH at 1015 PM. The wind continued to gust above there 58 MPH from 615 PM until 145 AM.

The Humbug Creek RAWS had wind gust over 58 MPH between 1020 PM and around 230 AM.  The peak wind gust was 76 MPH at 148 AM. The wind blew down power lines two miles west-northwest of Prescott at 1253 AM and two miles south of Iron Springs at 101 AM.

The Window Rock Airport reported sustained winds of 40 MPH and higher between 245 and 255 AM MST. The peak wind gust was 64 MPH at 253 AM. The ADOT wind sensor along I-40 at Lupton measured wind gusts above 58 MPH between 230 and 300 AM.  The peak wind gust was 77 MPH at 233 AM. Power outages from damaged and/or downed power lines were reported in Nazlini, Hunters Point, Ganado Lakes area, and form Tsaile to Wheatfields (for over 6 hours).
Limestone Canyon RAWS had wind gusts over 58 MPH from 1220 AM to 330 AM. The peak wind gust of 72 MPH was at 124 AM. The Mogollon Airpark had a peak wind gust of 60 MPH at 1235 AM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN NAVAJO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The ADOT wind sensor on Highway 77 (mile marker 14) wind gust higher than 58 MPH between around 300 AM and 330 AM. The highest wind gust was 65 MPH at 320 AM. The peak wind gust at the Taylor Airport was 59 MPH at 115 AM. A wind sensor along Interstate 40 near Jackrabbit (MM270) reported a peak wind gust of 59 MPH at 223 AM. Power outages due to the wind (power lines down) were reported in Joseph City around 220 AM.
A wind sensor at Tuzigoot National Monument measured a peak wind gust of 58 MPH at 121 AM. The wind blew down power lines 13 miles northwest of Paulden at 341 AM.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN COCONINO COUNTY
events.event_narrative: High winds blew down power poles 3 miles northwest of Gray Mountain at 326 AM.  Wind gusts to 57 MPH were reported in Tuba City between 325 and 335 AM.

events.cz_name: NORTHEAST PLATEAUS AND MESAS FROM HIGHWAY 264 NORTH
events.event_narrative: Strong winds blew down power lines on Second Mesa between 250 and 300 AM. Other communities that were also without power include: Kaibeto, The Gap, Tsegi, Shonto, Pi��on, and Inscription.

events.cz_name: NORTHEAST PLATEAUS AND MESAS SOUTH OF HIGHWAY 264
events.event_narrative: Strong winds blew down power lines on Second Mesa at 253 AM.  Power was also knocked out in the communities of Dilkon, Jeddito, and Indian Wells reported around 730 AM.
The Navajo Tribal Utility Authority reported power outages due to downed and/or damaged power lines in Dennehotso, Kayenta, Many Farms, Nazlini, and Tsaile.
A 12 foot portion of a new porch roof attached to a house was removed by the strong winds around 1000 PM four miles southwest of Valle.

A vehicle was caught in the flood waters of Dinnebito Wash near Route 6720 and Saltwater Wash. There was one fatality and two others trapped in the water. This was located about 72 air miles downstream from the headwaters of this wash.
Heavy rain fell across the lower elevations of Yavapai County.  Just over an inch of rain fell in Black Canyon City in 12 hours.
Rain fell overnight (0.78) before turning to snow around 500 AM in Forest Lakes. Ten inches of snow then fell by 700 PM.
Nine inches of snow fell at Sunrise Ski Park by 100 PM with snow ongoing.
Ten inches of snow fell by 900 AM at 8,080 feet about 13 miles northwest of the Flagstaff Airport. Snow continued to fall through the day.
Heavy rain fell across Yavapai County with reports of one to three inches of rain.
Heavy rain fell across the upslope areas of southern Navajo County.  Amounts ranged from less than an inch to 2.36 inches.
Heavy rain fell across northern Gila County.  Rainfall amounts ranged from over an inch and a half at Payson to 2.80 inches just south of Washington Park.
Heavy rain fell across Coconino County before turning to snow across the higher elevations.  Amounts ranged from around an inch at the Grand Canyon to over 2.50 inches at Munds Park and Mormon Lake.

A wind sensor on Highway 260 (and Highway 273) at an elevation of 9124 feet had a peak wind gust of 70 MPH at 353 AM.  The winds gusted over 58 MPH from 230 AM to 820 AM. Greens Peak had a peak wind gust of Greens Peak 61 MPH at 409 AM (10,118 feet) with gust above 58 MPH between 230 to 415  AM.

Heavy snow fell across the Western Mogollon Rim. Some reports include (in inches): Arizona Snowbowl (10,800 feet) 13.0, Flagstaff Airport 10.1,  Parks 10.0,  Kachina Village 9.0, Bellemont (NWS Flagstaff) 7.1, and Mormon Lake  7.0.
Forest Lakes reported 8 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: LITTLE COLORADO RIVER VALLEY IN APACHE COUNTY
events.event_narrative: The Springerville Airport ASOS reported a peak wind gust of 79 MPH at 400 AM.  St Johns Airport had a peak wind gust of 60 MPH at  157 AM.
